/*
4850
** CAPI3REF: Dynamically Typed Value Object
4851
** KEYWORDS: {protected sqlite3_value} {unprotected sqlite3_value}
4852
**
4853
** SQLite uses the sqlite3_value object to represent all values
4854
** that can be stored in a database table. SQLite uses dynamic typing
4855
** for the values it stores.  ^Values stored in sqlite3_value objects
4856
** can be integers, floating point values, strings, BLOBs, or NULL.
4857
**
4858
** An sqlite3_value object may be either "protected" or "unprotected".
4859
** Some interfaces require a protected sqlite3_value.  Other interfaces
4860
** will accept either a protected or an unprotected sqlite3_value.
4861
** Every interface that accepts sqlite3_value arguments specifies
4862
** whether or not it requires a protected sqlite3_value.  The
4863
** [sqlite3_value_dup()] interface can be used to construct a new
4864
** protected sqlite3_value from an unprotected sqlite3_value.
4865
**
4866
** The terms "protected" and "unprotected" refer to whether or not
4867
** a mutex is held.  An internal mutex is held for a protected
4868
** sqlite3_value object but no mutex is held for an unprotected
4869
** sqlite3_value object.  If SQLite is compiled to be single-threaded
4870
** (with [SQLITE_THREADSAFE=0] and with [sqlite3_threadsafe()] returning 0)
4871
** or if SQLite is run in one of reduced mutex modes
4872
** [SQLITE_CONFIG_SINGLETHREAD] or [SQLITE_CONFIG_MULTITHREAD]
4873
** then there is no distinction between protected and unprotected
4874
** sqlite3_value objects and they can be used interchangeably.  However,
4875
** for maximum code portability it is recommended that applications
4876
** still make the distinction between protected and unprotected
4877
** sqlite3_value objects even when not strictly required.
4878
**
4879
** ^The sqlite3_value objects that are passed as parameters into the
4880
** implementation of [application-defined SQL functions] are protected.
4881
** ^The sqlite3_value objects returned by [sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value()]
4882
** are protected.
4883
** ^The sqlite3_value object returned by
4884
** [sqlite3_column_value()] is unprotected.
4885
** Unprotected sqlite3_value objects may only be used as arguments
4886
** to [sqlite3_result_value()], [sqlite3_bind_value()], and
4887
** [sqlite3_value_dup()].
4888
** The [sqlite3_value_blob | sqlite3_value_type()] family of
4889
** interfaces require protected sqlite3_value objects.
4890
*/
4891
typedef struct sqlite3_value sqlite3_value;
4892
4893
/*
4894
** CAPI3REF: SQL Function Context Object
4895
**
4896
** The context in which an SQL function executes is stored in an
4897
** sqlite3_context object.  ^A pointer to an sqlite3_context object
4898
** is always the first parameter to [application-defined SQL functions].
4899
** The application-defined SQL function implementation will pass this
4900
** pointer through into calls to [sqlite3_result_int | sqlite3_result()],
4901
** [sqlite3_aggregate_context()], [sqlite3_user_data()],
4902
** [sqlite3_context_db_handle()], [sqlite3_get_auxdata()],
4903
** and/or [sqlite3_set_auxdata()].
4904
*/
4905
typedef struct sqlite3_context sqlite3_context;
4906
4907
/*
4908
** CAPI3REF: Binding Values To Prepared Statements
4909
** KEYWORDS: {host parameter} {host parameters} {host parameter name}
4910
** KEYWORDS: {SQL parameter} {SQL parameters} {parameter binding}
4911
** METHOD: sqlite3_stmt
4912
**
4913
** ^(In the SQL statement text input to [sqlite3_prepare_v2()] and its variants,
4914
** literals may be replaced by a [parameter] that matches one of the following
4915
** templates:
4916
**
4917
** <ul>
4918
** <li>  ?
4919
** <li>  ?NNN
4920
** <li>  :VVV
4921
** <li>  @VVV
4922
** <li>  $VVV
4923
** </ul>
4924
**
4925
** In the templates above, NNN represents an integer literal,
4926
** and VVV represents an alphanumeric identifier.)^  ^The values of these
4927
** parameters (also called "host parameter names" or "SQL parameters")
4928
** can be set using the sqlite3_bind_*() routines defined here.
4929
**
4930
** ^The first argument to the sqlite3_bind_*() routines is always
4931
** a pointer to the [sqlite3_stmt] object returned from
4932
** [sqlite3_prepare_v2()] or its variants.
4933
**
4934
** ^The second argument is the index of the SQL parameter to be set.
4935
** ^The leftmost SQL parameter has an index of 1.  ^When the same named
4936
** SQL parameter is used more than once, second and subsequent
4937
** occurrences have the same index as the first occurrence.
4938
** ^The index for named parameters can be looked up using the
4939
** [sqlite3_bind_parameter_index()] API if desired.  ^The index
4940
** for "?NNN" parameters is the value of NNN.
4941
** ^The NNN value must be between 1 and the [sqlite3_limit()]
4942
** parameter [SQLITE_LIMIT_VARIABLE_NUMBER] (default value: 32766).
4943
**
4944
** ^The third argument is the value to bind to the parameter.
4945
** ^If the third parameter to sqlite3_bind_text() or sqlite3_bind_text16()
4946
** or sqlite3_bind_blob() is a NULL pointer then the fourth parameter
4947
** is ignored and the end result is the same as sqlite3_bind_null().
4948
** ^If the third parameter to sqlite3_bind_text() is not NULL, then
4949
** it should be a pointer to well-formed UTF8 text.
4950
** ^If the third parameter to sqlite3_bind_text16() is not NULL, then
4951
** it should be a pointer to well-formed UTF16 text.
4952
** ^If the third parameter to sqlite3_bind_text64() is not NULL, then
4953
** it should be a pointer to a well-formed unicode string that is
4954
** either UTF8 if the sixth parameter is SQLITE_UTF8 or SQLITE_UTF8_ZT,
4955
** or UTF16 otherwise.
4956
**
4957
** [[byte-order determination rules]] ^The byte-order of
4958
** UTF16 input text is determined by the byte-order mark (BOM, U+FEFF)
4959
** found in the first character, which is removed, or in the absence of a BOM
4960
** the byte order is the native byte order of the host
4961
** machine for sqlite3_bind_text16() or the byte order specified in
4962
** the 6th parameter for sqlite3_bind_text64().)^
4963
** ^If UTF16 input text contains invalid unicode
4964
** characters, then SQLite might change those invalid characters
4965
** into the unicode replacement character: U+FFFD.
4966
**
4967
** ^(In those routines that have a fourth argument, its value is the
4968
** number of bytes in the parameter.  To be clear: the value is the
4969
** number of <u>bytes</u> in the value, not the number of characters.)^
4970
** ^If the fourth parameter to sqlite3_bind_text() or sqlite3_bind_text16()
4971
** is negative, then the length of the string is
4972
** the number of bytes up to the first zero terminator.
4973
** If the fourth parameter to sqlite3_bind_blob() is negative, then
4974
** the behavior is undefined.
4975
** If a non-negative fourth parameter is provided to sqlite3_bind_text()
4976
** or sqlite3_bind_text16() or sqlite3_bind_text64() then
4977
** that parameter must be the byte offset
4978
** where the NUL terminator would occur assuming the string were NUL
4979
** terminated.  If any NUL characters occur at byte offsets less than
4980
** the value of the fourth parameter then the resulting string value will
4981
** contain embedded NULs.  The result of expressions involving strings
4982
** with embedded NULs is undefined.
4983
**
4984
** ^The fifth argument to the BLOB and string binding interfaces controls
4985
** or indicates the lifetime of the object referenced by the third parameter.
4986
** These three options exist:
4987
** ^ (1) A destructor to dispose of the BLOB or string after SQLite has finished
4988
** with it may be passed. ^It is called to dispose of the BLOB or string even
4989
** if the call to the bind API fails, except the destructor is not called if
4990
** the third parameter is a NULL pointer or the fourth parameter is negative.
4991
** ^ (2) The special constant, [SQLITE_STATIC], may be passed to indicate that
4992
** the application remains responsible for disposing of the object. ^In this
4993
** case, the object and the provided pointer to it must remain valid until
4994
** either the prepared statement is finalized or the same SQL parameter is
4995
** bound to something else, whichever occurs sooner.
4996
** ^ (3) The constant, [SQLITE_TRANSIENT], may be passed to indicate that the
4997
** object is to be copied prior to the return from sqlite3_bind_*(). ^The
4998
** object and pointer to it must remain valid until then. ^SQLite will then
4999
** manage the lifetime of its private copy.
5000
**
5001
** ^The sixth argument (the E argument)
5002
** to sqlite3_bind_text64(S,K,Z,N,D,E) must be one of
5003
** [SQLITE_UTF8], [SQLITE_UTF8_ZT], [SQLITE_UTF16], [SQLITE_UTF16BE],
5004
** or [SQLITE_UTF16LE] to specify the encoding of the text in the
5005
** third parameter, Z.  The special value [SQLITE_UTF8_ZT] means that the
5006
** string argument is both UTF-8 encoded and is zero-terminated.  In other
5007
** words, SQLITE_UTF8_ZT means that the Z array is allocated to hold at
5008
** least N+1 bytes and that the Z&#91;N&#93; byte is zero.  If
5009
** the E argument to sqlite3_bind_text64(S,K,Z,N,D,E) is not one of the
5010
** allowed values shown above, or if the text encoding is different
5011
** from the encoding specified by the sixth parameter, then the behavior
5012
** is undefined.
5013
**
5014
** ^The sqlite3_bind_zeroblob() routine binds a BLOB of length N that
5015
** is filled with zeroes.  ^A zeroblob uses a fixed amount of memory
5016
** (just an integer to hold its size) while it is being processed.
5017
** Zeroblobs are intended to serve as placeholders for BLOBs whose
5018
** content is later written using
5019
** [sqlite3_blob_open | incremental BLOB I/O] routines.
5020
** ^A negative value for the zeroblob results in a zero-length BLOB.
5021
**
5022
** ^The sqlite3_bind_pointer(S,I,P,T,D) routine causes the I-th parameter in
5023
** [prepared statement] S to have an SQL value of NULL, but to also be
5024
** associated with the pointer P of type T.  ^D is either a NULL pointer or
5025
** a pointer to a destructor function for P. ^SQLite will invoke the
5026
** destructor D with a single argument of P when it is finished using
5027
** P, even if the call to sqlite3_bind_pointer() fails.  Due to a
5028
** historical design quirk, results are undefined if D is
5029
** SQLITE_TRANSIENT. The T parameter should be a static string,
5030
** preferably a string literal. The sqlite3_bind_pointer() routine is
5031
** part of the [pointer passing interface] added for SQLite 3.20.0.
5032
**
5033
** ^If any of the sqlite3_bind_*() routines are called with a NULL pointer
5034
** for the [prepared statement] or with a prepared statement for which
5035
** [sqlite3_step()] has been called more recently than [sqlite3_reset()],
5036
** then the call will return [SQLITE_MISUSE].  If any sqlite3_bind_()
5037
** routine is passed a [prepared statement] that has been finalized, the
5038
** result is undefined and probably harmful.
5039
**
5040
** ^Bindings are not cleared by the [sqlite3_reset()] routine.
5041
** ^Unbound parameters are interpreted as NULL.
5042
**
5043
** ^The sqlite3_bind_* routines return [SQLITE_OK] on success or an
5044
** [error code] if anything goes wrong.
5045
** ^[SQLITE_TOOBIG] might be returned if the size of a string or BLOB
5046
** exceeds limits imposed by [sqlite3_limit]([SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH]) or
5047
** [SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH].
5048
** ^[SQLITE_RANGE] is returned if the parameter
5049
** index is out of range.  ^[SQLITE_NOMEM] is returned if malloc() fails.
5050
**
5051
** See also: [sqlite3_bind_parameter_count()],
5052
** [sqlite3_bind_parameter_name()], and [sqlite3_bind_parameter_index()].
5053
*/
5054
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_blob(sqlite3_stmt*, int, const void*, int n, void(*)(void*));
5055
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_blob64(sqlite3_stmt*, int, const void*, sqlite3_uint64,
5056
                        void(*)(void*));

SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_double(sqlite3_stmt*, int, double);
5058
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_int(sqlite3_stmt*, int, int);
5059
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_int64(sqlite3_stmt*, int, sqlite3_int64);
5060
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_null(sqlite3_stmt*, int);
5061
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_text(sqlite3_stmt*,int,const char*,int,void(*)(void*));
5062
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_text16(sqlite3_stmt*, int, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
5063
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_text64(sqlite3_stmt*, int, const char*, sqlite3_uint64,
5064
                         void(*)(void*), unsigned char encoding);

5066
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_pointer(sqlite3_stmt*, int, void*, const char*,void(*)(void*));

/*
5071
** CAPI3REF: Number Of SQL Parameters
5072
** METHOD: sqlite3_stmt
5073
**
5074
** ^This routine can be used to find the number of [SQL parameters]
5075
** in a [prepared statement].  SQL parameters are tokens of the
5076
** form "?", "?NNN", ":AAA", "$AAA", or "@AAA" that serve as
5077
** placeholders for values that are [sqlite3_bind_blob | bound]
5078
** to the parameters at a later time.
5079
**
5080
** ^(This routine actually returns the index of the largest (rightmost)
5081
** parameter. For all forms except ?NNN, this will correspond to the
5082
** number of unique parameters.  If parameters of the ?NNN form are used,
5083
** there may be gaps in the list.)^
5084
**
5085
** See also: [sqlite3_bind_blob|sqlite3_bind()],
5086
** [sqlite3_bind_parameter_name()], and
5087
** [sqlite3_bind_parameter_index()].
5088
*/

5096

5097

5101

5108

5109

5110

5111

**
5113
** See also: [sqlite3_bind_blob|sqlite3_bind()],
5114
** [sqlite3_bind_parameter_count()], and
5115
** [sqlite3_bind_parameter_index()].

5179

5180

5181

5182

5183

5185

5186

5187

5194

5195

5196

5198

5199
** [SELECT] statement.
5200

5201

5202
** the database name, the _table_ routines return the table name, and
5203

5204

5205
** using [sqlite3_finalize()] or until the statement is automatically
5206
** reprepared by the first call to [sqlite3_step()] for a particular run
5207
** or until the same information is requested
5208
** again in a different encoding.
5209
**
5210

5211
** database, table, and column.
5212
**
5213
** ^The first argument to these interfaces is a [prepared statement].
5214
** ^These functions return information about the Nth result column returned by
5215
** the statement, where N is the second function argument.
5216
** ^The left-most column is column 0 for these routines.
5217
**
5218
** ^If the Nth column returned by the statement is an expression or
5219
** subquery and is not a column value, then all of these functions return
5220

5221
** occurs.  ^Otherwise, they return the name of the attached database, table,
5222
** or column that query result column was extracted from.
5223
**
5224

5225
** UTF-16 encoded strings and the other functions return UTF-8.
5226
**
5227
** ^These APIs are only available if the library was compiled with the
5228
** [SQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA] C-preprocessor symbol.
5229
**
5230
** If two or more threads call one or more
5231
** [sqlite3_column_database_name | column metadata interfaces]
5232
** for the same [prepared statement] and result column
5233
** at the same time then the results are undefined.
5234
*/

5243
** CAPI3REF: Declared Datatype Of A Query Result
5244
** METHOD: sqlite3_stmt
5245
**
5246

5247
** If this statement is a [SELECT] statement and the Nth column of the
5248
** returned result set of that [SELECT] is a table column (not an
5249
** expression or subquery) then the declared type of the table
5250
** column is returned.)^  ^If the Nth column of the result set is an
5251
** expression or subquery, then a NULL pointer is returned.
5252
** ^The returned string is always UTF-8 encoded.
5253
**
5254
** ^(For example, given the database schema:
5255
**
5256
** CREATE TABLE t1(c1 VARIANT);
5257
**
5258
** and the following statement to be compiled:
5259
**
5260
** SELECT c1 + 1, c1 FROM t1;
5261
**
5262
** this routine would return the string "VARIANT" for the second result
5263
** column (i==1), and a NULL pointer for the first result column (i==0).)^
5264
**
5265
** ^SQLite uses dynamic run-time typing.  ^So just because a column
5266
** is declared to contain a particular type does not mean that the
5267
** data stored in that column is of the declared type.  SQLite is
5268
** strongly typed, but the typing is dynamic not static.  ^Type
5269
** is associated with individual values, not with the containers
5270
** used to hold those values.
5271
*/

SQLITE_API const void *sqlite3_column_decltype16(sqlite3_stmt*,int);

/*
5276
** CAPI3REF: Evaluate An SQL Statement
5277
** METHOD: sqlite3_stmt
5278
**
5279
** After a [prepared statement] has been prepared using any of
5280
** [sqlite3_prepare_v2()], [sqlite3_prepare_v3()], [sqlite3_prepare16_v2()],
5281
** or [sqlite3_prepare16_v3()] or one of the legacy
5282
** interfaces [sqlite3_prepare()] or [sqlite3_prepare16()], this function
5283
** must be called one or more times to evaluate the statement.
5284
**
5285
** The details of the behavior of the sqlite3_step() interface depend
5286
** on whether the statement was prepared using the newer "vX" interfaces
5287
** [sqlite3_prepare_v3()], [sqlite3_prepare_v2()], [sqlite3_prepare16_v3()],
5288
** [sqlite3_prepare16_v2()] or the older legacy
5289
** interfaces [sqlite3_prepare()] and [sqlite3_prepare16()].  The use of the
5290
** new "vX" interface is recommended for new applications but the legacy
5291
** interface will continue to be supported.
5292
**
5293
** ^In the legacy interface, the return value will be either [SQLITE_BUSY],
5294
** [SQLITE_DONE], [SQLITE_ROW], [SQLITE_ERROR], or [SQLITE_MISUSE].
5295
** ^With the "v2" interface, any of the other [result codes] or
5296
** [extended result codes] might be returned as well.
5297
**
5298
** ^[SQLITE_BUSY] means that the database engine was unable to acquire the
5299
** database locks it needs to do its job.  ^If the statement is a [COMMIT]
5300
** or occurs outside of an explicit transaction, then you can retry the
5301
** statement.  If the statement is not a [COMMIT] and occurs within an
5302
** explicit transaction then you should rollback the transaction before
5303
** continuing.
5304
**
5305
** ^[SQLITE_DONE] means that the statement has finished executing
5306
** successfully.  sqlite3_step() should not be called again on this virtual
5307
** machine without first calling [sqlite3_reset()] to reset the virtual
5308
** machine back to its initial state.
5309
**
5310
** ^If the SQL statement being executed returns any data, then [SQLITE_ROW]
5311
** is returned each time a new row of data is ready for processing by the
5312
** caller. The values may be accessed using the [column access functions].
5313
** sqlite3_step() is called again to retrieve the next row of data.
5314
**
5315
** ^[SQLITE_ERROR] means that a run-time error (such as a constraint
5316
** violation) has occurred.  sqlite3_step() should not be called again on
5317
** the VM. More information may be found by calling [sqlite3_errmsg()].
5318
** ^With the legacy interface, a more specific error code (for example,
5319
** [SQLITE_INTERRUPT], [SQLITE_SCHEMA], [SQLITE_CORRUPT], and so forth)
5320
** can be obtained by calling [sqlite3_reset()] on the
5321
** [prepared statement].  ^In the "v2" interface,
5322
** the more specific error code is returned directly by sqlite3_step().
5323
**
5324
** [SQLITE_MISUSE] means that this routine was called inappropriately.
5325
** Perhaps it was called on a [prepared statement] that has
5326
** already been [sqlite3_finalize | finalized] or on one that had
5327
** previously returned [SQLITE_ERROR] or [SQLITE_DONE].  Or it could
5328
** be the case that the same database connection is being used by two or
5329
** more threads at the same moment in time.
5330
**
5331
** For all versions of SQLite up to and including 3.6.23.1, a call to
5332
** [sqlite3_reset()] was required after sqlite3_step() returned anything
5333
** other than [SQLITE_ROW] before any subsequent invocation of
5334
** sqlite3_step().  Failure to reset the prepared statement using
5335
** [sqlite3_reset()] would result in an [SQLITE_MISUSE] return from
5336
** sqlite3_step().  But after [version 3.6.23.1] ([dateof:3.6.23.1]),
5337
** sqlite3_step() began
5338
** calling [sqlite3_reset()] automatically in this circumstance rather
5339
** than returning [SQLITE_MISUSE].  This is not considered a compatibility
5340
** break because any application that ever receives an SQLITE_MISUSE error
5341
** is broken by definition.  The [SQLITE_OMIT_AUTORESET] compile-time option
5342
** can be used to restore the legacy behavior.
5343
**
5344
** <b>Goofy Interface Alert:</b> In the legacy interface, the sqlite3_step()
5345
** API always returns a generic error code, [SQLITE_ERROR], following any
5346
** error other than [SQLITE_BUSY] and [SQLITE_MISUSE].  You must call
5347
** [sqlite3_reset()] or [sqlite3_finalize()] in order to find one of the
5348
** specific [error codes] that better describes the error.
5349
** We admit that this is a goofy design.  The problem has been fixed
5350
** with the "v2" interface.  If you prepare all of your SQL statements
5351
** using [sqlite3_prepare_v3()] or [sqlite3_prepare_v2()]
5352
** or [sqlite3_prepare16_v2()] or [sqlite3_prepare16_v3()] instead
5353
** of the legacy [sqlite3_prepare()] and [sqlite3_prepare16()] interfaces,
5354
** then the more specific [error codes] are returned directly
5355
** by sqlite3_step().  The use of the "vX" interfaces is recommended.
5356
*/
5357
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_step(sqlite3_stmt*);
5358
5359
/*
5360
** CAPI3REF: Number of columns in a result set
5361
** METHOD: sqlite3_stmt
5362
**
5363
** ^The sqlite3_data_count(P) interface returns the number of columns in the
5364
** current row of the result set of [prepared statement] P.
5365

5366
** (via calls to the [sqlite3_column_int | sqlite3_column()] family of
5367
** interfaces) then sqlite3_data_count(P) returns 0.
5368
** ^The sqlite3_data_count(P) routine also returns 0 if P is a NULL pointer.
5369
** ^The sqlite3_data_count(P) routine returns 0 if the previous call to
5370
** [sqlite3_step](P) returned [SQLITE_DONE].  ^The sqlite3_data_count(P)
5371
** will return non-zero if previous call to [sqlite3_step](P) returned
5372
** [SQLITE_ROW], except in the case of the [PRAGMA incremental_vacuum]
5373
** where it always returns zero since each step of that multi-step
5374
** pragma returns 0 columns of data.
5375
**
5376
** See also: [sqlite3_column_count()]
5377
*/
5378
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_data_count(sqlite3_stmt *pStmt);

5380
/*
5381
** CAPI3REF: Fundamental Datatypes
5382
** KEYWORDS: SQLITE_TEXT
5383
**
5384
** ^(Every value in SQLite has one of five fundamental datatypes:
5385
**
5386
** <ul>
5387
** <li> 64-bit signed integer
5388
** <li> 64-bit IEEE floating point number
5389
** <li> string
5390
** <li> BLOB
5391
** <li> NULL
5392
** </ul>)^
5393
**
5394
** These constants are codes for each of those types.
5395
**
5396
** Note that the SQLITE_TEXT constant was also used in SQLite version 2
5397
** for a completely different meaning.  Software that links against both
5398
** SQLite version 2 and SQLite version 3 should use SQLITE3_TEXT, not
5399
** SQLITE_TEXT.
5400
*/
5401
#define SQLITE_INTEGER  1
5402
#define SQLITE_FLOAT    2
5403
#define SQLITE_BLOB     4
5404
#define SQLITE_NULL     5
5405
#ifdef SQLITE_TEXT
5406
# undef SQLITE_TEXT
5407
#else
5408
# define SQLITE_TEXT     3
5409
#endif
5410
#define SQLITE3_TEXT     3
5411
5412
/*
5413
** CAPI3REF: Result Values From A Query
5414
** KEYWORDS: {column access functions}
5415
** METHOD: sqlite3_stmt
5416
**
5417
** <b>Summary:</b>
5418
** <blockquote><table border=0 cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0>
5419
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_blob</b><td>&rarr;<td>BLOB result
5420
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_double</b><td>&rarr;<td>REAL result
5421
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_int</b><td>&rarr;<td>32-bit INTEGER result
5422
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_int64</b><td>&rarr;<td>64-bit INTEGER result
5423
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_text</b><td>&rarr;<td>UTF-8 TEXT result
5424
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_text16</b><td>&rarr;<td>UTF-16 TEXT result
5425
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_value</b><td>&rarr;<td>The result as an
5426
** [sqlite3_value|unprotected sqlite3_value] object.
5427
** <tr><td>&nbsp;<td>&nbsp;<td>&nbsp;
5428
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_bytes</b><td>&rarr;<td>Size of a BLOB
5429
** or a UTF-8 TEXT result in bytes
5430
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_bytes16&nbsp;&nbsp;</b>
5431
** <td>&rarr;&nbsp;&nbsp;<td>Size of UTF-16
5432
** TEXT in bytes
5433
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_column_type</b><td>&rarr;<td>Default
5434
** datatype of the result
5435
** </table></blockquote>
5436
**
5437
** <b>Details:</b>
5438
**
5439
** ^These routines return information about a single column of the current
5440
** result row of a query.  ^In every case the first argument is a pointer
5441
** to the [prepared statement] that is being evaluated (the [sqlite3_stmt*]
5442
** that was returned from [sqlite3_prepare_v2()] or one of its variants)
5443
** and the second argument is the index of the column for which information
5444
** should be returned. ^The leftmost column of the result set has the index 0.
5445
** ^The number of columns in the result can be determined using
5446
** [sqlite3_column_count()].
5447
**
5448
** If the SQL statement does not currently point to a valid row, or if the
5449
** column index is out of range, the result is undefined.
5450
** These routines may only be called when the most recent call to
5451
** [sqlite3_step()] has returned [SQLITE_ROW] and neither
5452
** [sqlite3_reset()] nor [sqlite3_finalize()] have been called subsequently.
5453
** If any of these routines are called after [sqlite3_reset()] or
5454
** [sqlite3_finalize()] or after [sqlite3_step()] has returned
5455
** something other than [SQLITE_ROW], the results are undefined.
5456
** If [sqlite3_step()] or [sqlite3_reset()] or [sqlite3_finalize()]
5457
** are called from a different thread while any of these routines
5458
** are pending, then the results are undefined.
5459
**
5460
** The first six interfaces (_blob, _double, _int, _int64, _text, and _text16)
5461
** each return the value of a result column in a specific data format.  If
5462
** the result column is not initially in the requested format (for example,
5463
** if the query returns an integer but the sqlite3_column_text() interface
5464
** is used to extract the value) then an automatic type conversion is performed.
5465
**
5466
** ^The sqlite3_column_type() routine returns the
5467
** [SQLITE_INTEGER | datatype code] for the initial data type
5468
** of the result column.  ^The returned value is one of [SQLITE_INTEGER],
5469
** [SQLITE_FLOAT], [SQLITE_TEXT], [SQLITE_BLOB], or [SQLITE_NULL].
5470
** The return value of sqlite3_column_type() can be used to decide which
5471
** of the first six interface should be used to extract the column value.
5472
** The value returned by sqlite3_column_type() is only meaningful if no
5473
** automatic type conversions have occurred for the value in question.
5474
** After a type conversion, the result of calling sqlite3_column_type()
5475
** is undefined, though harmless.  Future
5476
** versions of SQLite may change the behavior of sqlite3_column_type()
5477
** following a type conversion.
5478
**
5479
** If the result is a BLOB or a TEXT string, then the sqlite3_column_bytes()
5480
** or sqlite3_column_bytes16() interfaces can be used to determine the size
5481
** of that BLOB or string.
5482
**
5483
** ^If the result is a BLOB or UTF-8 string then the sqlite3_column_bytes()
5484
** routine returns the number of bytes in that BLOB or string.
5485
** ^If the result is a UTF-16 string, then sqlite3_column_bytes() converts
5486
** the string to UTF-8 and then returns the number of bytes.
5487
** ^If the result is a numeric value then sqlite3_column_bytes() uses
5488
** [sqlite3_snprintf()] to convert that value to a UTF-8 string and returns
5489
** the number of bytes in that string.
5490
** ^If the result is NULL, then sqlite3_column_bytes() returns zero.
5491
**
5492
** ^If the result is a BLOB or UTF-16 string then the sqlite3_column_bytes16()
5493
** routine returns the number of bytes in that BLOB or string.
5494
** ^If the result is a UTF-8 string, then sqlite3_column_bytes16() converts
5495
** the string to UTF-16 and then returns the number of bytes.
5496
** ^If the result is a numeric value then sqlite3_column_bytes16() uses
5497
** [sqlite3_snprintf()] to convert that value to a UTF-16 string and returns
5498
** the number of bytes in that string.
5499
** ^If the result is NULL, then sqlite3_column_bytes16() returns zero.
5500
**
5501
** ^The values returned by [sqlite3_column_bytes()] and
5502
** [sqlite3_column_bytes16()] do not include the zero terminators at the end
5503
** of the string.  ^For clarity: the values returned by
5504
** [sqlite3_column_bytes()] and [sqlite3_column_bytes16()] are the number of
5505
** bytes in the string, not the number of characters.
5506
**
5507
** ^Strings returned by sqlite3_column_text() and sqlite3_column_text16(),
5508
** even empty strings, are always zero-terminated.  ^The return
5509
** value from sqlite3_column_blob() for a zero-length BLOB is a NULL pointer.
5510
**
5511
** ^Strings returned by sqlite3_column_text16() always have the endianness
5512
** which is native to the platform, regardless of the text encoding set
5513
** for the database.
5514
**
5515
** <b>Warning:</b> ^The object returned by [sqlite3_column_value()] is an
5516
** [unprotected sqlite3_value] object.  In a multithreaded environment,
5517
** an unprotected sqlite3_value object may only be used safely with
5518
** [sqlite3_bind_value()] and [sqlite3_result_value()].
5519
** If the [unprotected sqlite3_value] object returned by
5520
** [sqlite3_column_value()] is used in any other way, including calls
5521
** to routines like [sqlite3_value_int()], [sqlite3_value_text()],
5522
** or [sqlite3_value_bytes()], the behavior is not threadsafe.
5523
** Hence, the sqlite3_column_value() interface
5524
** is normally only useful within the implementation of
5525
** [application-defined SQL functions] or [virtual tables], not within
5526
** top-level application code.
5527
**
5528
** These routines may attempt to convert the datatype of the result.
5529
** ^For example, if the internal representation is FLOAT and a text result
5530
** is requested, [sqlite3_snprintf()] is used internally to perform the
5531
** conversion automatically.  ^(The following table details the conversions
5532
** that are applied:
5533
**
5534
** <blockquote>
5535
** <table border="1">
5536
** <tr><th> Internal<br>Type <th> Requested<br>Type <th>  Conversion
5537
**
5538
** <tr><td>  NULL    <td> INTEGER   <td> Result is 0
5539
** <tr><td>  NULL    <td>  FLOAT    <td> Result is 0.0
5540
** <tr><td>  NULL    <td>   TEXT    <td> Result is a NULL pointer
5541
** <tr><td>  NULL    <td>   BLOB    <td> Result is a NULL pointer
5542
** <tr><td> INTEGER  <td>  FLOAT    <td> Convert from integer to float
5543
** <tr><td> INTEGER  <td>   TEXT    <td> ASCII rendering of the integer
5544
** <tr><td> INTEGER  <td>   BLOB    <td> Same as INTEGER->TEXT
5545
** <tr><td>  FLOAT   <td> INTEGER   <td> [CAST] to INTEGER
5546
** <tr><td>  FLOAT   <td>   TEXT    <td> ASCII rendering of the float
5547
** <tr><td>  FLOAT   <td>   BLOB    <td> [CAST] to BLOB
5548
** <tr><td>  TEXT    <td> INTEGER   <td> [CAST] to INTEGER
5549
** <tr><td>  TEXT    <td>  FLOAT    <td> [CAST] to REAL
5550
** <tr><td>  TEXT    <td>   BLOB    <td> No change
5551
** <tr><td>  BLOB    <td> INTEGER   <td> [CAST] to INTEGER
5552
** <tr><td>  BLOB    <td>  FLOAT    <td> [CAST] to REAL
5553
** <tr><td>  BLOB    <td>   TEXT    <td> [CAST] to TEXT, ensure zero terminator
5554
** </table>
5555
** </blockquote>)^
5556
**
5557
** Note that when type conversions occur, pointers returned by prior
5558
** calls to sqlite3_column_blob(), sqlite3_column_text(), and/or
5559
** sqlite3_column_text16() may be invalidated.
5560
** Type conversions and pointer invalidations might occur
5561
** in the following cases:
5562
**
5563
** <ul>
5564
** <li> The initial content is a BLOB and sqlite3_column_text() or
5565
**      sqlite3_column_text16() is called.  A zero-terminator might
5566
**      need to be added to the string.</li>
5567
** <li> The initial content is UTF-8 text and sqlite3_column_bytes16() or
5568
**      sqlite3_column_text16() is called.  The content must be converted
5569
**      to UTF-16.</li>
5570
** <li> The initial content is UTF-16 text and sqlite3_column_bytes() or
5571
**      sqlite3_column_text() is called.  The content must be converted
5572
**      to UTF-8.</li>
5573
** </ul>
5574
**
5575
** ^Conversions between UTF-16be and UTF-16le are always done in place and do
5576
** not invalidate a prior pointer, though of course the content of the buffer
5577
** that the prior pointer references will have been modified.  Other kinds
5578
** of conversion are done in place when it is possible, but sometimes they
5579
** are not possible and in those cases prior pointers are invalidated.
5580
**
5581
** The safest policy is to invoke these routines
5582
** in one of the following ways:
5583
**
5584
** <ul>
5585
**  <li>sqlite3_column_text() followed by sqlite3_column_bytes()</li>
5586
**  <li>sqlite3_column_blob() followed by sqlite3_column_bytes()</li>
5587
**  <li>sqlite3_column_text16() followed by sqlite3_column_bytes16()</li>
5588
** </ul>
5589
**
5590
** In other words, you should call sqlite3_column_text(),
5591
** sqlite3_column_blob(), or sqlite3_column_text16() first to force the result
5592
** into the desired format, then invoke sqlite3_column_bytes() or
5593
** sqlite3_column_bytes16() to find the size of the result.  Do not mix calls
5594
** to sqlite3_column_text() or sqlite3_column_blob() with calls to
5595
** sqlite3_column_bytes16(), and do not mix calls to sqlite3_column_text16()
5596
** with calls to sqlite3_column_bytes().
5597
**
5598
** ^The pointers returned are valid until a type conversion occurs as
5599
** described above, or until [sqlite3_step()] or [sqlite3_reset()] or
5600
** [sqlite3_finalize()] is called.  ^The memory space used to hold strings
5601
** and BLOBs is freed automatically.  Do not pass the pointers returned
5602
** from [sqlite3_column_blob()], [sqlite3_column_text()], etc. into
5603
** [sqlite3_free()].
5604
**
5605
** As long as the input parameters are correct, these routines will only
5606
** fail if an out-of-memory error occurs during a format conversion.
5607
** Only the following subset of interfaces are subject to out-of-memory
5608
** errors:
5609
**
5610
** <ul>
5611
** <li> sqlite3_column_blob()
5612
** <li> sqlite3_column_text()
5613
** <li> sqlite3_column_text16()
5614
** <li> sqlite3_column_bytes()
5615
** <li> sqlite3_column_bytes16()
5616
** </ul>
5617
**
5618
** If an out-of-memory error occurs, then the return value from these
5619
** routines is the same as if the column had contained an SQL NULL value.
5620
** Valid SQL NULL returns can be distinguished from out-of-memory errors
5621
** by invoking the [sqlite3_errcode()] immediately after the suspect
5622
** return value is obtained and before any
5623
** other SQLite interface is called on the same [database connection].
5624
*/
5625
SQLITE_API const void *sqlite3_column_blob(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5626
SQLITE_API double sqlite3_column_double(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5627
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_column_int(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5628
SQLITE_API sqlite3_int64 sqlite3_column_int64(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5629
SQLITE_API const unsigned char *sqlite3_column_text(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5630
SQLITE_API const void *sqlite3_column_text16(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5631
SQLITE_API sqlite3_value *sqlite3_column_value(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5632
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_column_bytes(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5633
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_column_bytes16(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5634
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_column_type(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
5635
5636
/*
5637
** CAPI3REF: Destroy A Prepared Statement Object
5638
** DESTRUCTOR: sqlite3_stmt
5639
**
5640
** ^The sqlite3_finalize() function is called to delete a [prepared statement].
5641
** ^If the most recent evaluation of the statement encountered no errors
5642
** or if the statement has never been evaluated, then sqlite3_finalize() returns
5643
** SQLITE_OK.  ^If the most recent evaluation of statement S failed, then
5644
** sqlite3_finalize(S) returns the appropriate [error code] or
5645
** [extended error code].
5646
**
5647
** ^The sqlite3_finalize(S) routine can be called at any point during
5648
** the life cycle of [prepared statement] S:
5649
** before statement S is ever evaluated, after
5650
** one or more calls to [sqlite3_reset()], or after any call
5651
** to [sqlite3_step()] regardless of whether or not the statement has
5652
** completed execution.
5653
**
5654
** ^Invoking sqlite3_finalize() on a NULL pointer is a harmless no-op.
5655
**
5656
** The application must finalize every [prepared statement] in order to avoid
5657
** resource leaks.  It is a grievous error for the application to try to use
5658
** a prepared statement after it has been finalized.  Any use of a prepared
5659
** statement after it has been finalized can result in undefined and
5660
** undesirable behavior such as segfaults and heap corruption.
5661
*/
5662
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_finalize(sqlite3_stmt *pStmt);
5663
5664
/*
5665
** CAPI3REF: Reset A Prepared Statement Object
5666
** METHOD: sqlite3_stmt
5667
**
5668
** The sqlite3_reset() function is called to reset a [prepared statement]
5669
** object back to its initial state, ready to be re-executed.
5670
** ^Any SQL statement variables that had values bound to them using
5671
** the [sqlite3_bind_blob | sqlite3_bind_*() API] retain their values.
5672
** Use [sqlite3_clear_bindings()] to reset the bindings.
5673
**
5674
** ^The [sqlite3_reset(S)] interface resets the [prepared statement] S
5675
** back to the beginning of its program.
5676
**
5677
** ^The return code from [sqlite3_reset(S)] indicates whether or not
5678
** the previous evaluation of prepared statement S completed successfully.
5679
** ^If [sqlite3_step(S)] has never before been called on S or if
5680
** [sqlite3_step(S)] has not been called since the previous call
5681
** to [sqlite3_reset(S)], then [sqlite3_reset(S)] will return
5682
** [SQLITE_OK].
5683
**
5684
** ^If the most recent call to [sqlite3_step(S)] for the
5685
** [prepared statement] S indicated an error, then
5686
** [sqlite3_reset(S)] returns an appropriate [error code].
5687
** ^The [sqlite3_reset(S)] interface might also return an [error code]
5688
** if there were no prior errors but the process of resetting
5689
** the prepared statement caused a new error. ^For example, if an
5690
** [INSERT] statement with a [RETURNING] clause is only stepped one time,
5691
** that one call to [sqlite3_step(S)] might return SQLITE_ROW but
5692
** the overall statement might still fail and the [sqlite3_reset(S)] call
5693
** might return SQLITE_BUSY if locking constraints prevent the
5694
** database change from committing.  Therefore, it is important that
5695
** applications check the return code from [sqlite3_reset(S)] even if
5696
** no prior call to [sqlite3_step(S)] indicated a problem.
5697
**
5698
** ^The [sqlite3_reset(S)] interface does not change the values
5699
** of any [sqlite3_bind_blob|bindings] on the [prepared statement] S.
5700
*/
5701
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_reset(sqlite3_stmt *pStmt);
5702
5703
5704
/*
5705
** CAPI3REF: Create Or Redefine SQL Functions
5706
** KEYWORDS: {function creation routines}
5707
** METHOD: sqlite3
5708
**
5709
** ^These functions (collectively known as "function creation routines")
5710
** are used to add SQL functions or aggregates or to redefine the behavior
5711
** of existing SQL functions or aggregates. The only differences between
5712
** the three "sqlite3_create_function*" routines are the text encoding
5713
** expected for the second parameter (the name of the function being
5714
** created) and the presence or absence of a destructor callback for
5715
** the application data pointer. Function sqlite3_create_window_function()
5716
** is similar, but allows the user to supply the extra callback functions
5717
** needed by [aggregate window functions].
5718
**
5719
** ^The first parameter is the [database connection] to which the SQL
5720
** function is to be added.  ^If an application uses more than one database
5721
** connection then application-defined SQL functions must be added
5722
** to each database connection separately.
5723
**
5724
** ^The second parameter is the name of the SQL function to be created or
5725
** redefined.  ^The length of the name is limited to 255 bytes in a UTF-8
5726
** representation, exclusive of the zero-terminator.  ^Note that the name
5727
** length limit is in UTF-8 bytes, not characters nor UTF-16 bytes.
5728
** ^Any attempt to create a function with a longer name
5729
** will result in [SQLITE_MISUSE] being returned.
5730
**
5731
** ^The third parameter (nArg)
5732
** is the number of arguments that the SQL function or
5733
** aggregate takes. ^If this parameter is -1, then the SQL function or
5734
** aggregate may take any number of arguments between 0 and the limit
5735
** set by [sqlite3_limit]([SQLITE_LIMIT_FUNCTION_ARG]).  If the third
5736
** parameter is less than -1 or greater than 127 then the behavior is
5737
** undefined.
5738
**
5739
** ^The fourth parameter, eTextRep, specifies what
5740
** [SQLITE_UTF8 | text encoding] this SQL function prefers for
5741
** its parameters.  The application should set this parameter to
5742
** [SQLITE_UTF16LE] if the function implementation invokes
5743
** [sqlite3_value_text16le()] on an input, or [SQLITE_UTF16BE] if the
5744
** implementation invokes [sqlite3_value_text16be()] on an input, or
5745
** [SQLITE_UTF16] if [sqlite3_value_text16()] is used, or [SQLITE_UTF8]
5746
** otherwise.  ^The same SQL function may be registered multiple times using
5747
** different preferred text encodings, with different implementations for
5748
** each encoding.
5749
** ^When multiple implementations of the same function are available, SQLite
5750
** will pick the one that involves the least amount of data conversion.
5751
**
5752
** ^The fourth parameter may optionally be ORed with [SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC]
5753
** to signal that the function will always return the same result given
5754
** the same inputs within a single SQL statement.  Most SQL functions are
5755
** deterministic.  The built-in [random()] SQL function is an example of a
5756
** function that is not deterministic.  The SQLite query planner is able to
5757
** perform additional optimizations on deterministic functions, so use
5758
** of the [SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC] flag is recommended where possible.
5759
**
5760
** ^The fourth parameter may also optionally include the [SQLITE_DIRECTONLY]
5761
** flag, which if present prevents the function from being invoked from
5762
** within VIEWs, TRIGGERs, CHECK constraints, generated column expressions,
5763
** index expressions, or the WHERE clause of partial indexes.
5764
**
5765
** For best security, the [SQLITE_DIRECTONLY] flag is recommended for
5766
** all application-defined SQL functions that do not need to be
5767
** used inside of triggers, views, CHECK constraints, or other elements of
5768
** the database schema.  This flag is especially recommended for SQL
5769
** functions that have side effects or reveal internal application state.
5770
** Without this flag, an attacker might be able to modify the schema of
5771
** a database file to include invocations of the function with parameters
5772
** chosen by the attacker, which the application will then execute when
5773
** the database file is opened and read.
5774
**
5775
** ^(The fifth parameter is an arbitrary pointer.  The implementation of the
5776
** function can gain access to this pointer using [sqlite3_user_data()].)^
5777
**
5778
** ^The sixth, seventh and eighth parameters passed to the three
5779
** "sqlite3_create_function*" functions, xFunc, xStep and xFinal, are
5780
** pointers to C-language functions that implement the SQL function or
5781
** aggregate. ^A scalar SQL function requires an implementation of the xFunc
5782
** callback only; NULL pointers must be passed as the xStep and xFinal
5783
** parameters. ^An aggregate SQL function requires an implementation of xStep
5784
** and xFinal and NULL pointer must be passed for xFunc. ^To delete an existing
5785
** SQL function or aggregate, pass NULL pointers for all three function
5786
** callbacks.
5787
**
5788
** ^The sixth, seventh, eighth and ninth parameters (xStep, xFinal, xValue
5789
** and xInverse) passed to sqlite3_create_window_function are pointers to
5790
** C-language callbacks that implement the new function. xStep and xFinal
5791
** must both be non-NULL. xValue and xInverse may either both be NULL, in
5792
** which case a regular aggregate function is created, or must both be
5793
** non-NULL, in which case the new function may be used as either an aggregate
5794
** or aggregate window function. More details regarding the implementation
5795
** of aggregate window functions are
5796
** [user-defined window functions|available here].
5797
**
5798
** ^(If the final parameter to sqlite3_create_function_v2() or
5799
** sqlite3_create_window_function() is not NULL, then it is the destructor for
5800
** the application data pointer. The destructor is invoked when the function
5801
** is deleted, either by being overloaded or when the database connection
5802
** closes.)^ ^The destructor is also invoked if the call to
5803
** sqlite3_create_function_v2() fails.  ^When the destructor callback is
5804
** invoked, it is passed a single argument which is a copy of the application
5805
** data pointer which was the fifth parameter to sqlite3_create_function_v2().
5806
**
5807
** ^It is permitted to register multiple implementations of the same
5808
** functions with the same name but with either differing numbers of
5809
** arguments or differing preferred text encodings.  ^SQLite will use
5810
** the implementation that most closely matches the way in which the
5811
** SQL function is used.  ^A function implementation with a non-negative
5812
** nArg parameter is a better match than a function implementation with
5813
** a negative nArg.  ^A function where the preferred text encoding
5814
** matches the database encoding is a better
5815
** match than a function where the encoding is different.
5816
** ^A function where the encoding difference is between UTF16le and UTF16be
5817
** is a closer match than a function where the encoding difference is
5818
** between UTF8 and UTF16.
5819
**
5820
** ^Built-in functions may be overloaded by new application-defined functions.
5821
**
5822
** ^An application-defined function is permitted to call other
5823
** SQLite interfaces.  However, such calls must not
5824
** close the database connection nor finalize or reset the prepared
5825
** statement in which the function is running.
5826
*/
5827
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_function(
5828
  sqlite3 *db,
5829
  const char *zFunctionName,
5830
  int nArg,
5831
  int eTextRep,
5832
  void *pApp,
5833
  void (*xFunc)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**),
5834
  void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**),
5835
  void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*)
5836
);
5837
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_function16(
5838
  sqlite3 *db,
5839
  const void *zFunctionName,
5840
  int nArg,
5841
  int eTextRep,
5842
  void *pApp,
5843
  void (*xFunc)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**),
5844
  void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**),
5845
  void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*)
5846
);
5847
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_function_v2(
5848
  sqlite3 *db,
5849
  const char *zFunctionName,
5850
  int nArg,
5851
  int eTextRep,
5852
  void *pApp,
5853
  void (*xFunc)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**),
5854
  void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**),
5855
  void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*),
5856
  void(*xDestroy)(void*)
5857
);
5858
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_window_function(
5859
  sqlite3 *db,
5860
  const char *zFunctionName,
5861
  int nArg,
5862
  int eTextRep,
5863
  void *pApp,
5864
  void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**),
5865
  void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*),
5866
  void (*xValue)(sqlite3_context*),
5867
  void (*xInverse)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**),
5868
  void(*xDestroy)(void*)
5869
);
5870
5871
/*
5872
** CAPI3REF: Text Encodings
5873
**
5874
** These constants define integer codes that represent the various
5875
** text encodings supported by SQLite.
5876
**
5877
** <dl>
5878
** [[SQLITE_UTF8]] <dt>SQLITE_UTF8</dt><dd>Text is encoding as UTF-8</dd>
5879
**
5880
** [[SQLITE_UTF16LE]] <dt>SQLITE_UTF16LE</dt><dd>Text is encoding as UTF-16
5881
** with each code point being expressed "little endian" - the least significant
5882
** byte first.  This is the usual encoding, for example on Windows.</dd>
5883
**
5884
** [[SQLITE_UTF16BE]] <dt>SQLITE_UTF16BE</dt><dd>Text is encoding as UTF-16
5885
** with each code point being expressed "big endian" - the most significant
5886
** byte first.  This encoding is less common, but is still sometimes seen,
5887
** specially on older systems.
5888
**
5889
** [[SQLITE_UTF16]] <dt>SQLITE_UTF16</dt><dd>Text is encoding as UTF-16
5890
** with each code point being expressed either little endian or as big
5891
** endian, according to the native endianness of the host computer.
5892
**
5893
** [[SQLITE_ANY]] <dt>SQLITE_ANY</dt><dd>This encoding value may only be used
5894
** to declare the preferred text for [application-defined SQL functions]
5895
** created using [sqlite3_create_function()] and similar.  If the preferred
5896
** encoding (the 4th parameter to sqlite3_create_function() - the eTextRep
5897
** parameter) is SQLITE_ANY, that indicates that the function does not have
5898
** a preference regarding the text encoding of its parameters and can take
5899
** any text encoding that the SQLite core find convenient to supply.  This
5900
** option is deprecated.  Please do not use it in new applications.
5901
**
5902
** [[SQLITE_UTF16_ALIGNED]] <dt>SQLITE_UTF16_ALIGNED</dt><dd>This encoding
5903
** value may be used as the 3rd parameter (the eTextRep parameter) to
5904
** [sqlite3_create_collation()] and similar.  This encoding value means
5905
** that the application-defined collating sequence created expects its
5906
** input strings to be in UTF16 in native byte order, and that the start
5907
** of the strings must be aligned to a 2-byte boundary.
5908
**
5909
** [[SQLITE_UTF8_ZT]] <dt>SQLITE_UTF8_ZT</dt><dd>This option can only be
5910
** used to specify the text encoding to strings input to
5911
** [sqlite3_result_text64()] and [sqlite3_bind_text64()].
5912
** The SQLITE_UTF8_ZT encoding means that the input string (call it "z")
5913
** is UTF-8 encoded and that it is zero-terminated.  If the length parameter
5914
** (call it "n") is non-negative, this encoding option means that the caller
5915
** guarantees that z array contains at least n+1 bytes and that the z&#91;n&#93;
5916
** byte has a value of zero.
5917
** This option gives the same output as SQLITE_UTF8, but can be more efficient
5918
** by avoiding the need to make a copy of the input string, in some cases.
5919
** However, if z is allocated to hold fewer than n+1 bytes or if the
5920
** z&#91;n&#93; byte is not zero, undefined behavior may result.
5921
** </dl>
5922
*/
5923
#define SQLITE_UTF8           1    /* IMP: R-37514-35566 */
5924
#define SQLITE_UTF16LE        2    /* IMP: R-03371-37637 */
5925
#define SQLITE_UTF16BE        3    /* IMP: R-51971-34154 */
5926
#define SQLITE_UTF16          4    /* Use native byte order */
5927
#define SQLITE_ANY            5    /* Deprecated */
5928
#define SQLITE_UTF16_ALIGNED  8    /* sqlite3_create_collation only */
5929
#define SQLITE_UTF8_ZT       16    /* Zero-terminated UTF8 */
5930
5931
/*
5932
** CAPI3REF: Function Flags
5933
**
5934
** These constants may be ORed together with the
5935
** [SQLITE_UTF8 | preferred text encoding] as the fourth argument
5936
** to [sqlite3_create_function()], [sqlite3_create_function16()], or
5937
** [sqlite3_create_function_v2()].
5938
**
5939
** <dl>
5940
** [[SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC]] <dt>SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC</dt><dd>
5941
** The SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC flag means that the new function always gives
5942
** the same output when the input parameters are the same.
5943
** The [abs|abs() function] is deterministic, for example, but
5944
** [randomblob|randomblob()] is not.  Functions must
5945
** be deterministic in order to be used in certain contexts such as
5946
** with the WHERE clause of [partial indexes] or in [generated columns].
5947
** SQLite might also optimize deterministic functions by factoring them
5948
** out of inner loops.
5949
** </dd>
5950
**
5951
** [[SQLITE_DIRECTONLY]] <dt>SQLITE_DIRECTONLY</dt><dd>
5952
** The SQLITE_DIRECTONLY flag means that the function may only be invoked
5953
** from top-level SQL, and cannot be used in VIEWs or TRIGGERs nor in
5954
** schema structures such as [CHECK constraints], [DEFAULT clauses],
5955
** [expression indexes], [partial indexes], or [generated columns].
5956
** <p>
5957
** The SQLITE_DIRECTONLY flag is recommended for any
5958
** [application-defined SQL function]
5959
** that has side-effects or that could potentially leak sensitive information.
5960
** This will prevent attacks in which an application is tricked
5961
** into using a database file that has had its schema surreptitiously
5962
** modified to invoke the application-defined function in ways that are
5963
** harmful.
5964
** <p>
5965
** Some people say it is good practice to set SQLITE_DIRECTONLY on all
5966
** [application-defined SQL functions], regardless of whether or not they
5967
** are security sensitive, as doing so prevents those functions from being used
5968
** inside of the database schema, and thus ensures that the database
5969
** can be inspected and modified using generic tools (such as the [CLI])
5970
** that do not have access to the application-defined functions.
5971
** </dd>
5972
**
5973
** [[SQLITE_INNOCUOUS]] <dt>SQLITE_INNOCUOUS</dt><dd>
5974
** The SQLITE_INNOCUOUS flag means that the function is unlikely
5975
** to cause problems even if misused.  An innocuous function should have
5976
** no side effects and should not depend on any values other than its
5977
** input parameters. The [abs|abs() function] is an example of an
5978
** innocuous function.
5979
** The [load_extension() SQL function] is not innocuous because of its
5980
** side effects.
5981
** <p> SQLITE_INNOCUOUS is similar to SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC, but is not
5982
** exactly the same.  The [random|random() function] is an example of a
5983
** function that is innocuous but not deterministic.
5984
** <p>Some heightened security settings
5985
** ([SQLITE_DBCONFIG_TRUSTED_SCHEMA] and [PRAGMA trusted_schema=OFF])
5986
** disable the use of SQL functions inside views and triggers and in
5987
** schema structures such as [CHECK constraints], [DEFAULT clauses],
5988
** [expression indexes], [partial indexes], and [generated columns] unless
5989
** the function is tagged with SQLITE_INNOCUOUS.  Most built-in functions
5990
** are innocuous.  Developers are advised to avoid using the
5991
** SQLITE_INNOCUOUS flag for application-defined functions unless the
5992
** function has been carefully audited and found to be free of potentially
5993
** security-adverse side-effects and information-leaks.
5994
** </dd>
5995
**
5996
** [[SQLITE_SUBTYPE]] <dt>SQLITE_SUBTYPE</dt><dd>
5997
** The SQLITE_SUBTYPE flag indicates to SQLite that a function might call
5998
** [sqlite3_value_subtype()] to inspect the sub-types of its arguments.
5999
** This flag instructs SQLite to omit some corner-case optimizations that
6000
** might disrupt the operation of the [sqlite3_value_subtype()] function,
6001
** causing it to return zero rather than the correct subtype().
6002
** All SQL functions that invoke [sqlite3_value_subtype()] should have this
6003
** property.  If the SQLITE_SUBTYPE property is omitted, then the return
6004
** value from [sqlite3_value_subtype()] might sometimes be zero even though
6005
** a non-zero subtype was specified by the function argument expression.
6006
**
6007
** [[SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE]] <dt>SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE</dt><dd>
6008
** The SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE flag indicates to SQLite that a function might call
6009
** [sqlite3_result_subtype()] to cause a sub-type to be associated with its
6010
** result.
6011
** Every function that invokes [sqlite3_result_subtype()] should have this
6012
** property.  If it does not, then the call to [sqlite3_result_subtype()]
6013
** might become a no-op if the function is used as a term in an
6014
** [expression index].  On the other hand, SQL functions that never invoke
6015
** [sqlite3_result_subtype()] should avoid setting this property, as the
6016
** purpose of this property is to disable certain optimizations that are
6017
** incompatible with subtypes.
6018
**
6019
** [[SQLITE_SELFORDER1]] <dt>SQLITE_SELFORDER1</dt><dd>
6020
** The SQLITE_SELFORDER1 flag indicates that the function is an aggregate
6021
** that internally orders the values provided to the first argument.  The
6022
** ordered-set aggregate SQL notation with a single ORDER BY term can be
6023
** used to invoke this function.  If the ordered-set aggregate notation is
6024
** used on a function that lacks this flag, then an error is raised. Note
6025
** that the ordered-set aggregate syntax is only available if SQLite is
6026
** built using the -DSQLITE_ENABLE_ORDERED_SET_AGGREGATES compile-time option.
6027
** </dd>
6028
** </dl>
6029
*/
6030
#define SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC    0x000000800
6031
#define SQLITE_DIRECTONLY       0x000080000
6032
#define SQLITE_SUBTYPE          0x000100000
6033
#define SQLITE_INNOCUOUS        0x000200000
6034
#define SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE   0x001000000
6035
#define SQLITE_SELFORDER1       0x002000000
6036
6037

/*
6058
** CAPI3REF: Obtaining SQL Values
6059
** METHOD: sqlite3_value
6060
**
6061
** <b>Summary:</b>
6062
** <blockquote><table border=0 cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0>
6063
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_blob</b><td>&rarr;<td>BLOB value
6064
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_double</b><td>&rarr;<td>REAL value
6065
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_int</b><td>&rarr;<td>32-bit INTEGER value
6066
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_int64</b><td>&rarr;<td>64-bit INTEGER value
6067
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_pointer</b><td>&rarr;<td>Pointer value
6068
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_text</b><td>&rarr;<td>UTF-8 TEXT value
6069
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_text16</b><td>&rarr;<td>UTF-16 TEXT value in
6070
** the native byteorder
6071
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_text16be</b><td>&rarr;<td>UTF-16be TEXT value
6072
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_text16le</b><td>&rarr;<td>UTF-16le TEXT value
6073
** <tr><td>&nbsp;<td>&nbsp;<td>&nbsp;
6074
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_bytes</b><td>&rarr;<td>Size of a BLOB
6075
** or a UTF-8 TEXT in bytes
6076
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_bytes16&nbsp;&nbsp;</b>
6077
** <td>&rarr;&nbsp;&nbsp;<td>Size of UTF-16
6078
** TEXT in bytes
6079
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_type</b><td>&rarr;<td>Default
6080
** datatype of the value
6081
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_numeric_type&nbsp;&nbsp;</b>
6082
** <td>&rarr;&nbsp;&nbsp;<td>Best numeric datatype of the value
6083
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_nochange&nbsp;&nbsp;</b>
6084
** <td>&rarr;&nbsp;&nbsp;<td>True if the column is unchanged in an UPDATE
6085
** against a virtual table.
6086
** <tr><td><b>sqlite3_value_frombind&nbsp;&nbsp;</b>
6087
** <td>&rarr;&nbsp;&nbsp;<td>True if value originated from a [bound parameter]
6088
** </table></blockquote>
6089
**
6090
** <b>Details:</b>
6091
**
6092
** These routines extract type, size, and content information from
6093
** [protected sqlite3_value] objects.  Protected sqlite3_value objects
6094
** are used to pass parameter information into the functions that
6095
** implement [application-defined SQL functions] and [virtual tables].
6096
**
6097
** These routines work only with [protected sqlite3_value] objects.
6098
** Any attempt to use these routines on an [unprotected sqlite3_value]
6099
** is not threadsafe.
6100
**
6101
** ^These routines work just like the corresponding [column access functions]
6102
** except that these routines take a single [protected sqlite3_value] object
6103
** pointer instead of a [sqlite3_stmt*] pointer and an integer column number.
6104
**
6105
** ^The sqlite3_value_text16() interface extracts a UTF-16 string
6106
** in the native byte-order of the host machine.  ^The
6107
** sqlite3_value_text16be() and sqlite3_value_text16le() interfaces
6108
** extract UTF-16 strings as big-endian and little-endian respectively.
6109
**
6110
** ^If [sqlite3_value] object V was initialized
6111
** using [sqlite3_bind_pointer(S,I,P,X,D)] or [sqlite3_result_pointer(C,P,X,D)]
6112
** and if X and Y are strings that compare equal according to strcmp(X,Y),
6113
** then sqlite3_value_pointer(V,Y) will return the pointer P.  ^Otherwise,
6114
** sqlite3_value_pointer(V,Y) returns a NULL. The sqlite3_bind_pointer()
6115
** routine is part of the [pointer passing interface] added for SQLite 3.20.0.
6116
**
6117
** ^(The sqlite3_value_type(V) interface returns the
6118
** [SQLITE_INTEGER | datatype code] for the initial datatype of the
6119
** [sqlite3_value] object V. The returned value is one of [SQLITE_INTEGER],
6120
** [SQLITE_FLOAT], [SQLITE_TEXT], [SQLITE_BLOB], or [SQLITE_NULL].)^
6121
** Other interfaces might change the datatype for an sqlite3_value object.
6122
** For example, if the datatype is initially SQLITE_INTEGER and
6123
** sqlite3_value_text(V) is called to extract a text value for that
6124
** integer, then subsequent calls to sqlite3_value_type(V) might return
6125
** SQLITE_TEXT.  Whether or not a persistent internal datatype conversion
6126
** occurs is undefined and may change from one release of SQLite to the next.
6127
**
6128
** ^(The sqlite3_value_numeric_type() interface attempts to apply
6129
** numeric affinity to the value.  This means that an attempt is
6130
** made to convert the value to an integer or floating point.  If
6131
** such a conversion is possible without loss of information (in other
6132
** words, if the value is a string that looks like a number)
6133
** then the conversion is performed.  Otherwise no conversion occurs.
6134
** The [SQLITE_INTEGER | datatype] after conversion is returned.)^
6135
**
6136
** ^Within the [xUpdate] method of a [virtual table], the
6137
** sqlite3_value_nochange(X) interface returns true if and only if
6138
** the column corresponding to X is unchanged by the UPDATE operation
6139
** that the xUpdate method call was invoked to implement and if
6140
** the prior [xColumn] method call that was invoked to extract
6141
** the value for that column returned without setting a result (probably
6142
** because it queried [sqlite3_vtab_nochange()] and found that the column
6143
** was unchanging).  ^Within an [xUpdate] method, any value for which
6144
** sqlite3_value_nochange(X) is true will in all other respects appear
6145
** to be a NULL value.  If sqlite3_value_nochange(X) is invoked anywhere other
6146
** than within an [xUpdate] method call for an UPDATE statement, then
6147
** the return value is arbitrary and meaningless.
6148
**
6149
** ^The sqlite3_value_frombind(X) interface returns non-zero if the
6150
** value X originated from one of the [sqlite3_bind_int|sqlite3_bind()]
6151
** interfaces.  ^If X comes from an SQL literal value, or a table column,
6152
** or an expression, then sqlite3_value_frombind(X) returns zero.
6153
**
6154
** Please pay particular attention to the fact that the pointer returned
6155
** from [sqlite3_value_blob()], [sqlite3_value_text()], or
6156
** [sqlite3_value_text16()] can be invalidated by a subsequent call to
6157
** [sqlite3_value_bytes()], [sqlite3_value_bytes16()], [sqlite3_value_text()],
6158
** or [sqlite3_value_text16()].
6159
**
6160
** These routines must be called from the same thread as
6161
** the SQL function that supplied the [sqlite3_value*] parameters.
6162
**
6163
** As long as the input parameter is correct, these routines can only
6164
** fail if an out-of-memory error occurs while trying to do a
6165
** UTF8&rarr;UTF16 or UTF16&rarr;UTF8 conversion.
6166
** If an out-of-memory error occurs, then the return value from these
6167
** routines is the same as if the column had contained an SQL NULL value.
6168
** If the input sqlite3_value was not obtained from [sqlite3_value_dup()],
6169
** then valid SQL NULL returns can also be distinguished from
6170
** out-of-memory errors after extracting the value
6171
** by invoking the [sqlite3_errcode()] immediately after the suspicious
6172
** return value is obtained and before any
6173
** other SQLite interface is called on the same [database connection].
6174
** If the input sqlite3_value was obtained from sqlite3_value_dup() then
6175
** it is disconnected from the database connection and so sqlite3_errcode()
6176
** will not work.
6177
** In that case, the only way to distinguish an out-of-memory
6178
** condition from a true SQL NULL is to invoke sqlite3_value_type() on the
6179
** input to see if it is NULL prior to trying to extract the value.
6180
*/
6181
SQLITE_API const void *sqlite3_value_blob(sqlite3_value*);
6182
SQLITE_API double sqlite3_value_double(sqlite3_value*);
6183
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_value_int(sqlite3_value*);
6184
SQLITE_API sqlite3_int64 sqlite3_value_int64(sqlite3_value*);
6185
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_value_pointer(sqlite3_value*, const char*);
6186
SQLITE_API const unsigned char *sqlite3_value_text(sqlite3_value*);
6187
SQLITE_API const void *sqlite3_value_text16(sqlite3_value*);
6188
SQLITE_API const void *sqlite3_value_text16le(sqlite3_value*);
6189
SQLITE_API const void *sqlite3_value_text16be(sqlite3_value*);
6190
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_value_bytes(sqlite3_value*);
6191
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_value_bytes16(sqlite3_value*);
6192
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_value_type(sqlite3_value*);
6193
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_value_numeric_type(sqlite3_value*);
6194
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_value_nochange(sqlite3_value*);
6195
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_value_frombind(sqlite3_value*);
6196

6198
** CAPI3REF: Report the internal text encoding state of an sqlite3_value object

** METHOD: sqlite3_value

**
6201
** ^(The sqlite3_value_encoding(X) interface returns one of [SQLITE_UTF8],
6202

6210

6213

6214
** internal state of an [sqlite3_value] object.  Ordinary applications should
6215
** not need to know what the internal state of an sqlite3_value object is and
6216
** hence should not need to use this interface.

*/

**
6224

6225
** an [application-defined SQL function] argument V.  The subtype
6226

6228

6230

6231

6232

6233
** If the [SQLITE_SUBTYPE] property is omitted, then sqlite3_value_subtype()
6234
** might return zero instead of the upstream subtype in some corner cases.

*/

6243

6244

6246

6247

6248
**
6249
** ^The sqlite3_value_free(V) interface frees an [sqlite3_value] object
6250
** previously obtained from [sqlite3_value_dup()].  ^If V is a NULL pointer
6251
** then sqlite3_value_free(V) is a harmless no-op.
6252
*/

/*
6257
** CAPI3REF: Obtain Aggregate Function Context
6258
** METHOD: sqlite3_context
6259
**
6260
** Implementations of aggregate SQL functions use this
6261
** routine to allocate memory for storing their state.
6262
**
6263
** ^The first time the sqlite3_aggregate_context(C,N) routine is called
6264
** for a particular aggregate function, SQLite allocates
6265
** N bytes of memory, zeroes out that memory, and returns a pointer
6266
** to the new memory. ^On second and subsequent calls to
6267
** sqlite3_aggregate_context() for the same aggregate function instance,
6268
** the same buffer is returned.  Sqlite3_aggregate_context() is normally
6269
** called once for each invocation of the xStep callback and then one
6270
** last time when the xFinal callback is invoked.  ^(When no rows match
6271
** an aggregate query, the xStep() callback of the aggregate function
6272
** implementation is never called and xFinal() is called exactly once.
6273
** In those cases, sqlite3_aggregate_context() might be called for the
6274
** first time from within xFinal().)^
6275
**
6276
** ^The sqlite3_aggregate_context(C,N) routine returns a NULL pointer
6277
** when first called if N is less than or equal to zero or if a memory
6278
** allocation error occurs.
6279
**
6280
** ^(The amount of space allocated by sqlite3_aggregate_context(C,N) is
6281
** determined by the N parameter on the first successful call.  Changing the
6282
** value of N in any subsequent call to sqlite3_aggregate_context() within
6283
** the same aggregate function instance will not resize the memory
6284
** allocation.)^  Within the xFinal callback, it is customary to set
6285
** N=0 in calls to sqlite3_aggregate_context(C,N) so that no
6286
** pointless memory allocations occur.
6287
**
6288
** ^SQLite automatically frees the memory allocated by
6289
** sqlite3_aggregate_context() when the aggregate query concludes.
6290
**
6291
** The first parameter must be a copy of the
6292
** [sqlite3_context | SQL function context] that is the first parameter
6293
** to the xStep or xFinal callback routine that implements the aggregate
6294
** function.
6295
**
6296
** This routine must be called from the same thread in which
6297
** the aggregate SQL function is running.
6298
*/
6299
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_aggregate_context(sqlite3_context*, int nBytes);
6300
6301
/*
6302
** CAPI3REF: User Data For Functions
6303
** METHOD: sqlite3_context
6304
**
6305
** ^The sqlite3_user_data() interface returns a copy of
6306
** the pointer that was the pUserData parameter (the 5th parameter)
6307
** of the [sqlite3_create_function()]
6308
** and [sqlite3_create_function16()] routines that originally
6309
** registered the application defined function.
6310
**
6311
** This routine must be called from the same thread in which
6312
** the application-defined function is running.
6313
*/
6314
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_user_data(sqlite3_context*);

6317

6318

6319

6320

6321
** the pointer to the [database connection] (the 1st parameter)
6322
** of the [sqlite3_create_function()]
6323
** and [sqlite3_create_function16()] routines that originally
6324
** registered the application defined function.
6325
*/
6326
SQLITE_API sqlite3 *sqlite3_context_db_handle(sqlite3_context*);
