6328
/*
6329
** CAPI3REF: Function Auxiliary Data
6330
** METHOD: sqlite3_context
6331
**
6332
** These functions may be used by (non-aggregate) SQL functions to
6333
** associate auxiliary data with argument values. If the same argument
6334
** value is passed to multiple invocations of the same SQL function during
6335
** query execution, under some circumstances the associated auxiliary data
6336
** might be preserved.  An example of where this might be useful is in a
6337
** regular-expression matching function. The compiled version of the regular
6338
** expression can be stored as auxiliary data associated with the pattern
6339
** string. Then as long as the pattern string remains the same,
6340
** the compiled regular expression can be reused on multiple
6341
** invocations of the same function.
6342
**
6343
** ^The sqlite3_get_auxdata(C,N) interface returns a pointer to the auxiliary
6344
** data associated by the sqlite3_set_auxdata(C,N,P,X) function with the
6345
** Nth argument value to the application-defined function.  ^N is zero
6346
** for the left-most function argument.  ^If there is no auxiliary data
6347
** associated with the function argument, the sqlite3_get_auxdata(C,N)
6348
** interface returns a NULL pointer.
6349
**
6350
** ^The sqlite3_set_auxdata(C,N,P,X) interface saves P as auxiliary data for the
6351
** N-th argument of the application-defined function.  ^Subsequent
6352
** calls to sqlite3_get_auxdata(C,N) return P from the most recent
6353
** sqlite3_set_auxdata(C,N,P,X) call if the auxiliary data is still valid or
6354
** NULL if the auxiliary data has been discarded.
6355
** ^After each call to sqlite3_set_auxdata(C,N,P,X) where X is not NULL,
6356
** SQLite will invoke the destructor function X with parameter P exactly
6357
** once, when the auxiliary data is discarded.
6358
** SQLite is free to discard the auxiliary data at any time, including: <ul>
6359
** <li> ^(when the corresponding function parameter changes)^, or
6360
** <li> ^(when [sqlite3_reset()] or [sqlite3_finalize()] is called for the
6361
**      SQL statement)^, or
6362
** <li> ^(when sqlite3_set_auxdata() is invoked again on the same
6363
**       parameter)^, or
6364
** <li> ^(during the original sqlite3_set_auxdata() call when a memory
6365
**      allocation error occurs.)^
6366
** <li> ^(during the original sqlite3_set_auxdata() call if the function
6367
**      is evaluated during query planning instead of during query execution,
6368
**      as sometimes happens with [SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT4].)^ </ul>
6369
**
6370
** Note the last two bullets in particular.  The destructor X in
6371
** sqlite3_set_auxdata(C,N,P,X) might be called immediately, before the
6372
** sqlite3_set_auxdata() interface even returns.  Hence sqlite3_set_auxdata()
6373
** should be called near the end of the function implementation and the
6374
** function implementation should not make any use of P after
6375
** sqlite3_set_auxdata() has been called.  Furthermore, a call to
6376
** sqlite3_get_auxdata() that occurs immediately after a corresponding call
6377
** to sqlite3_set_auxdata() might still return NULL if an out-of-memory
6378
** condition occurred during the sqlite3_set_auxdata() call or if the
6379
** function is being evaluated during query planning rather than during
6380
** query execution.
6381
**
6382
** ^(In practice, auxiliary data is preserved between function calls for
6383
** function parameters that are compile-time constants, including literal
6384
** values and [parameters] and expressions composed from the same.)^
6385
**
6386
** The value of the N parameter to these interfaces should be non-negative.
6387
** Future enhancements may make use of negative N values to define new
6388
** kinds of function caching behavior.
6389
**
6390
** These routines must be called from the same thread in which
6391
** the SQL function is running.
6392
**
6393
** See also: [sqlite3_get_clientdata()] and [sqlite3_set_clientdata()].
6394
*/
6395
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_get_auxdata(sqlite3_context*, int N);
6396
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_set_auxdata(sqlite3_context*, int N, void*, void (*)(void*));
6397
6398
/*
6399
** CAPI3REF: Database Connection Client Data
6400
** METHOD: sqlite3
6401
**
6402
** These functions are used to associate one or more named pointers
6403
** with a [database connection].
6404
** A call to sqlite3_set_clientdata(D,N,P,X) causes the pointer P
6405
** to be attached to [database connection] D using name N.  Subsequent
6406
** calls to sqlite3_get_clientdata(D,N) will return a copy of pointer P
6407
** or a NULL pointer if there were no prior calls to
6408
** sqlite3_set_clientdata() with the same values of D and N.
6409
** Names are compared using strcmp() and are thus case sensitive.
6410
** It returns 0 on success and SQLITE_NOMEM on allocation failure.
6411
**
6412
** If P and X are both non-NULL, then the destructor X is invoked with
6413
** argument P on the first of the following occurrences:
6414
** <ul>
6415
** <li> An out-of-memory error occurs during the call to
6416
**      sqlite3_set_clientdata() which attempts to register pointer P.
6417
** <li> A subsequent call to sqlite3_set_clientdata(D,N,P,X) is made
6418
**      with the same D and N parameters.
6419
** <li> The database connection closes.  SQLite does not make any guarantees
6420
**      about the order in which destructors are called, only that all
6421
**      destructors will be called exactly once at some point during the
6422
**      database connection closing process.
6423
** </ul>
6424
**
6425
** SQLite does not do anything with client data other than invoke
6426
** destructors on the client data at the appropriate time.  The intended
6427
** use for client data is to provide a mechanism for wrapper libraries
6428
** to store additional information about an SQLite database connection.
6429
**
6430
** There is no limit (other than available memory) on the number of different
6431
** client data pointers (with different names) that can be attached to a
6432
** single database connection.  However, the current implementation stores
6433
** the content on a linked list.  Insert and retrieval performance will
6434
** be proportional to the number of entries.  The design use case, and
6435
** the use case for which the implementation is optimized, is
6436
** that an application will store only small number of client data names,
6437
** typically just one or two.  This interface is not intended to be a
6438
** generalized key/value store for thousands or millions of keys.  It
6439
** will work for that, but performance might be disappointing.
6440
**
6441
** There is no way to enumerate the client data pointers
6442
** associated with a database connection.  The N parameter can be thought
6443
** of as a secret key such that only code that knows the secret key is able
6444
** to access the associated data.
6445
**
6446
** Security Warning:  These interfaces should not be exposed in scripting
6447
** languages or in other circumstances where it might be possible for an
6448
** attacker to invoke them.  Any agent that can invoke these interfaces
6449
** can probably also take control of the process.
6450
**
6451
** Database connection client data is only available for SQLite
6452
** version 3.44.0 ([dateof:3.44.0]) and later.
6453
**
6454
** See also: [sqlite3_set_auxdata()] and [sqlite3_get_auxdata()].
6455
*/
6456
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_get_clientdata(sqlite3*,const char*);
6457
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_set_clientdata(sqlite3*, const char*, void*, void(*)(void*));
6458
6459
/*
6460
** CAPI3REF: Constants Defining Special Destructor Behavior
6461
**
6462
** These are special values for the destructor that is passed in as the
6463
** final argument to routines like [sqlite3_result_blob()].  ^If the destructor
6464
** argument is SQLITE_STATIC, it means that the content pointer is constant
6465
** and will never change.  It does not need to be destroyed.  ^The
6466
** SQLITE_TRANSIENT value means that the content will likely change in
6467
** the near future and that SQLite should make its own private copy of
6468
** the content before returning.
6469
**
6470
** The typedef is necessary to work around problems in certain
6471
** C++ compilers.
6472
*/
6473
typedef void (*sqlite3_destructor_type)(void*);
6474
#define SQLITE_STATIC      ((sqlite3_destructor_type)0)
6475
#define SQLITE_TRANSIENT   ((sqlite3_destructor_type)-1)
6476
6477
/*
6478
** CAPI3REF: Setting The Result Of An SQL Function
6479
** METHOD: sqlite3_context
6480
**
6481
** These routines are used by the xFunc or xFinal callbacks that
6482
** implement SQL functions and aggregates.  See
6483
** [sqlite3_create_function()] and [sqlite3_create_function16()]
6484
** for additional information.
6485
**
6486
** These functions work very much like the [parameter binding] family of
6487
** functions used to bind values to host parameters in prepared statements.
6488
** Refer to the [SQL parameter] documentation for additional information.
6489
**
6490
** ^The sqlite3_result_blob() interface sets the result from
6491
** an application-defined function to be the BLOB whose content is pointed
6492
** to by the second parameter and which is N bytes long where N is the
6493
** third parameter.
6494
**
6495
** ^The sqlite3_result_zeroblob(C,N) and sqlite3_result_zeroblob64(C,N)
6496
** interfaces set the result of the application-defined function to be
6497
** a BLOB containing all zero bytes and N bytes in size.  The
6498
** zeroblob64(C,N) interface returns a [result code], which is normally
6499
** [SQLITE_OK] but might be some other value if the requested operation
6500
** could not be complete, for example if insufficient memory is available
6501
** or if the value of N is out of range.
6502
**
6503
** ^The sqlite3_result_double() interface sets the result from
6504
** an application-defined function to be a floating point value specified
6505
** by its 2nd argument.
6506
**
6507
** ^The sqlite3_result_error() and sqlite3_result_error16() functions
6508
** cause the implemented SQL function to throw an exception.
6509
** ^SQLite uses the string pointed to by the
6510
** 2nd parameter of sqlite3_result_error() or sqlite3_result_error16()
6511
** as the text of an error message.  ^SQLite interprets the error
6512
** message string from sqlite3_result_error() as UTF-8. ^SQLite
6513
** interprets the string from sqlite3_result_error16() as UTF-16 using
6514
** the same [byte-order determination rules] as [sqlite3_bind_text16()].
6515
** ^If the third parameter to sqlite3_result_error()
6516
** or sqlite3_result_error16() is negative then SQLite takes as the error
6517
** message all text up through the first zero character.
6518
** ^If the third parameter to sqlite3_result_error() or
6519
** sqlite3_result_error16() is non-negative then SQLite takes that many
6520
** bytes (not characters) from the 2nd parameter as the error message.
6521
** ^The sqlite3_result_error() and sqlite3_result_error16()
6522
** routines make a private copy of the error message text before
6523
** they return.  Hence, the calling function can deallocate or
6524
** modify the text after they return without harm.
6525
** ^The sqlite3_result_error_code() function changes the error code
6526
** returned by SQLite as a result of an error in a function.  ^By default,
6527
** the error code is SQLITE_ERROR.  ^A subsequent call to sqlite3_result_error()
6528
** or sqlite3_result_error16() resets the error code to SQLITE_ERROR.
6529
**
6530
** ^The sqlite3_result_error_toobig() interface causes SQLite to throw an
6531
** error indicating that a string or BLOB is too long to represent.
6532
**
6533
** ^The sqlite3_result_error_nomem() interface causes SQLite to throw an
6534
** error indicating that a memory allocation failed.
6535
**
6536
** ^The sqlite3_result_int() interface sets the return value
6537
** of the application-defined function to be the 32-bit signed integer
6538
** value given in the 2nd argument.
6539
** ^The sqlite3_result_int64() interface sets the return value
6540
** of the application-defined function to be the 64-bit signed integer
6541
** value given in the 2nd argument.
6542
**
6543
** ^The sqlite3_result_null() interface sets the return value
6544
** of the application-defined function to be NULL.
6545
**
6546
** ^The sqlite3_result_text(), sqlite3_result_text16(),
6547
** sqlite3_result_text16le(), and sqlite3_result_text16be() interfaces
6548
** set the return value of the application-defined function to be
6549
** a text string which is represented as UTF-8, UTF-16 native byte order,
6550
** UTF-16 little endian, or UTF-16 big endian, respectively.
6551
** ^The sqlite3_result_text64(C,Z,N,D,E) interface sets the return value of an
6552
** application-defined function to be a text string in an encoding
6553
** specified the E parameter, which must be one
6554
** of [SQLITE_UTF8], [SQLITE_UTF8_ZT], [SQLITE_UTF16], [SQLITE_UTF16BE],
6555
** or [SQLITE_UTF16LE].  ^The special value [SQLITE_UTF8_ZT] means that
6556
** the result text is both UTF-8 and zero-terminated.  In other words,
6557
** SQLITE_UTF8_ZT means that the Z array holds at least N+1 bytes and that
6558
** the Z&#91;N&#93; is zero.
6559
** ^SQLite takes the text result from the application from
6560
** the 2nd parameter of the sqlite3_result_text* interfaces.
6561
** ^If the 3rd parameter to any of the sqlite3_result_text* interfaces
6562
** other than sqlite3_result_text64() is negative, then SQLite computes
6563
** the string length itself by searching the 2nd parameter for the first
6564
** zero character.
6565
** ^If the 3rd parameter to the sqlite3_result_text* interfaces
6566
** is non-negative, then as many bytes (not characters) of the text
6567
** pointed to by the 2nd parameter are taken as the application-defined
6568
** function result.  If the 3rd parameter is non-negative, then it
6569
** must be the byte offset into the string where the NUL terminator would
6570
** appear if the string were NUL terminated.  If any NUL characters occur
6571
** in the string at a byte offset that is less than the value of the 3rd
6572
** parameter, then the resulting string will contain embedded NULs and the
6573
** result of expressions operating on strings with embedded NULs is undefined.
6574
** ^If the 4th parameter to the sqlite3_result_text* interfaces
6575
** or sqlite3_result_blob is a non-NULL pointer, then SQLite calls that
6576
** function as the destructor on the text or BLOB result when it has
6577
** finished using that result.
6578
** ^If the 4th parameter to the sqlite3_result_text* interfaces or to
6579
** sqlite3_result_blob is the special constant SQLITE_STATIC, then SQLite
6580
** assumes that the text or BLOB result is in constant space and does not
6581
** copy the content of the parameter nor call a destructor on the content
6582
** when it has finished using that result.
6583
** ^If the 4th parameter to the sqlite3_result_text* interfaces
6584
** or sqlite3_result_blob is the special constant SQLITE_TRANSIENT
6585
** then SQLite makes a copy of the result into space obtained
6586
** from [sqlite3_malloc()] before it returns.
6587
**
6588
** ^For the sqlite3_result_text16(), sqlite3_result_text16le(), and
6589
** sqlite3_result_text16be() routines, and for sqlite3_result_text64()
6590
** when the encoding is not UTF8, if the input UTF16 begins with a
6591
** byte-order mark (BOM, U+FEFF) then the BOM is removed from the
6592
** string and the rest of the string is interpreted according to the
6593
** byte-order specified by the BOM.  ^The byte-order specified by
6594
** the BOM at the beginning of the text overrides the byte-order
6595
** specified by the interface procedure.  ^So, for example, if
6596
** sqlite3_result_text16le() is invoked with text that begins
6597
** with bytes 0xfe, 0xff (a big-endian byte-order mark) then the
6598
** first two bytes of input are skipped and the remaining input
6599
** is interpreted as UTF16BE text.
6600
**
6601
** ^For UTF16 input text to the sqlite3_result_text16(),
6602
** sqlite3_result_text16be(), sqlite3_result_text16le(), and
6603
** sqlite3_result_text64() routines, if the text contains invalid
6604
** UTF16 characters, the invalid characters might be converted
6605
** into the unicode replacement character, U+FFFD.
6606
**
6607
** ^The sqlite3_result_value() interface sets the result of
6608
** the application-defined function to be a copy of the
6609
** [unprotected sqlite3_value] object specified by the 2nd parameter.  ^The
6610
** sqlite3_result_value() interface makes a copy of the [sqlite3_value]
6611
** so that the [sqlite3_value] specified in the parameter may change or
6612
** be deallocated after sqlite3_result_value() returns without harm.
6613
** ^A [protected sqlite3_value] object may always be used where an
6614
** [unprotected sqlite3_value] object is required, so either
6615
** kind of [sqlite3_value] object can be used with this interface.
6616
**
6617
** ^The sqlite3_result_pointer(C,P,T,D) interface sets the result to an
6618
** SQL NULL value, just like [sqlite3_result_null(C)], except that it
6619
** also associates the host-language pointer P or type T with that
6620
** NULL value such that the pointer can be retrieved within an
6621
** [application-defined SQL function] using [sqlite3_value_pointer()].
6622
** ^If the D parameter is not NULL, then it is a pointer to a destructor
6623
** for the P parameter.  ^SQLite invokes D with P as its only argument
6624
** when SQLite is finished with P.  The T parameter should be a static
6625
** string and preferably a string literal. The sqlite3_result_pointer()
6626
** routine is part of the [pointer passing interface] added for SQLite 3.20.0.
6627
**
6628
** If these routines are called from within a different thread
6629
** than the one containing the application-defined function that received
6630
** the [sqlite3_context] pointer, the results are undefined.
6631
*/
6632
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_blob(sqlite3_context*, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
6633
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_blob64(sqlite3_context*,const void*,
6634
                           sqlite3_uint64,void(*)(void*));
6635
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_double(sqlite3_context*, double);
6636
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_error(sqlite3_context*, const char*, int);
6637
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_error16(sqlite3_context*, const void*, int);
6638
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_error_toobig(sqlite3_context*);
6639
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_error_nomem(sqlite3_context*);
6640

6642

6644

6645

6646
                           void(*)(void*), unsigned char encoding);
6647

6649

6650

6651

/*
6657
** CAPI3REF: Setting The Subtype Of An SQL Function
6658
** METHOD: sqlite3_context
6659
**
6660
** The sqlite3_result_subtype(C,T) function causes the subtype of
6661
** the result from the [application-defined SQL function] with
6662
** [sqlite3_context] C to be the value T.  Only the lower 8 bits
6663
** of the subtype T are preserved in current versions of SQLite;
6664
** higher order bits are discarded.
6665
** The number of subtype bytes preserved by SQLite might increase
6666
** in future releases of SQLite.
6667
**
6668
** Every [application-defined SQL function] that invokes this interface
6669
** should include the [SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE] property in its
6670
** text encoding argument when the SQL function is
6671
** [sqlite3_create_function|registered].  If the [SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE]
6672
** property is omitted from the function that invokes sqlite3_result_subtype(),
6673
** then in some cases the sqlite3_result_subtype() might fail to set
6674
** the result subtype.
6675
**
6676
** If SQLite is compiled with -DSQLITE_STRICT_SUBTYPE=1, then any
6677
** SQL function that invokes the sqlite3_result_subtype() interface
6678
** and that does not have the SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE property will raise
6679
** an error.  Future versions of SQLite might enable -DSQLITE_STRICT_SUBTYPE=1
6680
** by default.
6681
*/
6682
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_subtype(sqlite3_context*,unsigned int);

/*
6685
** CAPI3REF: Define New Collating Sequences
6686
** METHOD: sqlite3
6687
**
6688
** ^These functions add, remove, or modify a [collation] associated
6689
** with the [database connection] specified as the first argument.
6690
**
6691
** ^The name of the collation is a UTF-8 string
6692
** for sqlite3_create_collation() and sqlite3_create_collation_v2()
6693
** and a UTF-16 string in native byte order for sqlite3_create_collation16().
6694
** ^Collation names that compare equal according to [sqlite3_strnicmp()] are
6695
** considered to be the same name.
6696
**
6697
** ^(The third argument (eTextRep) must be one of the constants:
6698
** <ul>
6699
** <li> [SQLITE_UTF8],
6700
** <li> [SQLITE_UTF16LE],
6701
** <li> [SQLITE_UTF16BE],
6702
** <li> [SQLITE_UTF16], or
6703
** <li> [SQLITE_UTF16_ALIGNED].
6704
** </ul>)^
6705
** ^The eTextRep argument determines the encoding of strings passed
6706
** to the collating function callback, xCompare.
6707
** ^The [SQLITE_UTF16] and [SQLITE_UTF16_ALIGNED] values for eTextRep
6708
** force strings to be UTF16 with native byte order.
6709
** ^The [SQLITE_UTF16_ALIGNED] value for eTextRep forces strings to begin
6710
** on an even byte address.
6711
**
6712
** ^The fourth argument, pArg, is an application data pointer that is passed
6713
** through as the first argument to the collating function callback.
6714
**
6715
** ^The fifth argument, xCompare, is a pointer to the collating function.
6716
** ^Multiple collating functions can be registered using the same name but
6717
** with different eTextRep parameters and SQLite will use whichever
6718
** function requires the least amount of data transformation.
6719
** ^If the xCompare argument is NULL then the collating function is
6720
** deleted.  ^When all collating functions having the same name are deleted,
6721
** that collation is no longer usable.
6722
**
6723
** ^The collating function callback is invoked with a copy of the pArg
6724
** application data pointer and with two strings in the encoding specified
6725
** by the eTextRep argument.  The two integer parameters to the collating
6726
** function callback are the length of the two strings, in bytes. The collating
6727
** function must return an integer that is negative, zero, or positive
6728
** if the first string is less than, equal to, or greater than the second,
6729
** respectively.  A collating function must always return the same answer
6730
** given the same inputs.  If two or more collating functions are registered
6731
** to the same collation name (using different eTextRep values) then all
6732
** must give an equivalent answer when invoked with equivalent strings.
6733
** The collating function must obey the following properties for all
6734
** strings A, B, and C:
6735
**
6736
** <ol>
6737
** <li> If A==B then B==A.
6738
** <li> If A==B and B==C then A==C.
6739
** <li> If A&lt;B THEN B&gt;A.
6740
** <li> If A&lt;B and B&lt;C then A&lt;C.
6741
** </ol>
6742
**
6743
** If a collating function fails any of the above constraints and that
6744
** collating function is registered and used, then the behavior of SQLite
6745
** is undefined.
6746
**
6747
** ^The sqlite3_create_collation_v2() works like sqlite3_create_collation()
6748
** with the addition that the xDestroy callback is invoked on pArg when
6749
** the collating function is deleted.
6750
** ^Collating functions are deleted when they are overridden by later
6751
** calls to the collation creation functions or when the
6752
** [database connection] is closed using [sqlite3_close()].
6753
**
6754
** ^The xDestroy callback is <u>not</u> called if the
6755
** sqlite3_create_collation_v2() function fails.  Applications that invoke
6756
** sqlite3_create_collation_v2() with a non-NULL xDestroy argument should
6757
** check the return code and dispose of the application data pointer
6758
** themselves rather than expecting SQLite to deal with it for them.
6759
** This is different from every other SQLite interface.  The inconsistency
6760
** is unfortunate but cannot be changed without breaking backwards
6761
** compatibility.
6762
**
6763
** See also:  [sqlite3_collation_needed()] and [sqlite3_collation_needed16()].
6764
*/
6765
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_collation(
6766
  sqlite3*,
6767
  const char *zName,
6768
  int eTextRep,
6769
  void *pArg,
6770
  int(*xCompare)(void*,int,const void*,int,const void*)
6771
);
6772
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_collation_v2(
6773
  sqlite3*,
6774
  const char *zName,
6775
  int eTextRep,
6776

6848

6851
** in the previous paragraphs.

6855

6856

6857

** ^(If this global variable is made to point to a string which is
6866
** the name of a folder (a.k.a. directory), then all temporary files
6867
** created by SQLite when using a built-in [sqlite3_vfs | VFS]
6868
** will be placed in that directory.)^  ^If this variable
6869
** is a NULL pointer, then SQLite performs a search for an appropriate
6870
** temporary file directory.

6874
** But for all other platforms, it is highly recommended that applications
6875
** neither read nor write this variable.  This global variable is a relic
6876
** that exists for backwards compatibility of legacy applications and should
6877
** be avoided in new projects.
6878
**
6879
** It is not safe to read or modify this variable in more than one
6880
** thread at a time.  It is not safe to read or modify this variable
6881
** if a [database connection] is being used at the same time in a separate
6882
** thread.
6883
** It is intended that this variable be set once
6884
** as part of process initialization and before any SQLite interface
6885
** routines have been called and that this variable remain unchanged
6886
** thereafter.

6888
** ^The [temp_store_directory pragma] may modify this variable and cause
6889
** it to point to memory obtained from [sqlite3_malloc].  ^Furthermore,
6890
** the [temp_store_directory pragma] always assumes that any string
6891
** that this variable points to is held in memory obtained from
6892
** [sqlite3_malloc] and the pragma may attempt to free that memory
6893
** using [sqlite3_free].
6894

6895

6896

6898

** so itself, taking care to only do so after all [database connection]
6901

6904

6906

6909
** LPCWSTR zPath = Windows::Storage::ApplicationData::Current->
6910
** &nbsp;     TemporaryFolder->Path->Data();

** char zPathBuf&#91;MAX_PATH + 1&#93;;
6912
** memset(zPathBuf, 0, sizeof(zPathBuf));
6913
** WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, zPath, -1, zPathBuf, sizeof(zPathBuf),
6914
** &nbsp;     NULL, NULL);

** sqlite3_temp_directory = sqlite3_mprintf("%s", zPathBuf);

** </pre></blockquote>

7102

7103
** <li value="1"> SQLITE_TXN_READ
7104
** <li value="2"> SQLITE_TXN_WRITE

7117
** constants in order to describe the transaction state of schema S
7118
** in [database connection] D.

7121
** [[SQLITE_TXN_NONE]] <dt>SQLITE_TXN_NONE</dt>
7122
** <dd>The SQLITE_TXN_NONE state means that no transaction is currently
7123
** pending.</dd>

7125

7126
** <dd>The SQLITE_TXN_READ state means that the database is currently
7127
** in a read transaction.  Content has been read from the database file
7128
** but nothing in the database file has changed.  The transaction state
7129
** will be advanced to SQLITE_TXN_WRITE if any changes occur and there are
7130
** no other conflicting concurrent write transactions.  The transaction
7131
** state will revert to SQLITE_TXN_NONE following a [ROLLBACK] or
7132
** [COMMIT].</dd>
7133
**
7134
** [[SQLITE_TXN_WRITE]] <dt>SQLITE_TXN_WRITE</dt>
7135
** <dd>The SQLITE_TXN_WRITE state means that the database is currently
7136
** in a write transaction.  Content has been written to the database file
7137
** but has not yet committed.  The transaction state will change to
7138
** SQLITE_TXN_NONE at the next [ROLLBACK] or [COMMIT].</dd>
7139
*/

#define SQLITE_TXN_NONE  0
7141
#define SQLITE_TXN_READ  1
7142
#define SQLITE_TXN_WRITE 2

/*
7161
** CAPI3REF: Commit And Rollback Notification Callbacks
7162
** METHOD: sqlite3
7163
**
7164
** ^The sqlite3_commit_hook() interface registers a callback
7165
** function to be invoked whenever a transaction is [COMMIT | committed].
7166
** ^Any callback set by a previous call to sqlite3_commit_hook()
7167
** for the same database connection is overridden.
7168
** ^The sqlite3_rollback_hook() interface registers a callback
7169
** function to be invoked whenever a transaction is [ROLLBACK | rolled back].
7170
** ^Any callback set by a previous call to sqlite3_rollback_hook()
7171
** for the same database connection is overridden.
7172
** ^The pArg argument is passed through to the callback.
7173
** ^If the callback on a commit hook function returns non-zero,
7174
** then the commit is converted into a rollback.
7175
**
7176
** ^The sqlite3_commit_hook(D,C,P) and sqlite3_rollback_hook(D,C,P) functions
7177
** return the P argument from the previous call of the same function
7178
** on the same [database connection] D, or NULL for
7179
** the first call for each function on D.
7180
**
7181
** The commit and rollback hook callbacks are not reentrant.
7182
** The callback implementation must not do anything that will modify
7183
** the database connection that invoked the callback.  Any actions
7184
** to modify the database connection must be deferred until after the
7185
** completion of the [sqlite3_step()] call that triggered the commit
7186
** or rollback hook in the first place.
7187
** Note that running any other SQL statements, including SELECT statements,
7188
** or merely calling [sqlite3_prepare_v2()] and [sqlite3_step()] will modify
7189
** the database connections for the meaning of "modify" in this paragraph.
7190
**
7191
** ^Registering a NULL function disables the callback.
7192
**
7193
** ^When the commit hook callback routine returns zero, the [COMMIT]
7194
** operation is allowed to continue normally.  ^If the commit hook
7195
** returns non-zero, then the [COMMIT] is converted into a [ROLLBACK].
7196
** ^The rollback hook is invoked on a rollback that results from a commit
7197
** hook returning non-zero, just as it would be with any other rollback.
7198
**
7199
** ^For the purposes of this API, a transaction is said to have been
7200
** rolled back if an explicit "ROLLBACK" statement is executed, or
7201
** an error or constraint causes an implicit rollback to occur.
7202
** ^The rollback callback is not invoked if a transaction is
7203
** automatically rolled back because the database connection is closed.
7204
**
7205
** See also the [sqlite3_update_hook()] interface.
7206
*/
7207
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_commit_hook(sqlite3*, int(*)(void*), void*);
7208
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_rollback_hook(sqlite3*, void(*)(void *), void*);
7209
7210
/*
7211
** CAPI3REF: Autovacuum Compaction Amount Callback
7212
** METHOD: sqlite3
7213
**
7214
** ^The sqlite3_autovacuum_pages(D,C,P,X) interface registers a callback
7215
** function C that is invoked prior to each autovacuum of the database
7216
** file.  ^The callback is passed a copy of the generic data pointer (P),
7217
** the schema-name of the attached database that is being autovacuumed,
7218
** the size of the database file in pages, the number of free pages,
7219
** and the number of bytes per page, respectively.  The callback should
7220
** return the number of free pages that should be removed by the
7221
** autovacuum.  ^If the callback returns zero, then no autovacuum happens.
7222
** ^If the value returned is greater than or equal to the number of
7223
** free pages, then a complete autovacuum happens.
7224
**
7225
** <p>^If there are multiple ATTACH-ed database files that are being
7226
** modified as part of a transaction commit, then the autovacuum pages
7227
** callback is invoked separately for each file.
7228
**
7229
** <p><b>The callback is not reentrant.</b> The callback function should
7230
** not attempt to invoke any other SQLite interface.  If it does, bad
7231
** things may happen, including segmentation faults and corrupt database
7232
** files.  The callback function should be a simple function that
7233
** does some arithmetic on its input parameters and returns a result.
7234
**
7235
** ^The X parameter to sqlite3_autovacuum_pages(D,C,P,X) is an optional
7236
** destructor for the P parameter.  ^If X is not NULL, then X(P) is
7237
** invoked whenever the database connection closes or when the callback
7238
** is overwritten by another invocation of sqlite3_autovacuum_pages().
7239
**
7240
** <p>^There is only one autovacuum pages callback per database connection.
7241
** ^Each call to the sqlite3_autovacuum_pages() interface overrides all
7242
** previous invocations for that database connection.  ^If the callback
7243
** argument (C) to sqlite3_autovacuum_pages(D,C,P,X) is a NULL pointer,
7244
** then the autovacuum steps callback is canceled.  The return value
7245
** from sqlite3_autovacuum_pages() is normally SQLITE_OK, but might
7246
** be some other error code if something goes wrong.  The current
7247
** implementation will only return SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_MISUSE, but other
7248
** return codes might be added in future releases.
7249
**
7250
** <p>If no autovacuum pages callback is specified (the usual case) or
7251
** a NULL pointer is provided for the callback,
7252
** then the default behavior is to vacuum all free pages.  So, in other
7253
** words, the default behavior is the same as if the callback function
7254
** were something like this:
7255
**
7256
** <blockquote><pre>
7257
** &nbsp;   unsigned int demonstration_autovac_pages_callback(
7258
** &nbsp;     void *pClientData,
7259
** &nbsp;     const char *zSchema,
7260
** &nbsp;     unsigned int nDbPage,
7261
** &nbsp;     unsigned int nFreePage,
7262
** &nbsp;     unsigned int nBytePerPage
7263
** &nbsp;   ){
7264
** &nbsp;     return nFreePage;
7265
** &nbsp;   }
7266
** </pre></blockquote>
7267
*/
7268
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_autovacuum_pages(
7269
  sqlite3 *db,
7270
  unsigned int(*)(void*,const char*,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int),
7271
  void*,
7272
  void(*)(void*)
7273
);
7274
7275

/*
7277
** CAPI3REF: Data Change Notification Callbacks
7278
** METHOD: sqlite3
7279
**
7280
** ^The sqlite3_update_hook() interface registers a callback function
7281
** with the [database connection] identified by the first argument
7282
** to be invoked whenever a row is updated, inserted or deleted in
7283
** a [rowid table].
7284
** ^Any callback set by a previous call to this function
7285
** for the same database connection is overridden.
7286
**
7287
** ^The second argument is a pointer to the function to invoke when a
7288
** row is updated, inserted or deleted in a rowid table.
7289
** ^The update hook is disabled by invoking sqlite3_update_hook()
7290
** with a NULL pointer as the second parameter.
7291
** ^The first argument to the callback is a copy of the third argument
7292
** to sqlite3_update_hook().
7293
** ^The second callback argument is one of [SQLITE_INSERT], [SQLITE_DELETE],
7294
** or [SQLITE_UPDATE], depending on the operation that caused the callback
7295
** to be invoked.
7296
** ^The third and fourth arguments to the callback contain pointers to the
7297
** database and table name containing the affected row.
7298
** ^The final callback parameter is the [rowid] of the row.
7299
** ^In the case of an update, this is the [rowid] after the update takes place.
7300
**
7301
** ^(The update hook is not invoked when internal system tables are
7302
** modified (i.e. sqlite_sequence).)^
7303
** ^The update hook is not invoked when [WITHOUT ROWID] tables are modified.
7304
**
7305
** ^In the current implementation, the update hook
7306
** is not invoked when conflicting rows are deleted because of an
7307
** [ON CONFLICT | ON CONFLICT REPLACE] clause.  ^Nor is the update hook
7308
** invoked when rows are deleted using the [truncate optimization].
7309
** The exceptions defined in this paragraph might change in a future
7310
** release of SQLite.
7311
**
7312
** Whether the update hook is invoked before or after the
7313
** corresponding change is currently unspecified and may differ
7314
** depending on the type of change. Do not rely on the order of the
7315
** hook call with regards to the final result of the operation which
7316
** triggers the hook.
7317
**
7318
** The update hook implementation must not do anything that will modify
7319
** the database connection that invoked the update hook.  Any actions
7320
** to modify the database connection must be deferred until after the
7321
** completion of the [sqlite3_step()] call that triggered the update hook.
7322
** Note that [sqlite3_prepare_v2()] and [sqlite3_step()] both modify their
7323
** database connections for the meaning of "modify" in this paragraph.
7324
**
7325
** ^The sqlite3_update_hook(D,C,P) function
7326
** returns the P argument from the previous call
7327
** on the same [database connection] D, or NULL for
7328
** the first call on D.
7329
**
7330
** See also the [sqlite3_commit_hook()], [sqlite3_rollback_hook()],
7331
** and [sqlite3_preupdate_hook()] interfaces.
7332
*/
7333
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_update_hook(
7334
  sqlite3*,
7335
  void(*)(void *,int ,char const *,char const *,sqlite3_int64),
7336
  void*
7337
);
7338
7339
/*
7340
** CAPI3REF: Enable Or Disable Shared Pager Cache
7341
**
7342
** ^(This routine enables or disables the sharing of the database cache
7343
** and schema data structures between [database connection | connections]
7344
** to the same database. Sharing is enabled if the argument is true
7345
** and disabled if the argument is false.)^
7346
**
7347
** This interface is omitted if SQLite is compiled with
7348
** [-DSQLITE_OMIT_SHARED_CACHE].  The [-DSQLITE_OMIT_SHARED_CACHE]
7349
** compile-time option is recommended because the
7350
** [use of shared cache mode is discouraged].
7351
**
7352
** ^Cache sharing is enabled and disabled for an entire process.
7353
** This is a change as of SQLite [version 3.5.0] ([dateof:3.5.0]).
7354
** In prior versions of SQLite,
7355
** sharing was enabled or disabled for each thread separately.
7356
**
7357
** ^(The cache sharing mode set by this interface effects all subsequent
7358
** calls to [sqlite3_open()], [sqlite3_open_v2()], and [sqlite3_open16()].
7359
** Existing database connections continue to use the sharing mode
7360
** that was in effect at the time they were opened.)^
7361
**
7362
** ^(This routine returns [SQLITE_OK] if shared cache was enabled or disabled
7363
** successfully.  An [error code] is returned otherwise.)^
7364
**
7365
** ^Shared cache is disabled by default. It is recommended that it stay
7366
** that way.  In other words, do not use this routine.  This interface
7367
** continues to be provided for historical compatibility, but its use is
7368
** discouraged.  Any use of shared cache is discouraged.  If shared cache
7369
** must be used, it is recommended that shared cache only be enabled for
7370
** individual database connections using the [sqlite3_open_v2()] interface
7371
** with the [SQLITE_OPEN_SHAREDCACHE] flag.
7372
**
7373
** Note: This method is disabled on MacOS X 10.7 and iOS version 5.0
7374
** and will always return SQLITE_MISUSE. On those systems,
7375
** shared cache mode should be enabled per-database connection via
7376
** [sqlite3_open_v2()] with [SQLITE_OPEN_SHAREDCACHE].
7377
**
7378
** This interface is threadsafe on processors where writing a
7379
** 32-bit integer is atomic.
7380
**
7381
** See Also:  [SQLite Shared-Cache Mode]
7382
*/
7383
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_enable_shared_cache(int);
7384

/*
7386
** CAPI3REF: Attempt To Free Heap Memory
7387
**
7388
** ^The sqlite3_release_memory() interface attempts to free N bytes
7389
** of heap memory by deallocating non-essential memory allocations
7390
** held by the database library.   Memory used to cache database
7391
** pages to improve performance is an example of non-essential memory.
7392
** ^sqlite3_release_memory() returns the number of bytes actually freed,
7393
** which might be more or less than the amount requested.
7394
** ^The sqlite3_release_memory() routine is a no-op returning zero
7395
** if SQLite is not compiled with [SQLITE_ENABLE_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT].
7396
**
7397
** See also: [sqlite3_db_release_memory()]
7398
*/
7399
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_release_memory(int);

7401
/*
7402
** CAPI3REF: Free Memory Used By A Database Connection
7403
** METHOD: sqlite3
7404
**
7405
** ^The sqlite3_db_release_memory(D) interface attempts to free as much heap
7406
** memory as possible from database connection D. Unlike the
7407
** [sqlite3_release_memory()] interface, this interface is in effect even
7408
** when the [SQLITE_ENABLE_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT] compile-time option is
7409
** omitted.
7410
**
7411
** See also: [sqlite3_release_memory()]
7412
*/
7413
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_db_release_memory(sqlite3*);

7415
/*
7416
** CAPI3REF: Impose A Limit On Heap Size
7417
**
7418
** These interfaces impose limits on the amount of heap memory that will be
7419
** used by all database connections within a single process.
7420
**
7421
** ^The sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64() interface sets and/or queries the
7422
** soft limit on the amount of heap memory that may be allocated by SQLite.
7423
** ^SQLite strives to keep heap memory utilization below the soft heap
7424
** limit by reducing the number of pages held in the page cache
7425
** as heap memory usages approaches the limit.
7426
** ^The soft heap limit is "soft" because even though SQLite strives to stay
7427
** below the limit, it will exceed the limit rather than generate
7428
** an [SQLITE_NOMEM] error.  In other words, the soft heap limit
7429
** is advisory only.
7430
**
7431
** ^The sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64(N) interface sets a hard upper bound of
7432
** N bytes on the amount of memory that will be allocated.  ^The
7433
** sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64(N) interface is similar to
7434
** sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64(N) except that memory allocations will fail
7435
** when the hard heap limit is reached.
7436
**
7437
** ^The return value from both sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64() and
7438
** sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64() is the size of
7439
** the heap limit prior to the call, or negative in the case of an
7440
** error.  ^If the argument N is negative
7441
** then no change is made to the heap limit.  Hence, the current
7442
** size of heap limits can be determined by invoking
7443
** sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64(-1) or sqlite3_hard_heap_limit(-1).
7444
**
7445
** ^Setting the heap limits to zero disables the heap limiter mechanism.
7446
**
7447
** ^The soft heap limit may not be greater than the hard heap limit.
7448
** ^If the hard heap limit is enabled and if sqlite3_soft_heap_limit(N)
7449
** is invoked with a value of N that is greater than the hard heap limit,
7450
** the soft heap limit is set to the value of the hard heap limit.
7451
** ^The soft heap limit is automatically enabled whenever the hard heap
7452
** limit is enabled. ^When sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64(N) is invoked and
7453
** the soft heap limit is outside the range of 1..N, then the soft heap
7454
** limit is set to N.  ^Invoking sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64(0) when the
7455
** hard heap limit is enabled makes the soft heap limit equal to the
7456
** hard heap limit.
7457
**
7458
** The memory allocation limits can also be adjusted using
7459
** [PRAGMA soft_heap_limit] and [PRAGMA hard_heap_limit].
7460
**
7461
** ^(The heap limits are not enforced in the current implementation
7462
** if one or more of following conditions are true:
7463
**
7464
** <ul>
7465
** <li> The limit value is set to zero.
7466
** <li> Memory accounting is disabled using a combination of the
7467
**      [sqlite3_config]([SQLITE_CONFIG_MEMSTATUS],...) start-time option and
7468
**      the [SQLITE_DEFAULT_MEMSTATUS] compile-time option.
7469
** <li> An alternative page cache implementation is specified using
7470
**      [sqlite3_config]([SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE2],...).
7471
** <li> The page cache allocates from its own memory pool supplied
7472
**      by [sqlite3_config]([SQLITE_CONFIG_PAGECACHE],...) rather than
7473
**      from the heap.
7474
** </ul>)^
7475
**
7476
** The circumstances under which SQLite will enforce the heap limits may
7477
** change in future releases of SQLite.
7478
*/
7479
SQLITE_API sqlite3_int64 sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64(sqlite3_int64 N);
7480
SQLITE_API sqlite3_int64 sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64(sqlite3_int64 N);
7481
7482
/*
7483
** CAPI3REF: Deprecated Soft Heap Limit Interface
7484
** DEPRECATED
7485
**
7486
** This is a deprecated version of the [sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64()]
7487
** interface.  This routine is provided for historical compatibility
7488
** only.  All new applications should use the
7489
** [sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64()] interface rather than this one.
7490
*/
7491
SQLITE_API SQLITE_DEPRECATED void sqlite3_soft_heap_limit(int N);

/*
7495
** CAPI3REF: Extract Metadata About A Column Of A Table
7496
** METHOD: sqlite3
7497
**
7498
** ^(The sqlite3_table_column_metadata(X,D,T,C,....) routine returns
7499
** information about column C of table T in database D
7500
** on [database connection] X.)^  ^The sqlite3_table_column_metadata()
7501
** interface returns SQLITE_OK and fills in the non-NULL pointers in
7502
** the final five arguments with appropriate values if the specified
7503
** column exists.  ^The sqlite3_table_column_metadata() interface returns
7504
** SQLITE_ERROR if the specified column does not exist.
7505
** ^If the column-name parameter to sqlite3_table_column_metadata() is a
7506
** NULL pointer, then this routine simply checks for the existence of the
7507
** table and returns SQLITE_OK if the table exists and SQLITE_ERROR if it
7508
** does not.  If the table name parameter T in a call to
7509
** sqlite3_table_column_metadata(X,D,T,C,...) is NULL then the result is
7510
** undefined behavior.
7511
**
7512
** ^The column is identified by the second, third and fourth parameters to
7513
** this function. ^(The second parameter is either the name of the database
7514
** (i.e. "main", "temp", or an attached database) containing the specified
7515
** table or NULL.)^ ^If it is NULL, then all attached databases are searched
7516
** for the table using the same algorithm used by the database engine to
7517
** resolve unqualified table references.
7518
**
7519
** ^The third and fourth parameters to this function are the table and column
7520
** name of the desired column, respectively.
7521
**
7522
** ^Metadata is returned by writing to the memory locations passed as the 5th
7523
** and subsequent parameters to this function. ^Any of these arguments may be
7524
** NULL, in which case the corresponding element of metadata is omitted.
7525
**
7526
** ^(<blockquote>
7527
** <table border="1">
7528
** <tr><th> Parameter <th> Output<br>Type <th>  Description
7529
**
7530
** <tr><td> 5th <td> const char* <td> Data type
7531
** <tr><td> 6th <td> const char* <td> Name of default collation sequence
7532
** <tr><td> 7th <td> int         <td> True if column has a NOT NULL constraint
7533
** <tr><td> 8th <td> int         <td> True if column is part of the PRIMARY KEY
7534
** <tr><td> 9th <td> int         <td> True if column is [AUTOINCREMENT]
7535
** </table>
7536
** </blockquote>)^
7537
**
7538
** ^The memory pointed to by the character pointers returned for the
7539
** declaration type and collation sequence is valid until the next
7540
** call to any SQLite API function.
7541
**
7542
** ^If the specified table is actually a view, an [error code] is returned.
7543
**
7544
** ^If the specified column is "rowid", "oid" or "_rowid_" and the table
7545
** is not a [WITHOUT ROWID] table and an
7546
** [INTEGER PRIMARY KEY] column has been explicitly declared, then the output
7547
** parameters are set for the explicitly declared column. ^(If there is no
7548
** [INTEGER PRIMARY KEY] column, then the outputs
7549
** for the [rowid] are set as follows:
7550
**
7551
** <pre>
7552
**     data type: "INTEGER"
7553
**     collation sequence: "BINARY"
7554
**     not null: 0
7555
**     primary key: 1
7556
**     auto increment: 0
7557
** </pre>)^
7558
**
7559
** ^This function causes all database schemas to be read from disk and
7560
** parsed, if that has not already been done, and returns an error if
7561
** any errors are encountered while loading the schema.
7562
*/
7563
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_table_column_metadata(
7564
  sqlite3 *db,                /* Connection handle */
7565
  const char *zDbName,        /* Database name or NULL */
7566
  const char *zTableName,     /* Table name */
7567
  const char *zColumnName,    /* Column name */
7568
  char const **pzDataType,    /* OUTPUT: Declared data type */
7569
  char const **pzCollSeq,     /* OUTPUT: Collation sequence name */
7570
  int *pNotNull,              /* OUTPUT: True if NOT NULL constraint exists */
7571
  int *pPrimaryKey,           /* OUTPUT: True if column part of PK */
7572
  int *pAutoinc               /* OUTPUT: True if column is auto-increment */
7573
);
7574

/*
7576
** CAPI3REF: Load An Extension
7577
** METHOD: sqlite3
7578
**
7579
** ^This interface loads an SQLite extension library from the named file.
7580
**
7581
** ^The sqlite3_load_extension() interface attempts to load an
7582
** [SQLite extension] library contained in the file zFile.  If
7583
** the file cannot be loaded directly, attempts are made to load
7584
** with various operating-system specific filename extensions added.
7585
** So for example, if "samplelib" cannot be loaded, then names like
7586
** "samplelib.so" or "samplelib.dylib" or "samplelib.dll" might
7587
** be tried also.
7588
**
7589
** ^The entry point is zProc.
7590
** ^(zProc may be 0, in which case SQLite will try to come up with an
7591
** entry point name on its own.  It first tries "sqlite3_extension_init".
7592
** If that does not work, it tries names of the form "sqlite3_X_init"
7593
** where X consists of the lower-case equivalent of all ASCII alphabetic
7594
** characters or all ASCII alphanumeric characters in the filename from
7595
** the last "/" to the first following "." and omitting any initial "lib".)^
7596
** ^The sqlite3_load_extension() interface returns
7597
** [SQLITE_OK] on success and [SQLITE_ERROR] if something goes wrong.
7598
** ^If an error occurs and pzErrMsg is not 0, then the
7599
** [sqlite3_load_extension()] interface shall attempt to
7600
** fill *pzErrMsg with error message text stored in memory
7601
** obtained from [sqlite3_malloc()]. The calling function
7602
** should free this memory by calling [sqlite3_free()].
7603
**
7604
** ^Extension loading must be enabled using
7605
** [sqlite3_enable_load_extension()] or
7606
** [sqlite3_db_config](db,[SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION],1,NULL)
7607
** prior to calling this API,
7608
** otherwise an error will be returned.
7609
**
7610
** <b>Security warning:</b> It is recommended that the
7611
** [SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION] method be used to enable only this
7612
** interface.  The use of the [sqlite3_enable_load_extension()] interface
7613
** should be avoided.  This will keep the SQL function [load_extension()]
7614
** disabled and prevent SQL injections from giving attackers
7615
** access to extension loading capabilities.
7616
**
7617
** See also the [load_extension() SQL function].
7618
*/
7619
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_load_extension(
7620
  sqlite3 *db,          /* Load the extension into this database connection */
7621
  const char *zFile,    /* Name of the shared library containing extension */
7622
  const char *zProc,    /* Entry point.  Derived from zFile if 0 */
7623
  char **pzErrMsg       /* Put error message here if not 0 */
7624
);
7625
7626
/*
7627
** CAPI3REF: Enable Or Disable Extension Loading
7628
** METHOD: sqlite3
7629
**
7630
** ^So as not to open security holes in older applications that are
7631
** unprepared to deal with [extension loading], and as a means of disabling
7632
** [extension loading] while evaluating user-entered SQL, the following API
7633
** is provided to turn the [sqlite3_load_extension()] mechanism on and off.
7634
**
7635
** ^Extension loading is off by default.
7636
** ^Call the sqlite3_enable_load_extension() routine with onoff==1
7637
** to turn extension loading on and call it with onoff==0 to turn
7638
** it back off again.
7639
**
7640
** ^This interface enables or disables both the C-API
7641
** [sqlite3_load_extension()] and the SQL function [load_extension()].
7642
** ^(Use [sqlite3_db_config](db,[SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION],..)
7643
** to enable or disable only the C-API.)^
7644
**
7645
** <b>Security warning:</b> It is recommended that extension loading
7646
** be enabled using the [SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION] method
7647
** rather than this interface, so the [load_extension()] SQL function
7648
** remains disabled. This will prevent SQL injections from giving attackers
7649
** access to extension loading capabilities.
7650
*/
7651
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_enable_load_extension(sqlite3 *db, int onoff);

7653
/*
7654
** CAPI3REF: Automatically Load Statically Linked Extensions
7655
**
7656
** ^This interface causes the xEntryPoint() function to be invoked for
7657
** each new [database connection] that is created.  The idea here is that
7658
** xEntryPoint() is the entry point for a statically linked [SQLite extension]
7659
** that is to be automatically loaded into all new database connections.
7660
**
7661
** ^(Even though the function prototype shows that xEntryPoint() takes
7662
** no arguments and returns void, SQLite invokes xEntryPoint() with three
7663
** arguments and expects an integer result as if the signature of the
7664
** entry point were as follows:
7665
**
7666
** <blockquote><pre>
7667
** &nbsp;  int xEntryPoint(
7668
** &nbsp;    sqlite3 *db,
7669
** &nbsp;    char **pzErrMsg,
7670
** &nbsp;    const struct sqlite3_api_routines *pThunk
7671
** &nbsp;  );
7672
** </pre></blockquote>)^
7673
**
7674
** If the xEntryPoint routine encounters an error, it should make *pzErrMsg
7675
** point to an appropriate error message (obtained from [sqlite3_mprintf()])
7676
** and return an appropriate [error code].  ^SQLite ensures that *pzErrMsg
7677
** is NULL before calling the xEntryPoint().  ^SQLite will invoke
7678
** [sqlite3_free()] on *pzErrMsg after xEntryPoint() returns.  ^If any
7679
** xEntryPoint() returns an error, the [sqlite3_open()], [sqlite3_open16()],
7680
** or [sqlite3_open_v2()] call that provoked the xEntryPoint() will fail.
7681
**
7682
** ^Calling sqlite3_auto_extension(X) with an entry point X that is already
7683
** on the list of automatic extensions is a harmless no-op. ^No entry point
7684
** will be called more than once for each database connection that is opened.
7685
**
7686
** See also: [sqlite3_reset_auto_extension()]
7687
** and [sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension()]
7688
*/
7689
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_auto_extension(void(*xEntryPoint)(void));
7690
7691
/*
7692
** CAPI3REF: Cancel Automatic Extension Loading
7693
**
7694
** ^The [sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension(X)] interface unregisters the
7695
** initialization routine X that was registered using a prior call to
7696
** [sqlite3_auto_extension(X)].  ^The [sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension(X)]
7697
** routine returns 1 if initialization routine X was successfully
7698
** unregistered and it returns 0 if X was not on the list of initialization
7699
** routines.
7700
*/
7701
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension(void(*xEntryPoint)(void));
