10039
/*
10040
** CAPI3REF: Write-Ahead Log Commit Hook
10041
** METHOD: sqlite3
10042
**
10043
** ^The [sqlite3_wal_hook()] function is used to register a callback that
10044
** is invoked each time data is committed to a database in wal mode.
10045
**
10046
** ^(The callback is invoked by SQLite after the commit has taken place and
10047
** the associated write-lock on the database released)^, so the implementation
10048
** may read, write or [checkpoint] the database as required.
10049
**
10050
** ^The first parameter passed to the callback function when it is invoked
10051
** is a copy of the third parameter passed to sqlite3_wal_hook() when
10052
** registering the callback. ^The second is a copy of the database handle.
10053
** ^The third parameter is the name of the database that was written to -
10054
** either "main" or the name of an [ATTACH]-ed database. ^The fourth parameter
10055
** is the number of pages currently in the write-ahead log file,
10056
** including those that were just committed.
10057
**
10058
** ^The callback function should normally return [SQLITE_OK].  ^If an error
10059
** code is returned, that error will propagate back up through the
10060
** SQLite code base to cause the statement that provoked the callback
10061
** to report an error, though the commit will have still occurred. If the
10062
** callback returns [SQLITE_ROW] or [SQLITE_DONE], or if it returns a value
10063
** that does not correspond to any valid SQLite error code, the results
10064
** are undefined.
10065
**
10066
** ^A single database handle may have at most a single write-ahead log
10067
** callback registered at one time. ^Calling [sqlite3_wal_hook()]
10068
** replaces the default behavior or previously registered write-ahead
10069
** log callback.
10070
**
10071
** ^The return value is a copy of the third parameter from the
10072
** previous call, if any, or 0.
10073
**
10074
** ^The [sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint()] interface and the
10075
** [wal_autocheckpoint pragma] both invoke [sqlite3_wal_hook()] and
10076
** will overwrite any prior [sqlite3_wal_hook()] settings.
10077
**
10078
** ^If a write-ahead log callback is set using this function then
10079
** [sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()] or [PRAGMA wal_checkpoint]
10080
** should be invoked periodically to keep the write-ahead log file
10081
** from growing without bound.
10082
**
10083
** ^Passing a NULL pointer for the callback disables automatic
10084
** checkpointing entirely. To re-enable the default behavior, call
10085
** sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(db,1000) or use [PRAGMA wal_checkpoint].
10086
*/
10087
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_wal_hook(
10088
  sqlite3*,
10089
  int(*)(void *,sqlite3*,const char*,int),
10090
  void*
10091
);
10092
10093
/*
10094
** CAPI3REF: Configure an auto-checkpoint
10095
** METHOD: sqlite3
10096
**
10097
** ^The [sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N)] is a wrapper around
10098
** [sqlite3_wal_hook()] that causes any database on [database connection] D
10099
** to automatically [checkpoint]
10100
** after committing a transaction if there are N or
10101
** more frames in the [write-ahead log] file.  ^Passing zero or
10102
** a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic
10103
** checkpoints entirely.
10104
**
10105
** ^The callback registered by this function replaces any existing callback
10106
** registered using [sqlite3_wal_hook()].  ^Likewise, registering a callback
10107
** using [sqlite3_wal_hook()] disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism
10108
** configured by this function.
10109
**
10110
** ^The [wal_autocheckpoint pragma] can be used to invoke this interface
10111
** from SQL.
10112
**
10113
** ^Checkpoints initiated by this mechanism are
10114
** [sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2|PASSIVE].
10115
**
10116
** ^Every new [database connection] defaults to having the auto-checkpoint
10117
** enabled with a threshold of 1000 or [SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT]
10118
** pages.
10119
**
10120
** ^The use of this interface is only necessary if the default setting
10121
** is found to be suboptimal for a particular application.
10122
*/
10123
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(sqlite3 *db, int N);
10124
10125
/*
10126
** CAPI3REF: Checkpoint a database
10127
** METHOD: sqlite3
10128
**
10129
** ^(The sqlite3_wal_checkpoint(D,X) is equivalent to
10130
** [sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2](D,X,[SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE],0,0).)^
10131
**
10132
** In brief, sqlite3_wal_checkpoint(D,X) causes the content in the
10133
** [write-ahead log] for database X on [database connection] D to be
10134
** transferred into the database file and for the write-ahead log to
10135
** be reset.  See the [checkpointing] documentation for addition
10136
** information.
10137
**
10138
** This interface used to be the only way to cause a checkpoint to
10139
** occur.  But then the newer and more powerful [sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()]
10140
** interface was added.  This interface is retained for backwards
10141
** compatibility and as a convenience for applications that need to manually
10142
** start a callback but which do not need the full power (and corresponding
10143
** complication) of [sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()].
10144
*/
10145
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_wal_checkpoint(sqlite3 *db, const char *zDb);
10146
10147
/*
10148
** CAPI3REF: Checkpoint a database
10149
** METHOD: sqlite3
10150
**
10151
** ^(The sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2(D,X,M,L,C) interface runs a checkpoint
10152
** operation on database X of [database connection] D in mode M.  Status
10153
** information is written back into integers pointed to by L and C.)^
10154
** ^(The M parameter must be a valid [checkpoint mode]:)^
10155
**
10156
** <dl>
10157
** <dt>SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE<dd>
10158
**   ^Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database
10159
**   readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames
10160
**   in the log were checkpointed. ^The [busy-handler callback]
10161
**   is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode.
10162
**   ^On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished
10163
**   if there are concurrent readers or writers.
10164
**
10165
** <dt>SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL<dd>
10166
**   ^This mode blocks (it invokes the
10167
**   [sqlite3_busy_handler|busy-handler callback]) until there is no
10168
**   database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database
10169
**   snapshot. ^It then checkpoints all frames in the log file and syncs the
10170
**   database file. ^This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending,
10171
**   but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.
10172
**
10173
** <dt>SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART<dd>
10174
**   ^This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL with the addition
10175
**   that after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the
10176
**   [busy-handler callback])
10177
**   until all readers are reading from the database file only. ^This ensures
10178
**   that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.
10179
**   ^Like SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, this mode blocks new
10180
**   database writer attempts while it is pending, but does not impede readers.
10181
**
10182
** <dt>SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE<dd>
10183
**   ^This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the
10184
**   addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior
10185
**   to a successful return.
10186
**
10187
** <dt>SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP<dd>
10188
**   ^This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke
10189
**   a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by
10190
**   sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.
10191
** </dl>
10192
**
10193
** ^If pnLog is not NULL, then *pnLog is set to the total number of frames in
10194
** the log file or to -1 if the checkpoint could not run because
10195
** of an error or because the database is not in [WAL mode]. ^If pnCkpt is not
10196
** NULL,then *pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the
10197
** log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function
10198
** was called) or to -1 if the checkpoint could not run due to an error or
10199
** because the database is not in WAL mode. ^Note that upon successful
10200
** completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been
10201
** truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.
10202
**
10203
** ^All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock on the database file. ^If
10204
** any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the
10205
** lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. ^Even if there is a
10206
** busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.
10207
**
10208
** ^The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the
10209
** exclusive "writer" lock on the database file. ^If the writer lock cannot be
10210
** obtained immediately, and a busy-handler is configured, it is invoked and
10211
** the writer lock retried until either the busy-handler returns 0 or the lock
10212
** is successfully obtained. ^The busy-handler is also invoked while waiting for
10213
** database readers as described above. ^If the busy-handler returns 0 before
10214
** the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the
10215
** checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as
10216
** SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE - checkpointing as many frames as possible
10217
** without blocking any further. ^SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.
10218
**
10219
** ^If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the
10220
** specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases [attached] to
10221
** [database connection] db.  In this case the
10222
** values written to output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt are undefined. ^If
10223
** an SQLITE_BUSY error is encountered when processing one or more of the
10224
** attached WAL databases, the operation is still attempted on any remaining
10225
** attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end. ^If any other
10226
** error occurs while processing an attached database, processing is abandoned
10227
** and the error code is returned to the caller immediately. ^If no error
10228
** (SQLITE_BUSY or otherwise) is encountered while processing the attached
10229
** databases, SQLITE_OK is returned.
10230
**
10231
** ^If database zDb is the name of an attached database that is not in WAL
10232
** mode, SQLITE_OK is returned and both *pnLog and *pnCkpt set to -1. ^If
10233
** zDb is not NULL (or a zero length string) and is not the name of any
10234
** attached database, SQLITE_ERROR is returned to the caller.
10235
**
10236
** ^Unless it returns SQLITE_MISUSE,
10237
** the sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() interface
10238
** sets the error information that is queried by
10239
** [sqlite3_errcode()] and [sqlite3_errmsg()].
10240
**
10241
** ^The [PRAGMA wal_checkpoint] command can be used to invoke this interface
10242
** from SQL.
10243
*/
10244
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2(
10245
  sqlite3 *db,                    /* Database handle */
10246
  const char *zDb,                /* Name of attached database (or NULL) */
10247
  int eMode,                      /* SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_* value */
10248
  int *pnLog,                     /* OUT: Size of WAL log in frames */
10249
  int *pnCkpt                     /* OUT: Total number of frames checkpointed */
10250
);
10251
10252
/*
10253
** CAPI3REF: Checkpoint Mode Values
10254
** KEYWORDS: {checkpoint mode}
10255
**
10256
** These constants define all valid values for the "checkpoint mode" passed
10257
** as the third parameter to the [sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()] interface.
10258
** See the [sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()] documentation for details on the
10259
** meaning of each of these checkpoint modes.
10260
*/
10261
#define SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP    -1  /* Do no work at all */
10262
#define SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE  0  /* Do as much as possible w/o blocking */
10263
#define SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL     1  /* Wait for writers, then checkpoint */
10264
#define SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART  2  /* Like FULL but wait for readers */
10265
#define SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE 3  /* Like RESTART but also truncate WAL */
10266
10267
/*
10268
** CAPI3REF: Virtual Table Interface Configuration
10269
**
10270
** This function may be called by either the [xConnect] or [xCreate] method
10271
** of a [virtual table] implementation to configure
10272
** various facets of the virtual table interface.
10273
**
10274
** If this interface is invoked outside the context of an xConnect or
10275
** xCreate virtual table method then the behavior is undefined.
10276
**
10277
** In the call sqlite3_vtab_config(D,C,...) the D parameter is the
10278
** [database connection] in which the virtual table is being created and
10279
** which is passed in as the first argument to the [xConnect] or [xCreate]
10280
** method that is invoking sqlite3_vtab_config().  The C parameter is one
10281
** of the [virtual table configuration options].  The presence and meaning
10282
** of parameters after C depend on which [virtual table configuration option]
10283
** is used.
10284
*/
10285
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_vtab_config(sqlite3*, int op, ...);
10286
10287
/*
10288
** CAPI3REF: Virtual Table Configuration Options
10289
** KEYWORDS: {virtual table configuration options}
10290
** KEYWORDS: {virtual table configuration option}
10291
**
10292
** These macros define the various options to the
10293
** [sqlite3_vtab_config()] interface that [virtual table] implementations
10294
** can use to customize and optimize their behavior.
10295
**
10296
** <dl>
10297
** [[SQLITE_VTAB_CONSTRAINT_SUPPORT]]
10298
** <dt>SQLITE_VTAB_CONSTRAINT_SUPPORT</dt>
10299
** <dd>Calls of the form
10300
** [sqlite3_vtab_config](db,SQLITE_VTAB_CONSTRAINT_SUPPORT,X) are supported,
10301
** where X is an integer.  If X is zero, then the [virtual table] whose
10302
** [xCreate] or [xConnect] method invoked [sqlite3_vtab_config()] does not
10303
** support constraints.  In this configuration (which is the default) if
10304
** a call to the [xUpdate] method returns [SQLITE_CONSTRAINT], then the entire
10305
** statement is rolled back as if [ON CONFLICT | OR ABORT] had been
10306
** specified as part of the user's SQL statement, regardless of the actual
10307
** ON CONFLICT mode specified.
10308
**
10309
** If X is non-zero, then the virtual table implementation guarantees
10310
** that if [xUpdate] returns [SQLITE_CONSTRAINT], it will do so before
10311
** any modifications to internal or persistent data structures have been made.
10312
** If the [ON CONFLICT] mode is ABORT, FAIL, IGNORE or ROLLBACK, SQLite
10313
** is able to roll back a statement or database transaction, and abandon
10314
** or continue processing the current SQL statement as appropriate.
10315
** If the ON CONFLICT mode is REPLACE and the [xUpdate] method returns
10316
** [SQLITE_CONSTRAINT], SQLite handles this as if the ON CONFLICT mode
10317
** had been ABORT.
10318
**
10319
** Virtual table implementations that are required to handle OR REPLACE
10320
** must do so within the [xUpdate] method. If a call to the
10321
** [sqlite3_vtab_on_conflict()] function indicates that the current ON
10322
** CONFLICT policy is REPLACE, the virtual table implementation should
10323
** silently replace the appropriate rows within the xUpdate callback and
10324
** return SQLITE_OK. Or, if this is not possible, it may return
10325
** SQLITE_CONSTRAINT, in which case SQLite falls back to OR ABORT
10326
** constraint handling.
10327
** </dd>
10328
**
10329
** [[SQLITE_VTAB_DIRECTONLY]]<dt>SQLITE_VTAB_DIRECTONLY</dt>
10330
** <dd>Calls of the form
10331
** [sqlite3_vtab_config](db,SQLITE_VTAB_DIRECTONLY) from within the
10332
** the [xConnect] or [xCreate] methods of a [virtual table] implementation
10333
** prohibits that virtual table from being used from within triggers and
10334
** views.
10335
** </dd>
10336
**
10337
** [[SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS]]<dt>SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS</dt>
10338
** <dd>Calls of the form
10339
** [sqlite3_vtab_config](db,SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS) from within the
10340
** [xConnect] or [xCreate] methods of a [virtual table] implementation
10341
** identify that virtual table as being safe to use from within triggers
10342
** and views.  Conceptually, the SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS tag means that the
10343
** virtual table can do no serious harm even if it is controlled by a
10344
** malicious hacker.  Developers should avoid setting the SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS
10345
** flag unless absolutely necessary.
10346
** </dd>
10347
**
10348
** [[SQLITE_VTAB_USES_ALL_SCHEMAS]]<dt>SQLITE_VTAB_USES_ALL_SCHEMAS</dt>
10349
** <dd>Calls of the form
10350
** [sqlite3_vtab_config](db,SQLITE_VTAB_USES_ALL_SCHEMA) from within the
10351
** the [xConnect] or [xCreate] methods of a [virtual table] implementation
10352
** instruct the query planner to begin at least a read transaction on
10353
** all schemas ("main", "temp", and any ATTACH-ed databases) whenever the
10354
** virtual table is used.
10355
** </dd>
10356
** </dl>
10357
*/
10358
#define SQLITE_VTAB_CONSTRAINT_SUPPORT 1
10359
#define SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS          2
10360
#define SQLITE_VTAB_DIRECTONLY         3
10361
#define SQLITE_VTAB_USES_ALL_SCHEMAS   4
10362
10363
/*
10364
** CAPI3REF: Determine The Virtual Table Conflict Policy
10365
**
10366
** This function may only be called from within a call to the [xUpdate] method
10367
** of a [virtual table] implementation for an INSERT or UPDATE operation. ^The
10368
** value returned is one of [SQLITE_ROLLBACK], [SQLITE_IGNORE], [SQLITE_FAIL],
10369
** [SQLITE_ABORT], or [SQLITE_REPLACE], according to the [ON CONFLICT] mode
10370
** of the SQL statement that triggered the call to the [xUpdate] method of the
10371
** [virtual table].
10372
*/
10373
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_vtab_on_conflict(sqlite3 *);
10374
10375
/*
10376
** CAPI3REF: Determine If Virtual Table Column Access Is For UPDATE
10377
**
10378
** If the sqlite3_vtab_nochange(X) routine is called within the [xColumn]
10379
** method of a [virtual table], then it might return true if the
10380
** column is being fetched as part of an UPDATE operation during which the
10381
** column value will not change.  The virtual table implementation can use
10382
** this hint as permission to substitute a return value that is less
10383
** expensive to compute and that the corresponding
10384
** [xUpdate] method understands as a "no-change" value.
10385
**
10386
** If the [xColumn] method calls sqlite3_vtab_nochange() and finds that
10387
** the column is not changed by the UPDATE statement, then the xColumn
10388
** method can optionally return without setting a result, without calling
10389
** any of the [sqlite3_result_int|sqlite3_result_xxxxx() interfaces].
10390
** In that case, [sqlite3_value_nochange(X)] will return true for the
10391
** same column in the [xUpdate] method.
10392
**
10393
** The sqlite3_vtab_nochange() routine is an optimization.  Virtual table
10394
** implementations should continue to give a correct answer even if the
10395
** sqlite3_vtab_nochange() interface were to always return false.  In the
10396
** current implementation, the sqlite3_vtab_nochange() interface does always
10397
** returns false for the enhanced [UPDATE FROM] statement.
10398
*/
10399
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_vtab_nochange(sqlite3_context*);
10400
10401
/*
10402
** CAPI3REF: Determine The Collation For a Virtual Table Constraint
10403
** METHOD: sqlite3_index_info
10404
**
10405
** This function may only be called from within a call to the [xBestIndex]
10406
** method of a [virtual table].  This function returns a pointer to a string
10407
** that is the name of the appropriate collation sequence to use for text
10408
** comparisons on the constraint identified by its arguments.
10409
**
10410
** The first argument must be the pointer to the [sqlite3_index_info] object
10411
** that is the first parameter to the xBestIndex() method. The second argument
10412
** must be an index into the aConstraint[] array belonging to the
10413
** sqlite3_index_info structure passed to xBestIndex.
10414
**
10415
** Important:
10416
** The first parameter must be the same pointer that is passed into the
10417
** xBestMethod() method.  The first parameter may not be a pointer to a
10418
** different [sqlite3_index_info] object, even an exact copy.
10419
**
10420
** The return value is computed as follows:
10421
**
10422
** <ol>
10423
** <li><p> If the constraint comes from a WHERE clause expression that contains
10424
**         a [COLLATE operator], then the name of the collation specified by
10425
**         that COLLATE operator is returned.
10426
** <li><p> If there is no COLLATE operator, but the column that is the subject
10427
**         of the constraint specifies an alternative collating sequence via
10428
**         a [COLLATE clause] on the column definition within the CREATE TABLE
10429
**         statement that was passed into [sqlite3_declare_vtab()], then the
10430
**         name of that alternative collating sequence is returned.
10431
** <li><p> Otherwise, "BINARY" is returned.
10432
** </ol>
10433
*/
10434
SQLITE_API const char *sqlite3_vtab_collation(sqlite3_index_info*,int);
10435
10436
/*
10437
** CAPI3REF: Determine if a virtual table query is DISTINCT
10438
** METHOD: sqlite3_index_info
10439
**
10440
** This API may only be used from within an [xBestIndex|xBestIndex method]
10441
** of a [virtual table] implementation. The result of calling this
10442
** interface from outside of xBestIndex() is undefined and probably harmful.
10443
**
10444
** ^The sqlite3_vtab_distinct() interface returns an integer between 0 and
10445
** 3.  The integer returned by sqlite3_vtab_distinct()
10446
** gives the virtual table additional information about how the query
10447
** planner wants the output to be ordered. As long as the virtual table
10448
** can meet the ordering requirements of the query planner, it may set
10449
** the "orderByConsumed" flag.
10450
**
10451
** <ol><li value="0"><p>
10452
** ^If the sqlite3_vtab_distinct() interface returns 0, that means
10453
** that the query planner needs the virtual table to return all rows in the
10454
** sort order defined by the "nOrderBy" and "aOrderBy" fields of the
10455
** [sqlite3_index_info] object.  This is the default expectation.  If the
10456
** virtual table outputs all rows in sorted order, then it is always safe for
10457
** the xBestIndex method to set the "orderByConsumed" flag, regardless of
10458
** the return value from sqlite3_vtab_distinct().
10459
** <li value="1"><p>
10460
** ^(If the sqlite3_vtab_distinct() interface returns 1, that means
10461
** that the query planner does not need the rows to be returned in sorted order
10462
** as long as all rows with the same values in all columns identified by the
10463
** "aOrderBy" field are adjacent.)^  This mode is used when the query planner
10464
** is doing a GROUP BY.
10465
** <li value="2"><p>
10466
** ^(If the sqlite3_vtab_distinct() interface returns 2, that means
10467
** that the query planner does not need the rows returned in any particular
10468
** order, as long as rows with the same values in all columns identified
10469
** by "aOrderBy" are adjacent.)^  ^(Furthermore, when two or more rows
10470
** contain the same values for all columns identified by "colUsed", all but
10471
** one such row may optionally be omitted from the result.)^
10472
** The virtual table is not required to omit rows that are duplicates
10473
** over the "colUsed" columns, but if the virtual table can do that without
10474
** too much extra effort, it could potentially help the query to run faster.
10475
** This mode is used for a DISTINCT query.
10476
** <li value="3"><p>
10477
** ^(If the sqlite3_vtab_distinct() interface returns 3, that means the
10478
** virtual table must return rows in the order defined by "aOrderBy" as
10479
** if the sqlite3_vtab_distinct() interface had returned 0.  However if
10480
** two or more rows in the result have the same values for all columns
10481
** identified by "colUsed", then all but one such row may optionally be
10482
** omitted.)^  Like when the return value is 2, the virtual table
10483
** is not required to omit rows that are duplicates over the "colUsed"
10484
** columns, but if the virtual table can do that without
10485
** too much extra effort, it could potentially help the query to run faster.
10486
** This mode is used for queries
10487
** that have both DISTINCT and ORDER BY clauses.
10488
** </ol>
10489
**
10490
** <p>The following table summarizes the conditions under which the
10491
** virtual table is allowed to set the "orderByConsumed" flag based on
10492
** the value returned by sqlite3_vtab_distinct().  This table is a
10493
** restatement of the previous four paragraphs:
10494
**
10495
** <table border=1 cellspacing=0 cellpadding=10 width="90%">
10496
** <tr>
10497
** <td valign="top">sqlite3_vtab_distinct() return value
10498
** <td valign="top">Rows are returned in aOrderBy order
10499
** <td valign="top">Rows with the same value in all aOrderBy columns are
10500
**                  adjacent
10501
** <td valign="top">Duplicates over all colUsed columns may be omitted
10502
** <tr><td>0<td>yes<td>yes<td>no
10503
** <tr><td>1<td>no<td>yes<td>no
10504
** <tr><td>2<td>no<td>yes<td>yes
10505
** <tr><td>3<td>yes<td>yes<td>yes
10506
** </table>
10507
**
10508
** ^For the purposes of comparing virtual table output values to see if the
10509
** values are the same value for sorting purposes, two NULL values are
10510
** considered to be the same.  In other words, the comparison operator is "IS"
10511
** (or "IS NOT DISTINCT FROM") and not "==".
10512
**
10513
** If a virtual table implementation is unable to meet the requirements
10514
** specified above, then it must not set the "orderByConsumed" flag in the
10515
** [sqlite3_index_info] object or an incorrect answer may result.
10516
**
10517
** ^A virtual table implementation is always free to return rows in any order
10518
** it wants, as long as the "orderByConsumed" flag is not set.  ^When the
10519
** "orderByConsumed" flag is unset, the query planner will add extra
10520
** [bytecode] to ensure that the final results returned by the SQL query are
10521
** ordered correctly.  The use of the "orderByConsumed" flag and the
10522
** sqlite3_vtab_distinct() interface is merely an optimization.  ^Careful
10523
** use of the sqlite3_vtab_distinct() interface and the "orderByConsumed"
10524
** flag might help queries against a virtual table to run faster.  Being
10525
** overly aggressive and setting the "orderByConsumed" flag when it is not
10526
** valid to do so, on the other hand, might cause SQLite to return incorrect
10527
** results.
10528
*/
10529
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_vtab_distinct(sqlite3_index_info*);
10530
10531
/*
10532
** CAPI3REF: Identify and handle IN constraints in xBestIndex
10533
**
10534
** This interface may only be used from within an
10535
** [xBestIndex|xBestIndex() method] of a [virtual table] implementation.
10536
** The result of invoking this interface from any other context is
10537
** undefined and probably harmful.
10538
**
10539
** ^(A constraint on a virtual table of the form
10540
** "[IN operator|column IN (...)]" is
10541
** communicated to the xBestIndex method as a
10542
** [SQLITE_INDEX_CONSTRAINT_EQ] constraint.)^  If xBestIndex wants to use
10543
** this constraint, it must set the corresponding
10544
** aConstraintUsage[].argvIndex to a positive integer.  ^(Then, under
10545
** the usual mode of handling IN operators, SQLite generates [bytecode]
10546
** that invokes the [xFilter|xFilter() method] once for each value
10547
** on the right-hand side of the IN operator.)^  Thus the virtual table
10548
** only sees a single value from the right-hand side of the IN operator
10549
** at a time.
10550
**
10551
** In some cases, however, it would be advantageous for the virtual
10552
** table to see all values on the right-hand of the IN operator all at
10553
** once.  The sqlite3_vtab_in() interfaces facilitates this in two ways:
10554
**
10555
** <ol>
10556
** <li><p>
10557
**   ^A call to sqlite3_vtab_in(P,N,-1) will return true (non-zero)
10558
**   if and only if the [sqlite3_index_info|P->aConstraint][N] constraint
10559
**   is an [IN operator] that can be processed all at once.  ^In other words,
10560
**   sqlite3_vtab_in() with -1 in the third argument is a mechanism
10561
**   by which the virtual table can ask SQLite if all-at-once processing
10562
**   of the IN operator is even possible.
10563
**
10564
** <li><p>
10565
**   ^A call to sqlite3_vtab_in(P,N,F) with F==1 or F==0 indicates
10566
**   to SQLite that the virtual table does or does not want to process
10567
**   the IN operator all-at-once, respectively.  ^Thus when the third
10568
**   parameter (F) is non-negative, this interface is the mechanism by
10569
**   which the virtual table tells SQLite how it wants to process the
10570
**   IN operator.
10571
** </ol>
10572
**
10573
** ^The sqlite3_vtab_in(P,N,F) interface can be invoked multiple times
10574
** within the same xBestIndex method call.  ^For any given P,N pair,
10575
** the return value from sqlite3_vtab_in(P,N,F) will always be the same
10576
** within the same xBestIndex call.  ^If the interface returns true
10577
** (non-zero), that means that the constraint is an IN operator
10578
** that can be processed all-at-once.  ^If the constraint is not an IN
10579
** operator or cannot be processed all-at-once, then the interface returns
10580
** false.
10581
**
10582
** ^(All-at-once processing of the IN operator is selected if both of the
10583
** following conditions are met:
10584
**
10585
** <ol>
10586
** <li><p> The P->aConstraintUsage[N].argvIndex value is set to a positive
10587
** integer.  This is how the virtual table tells SQLite that it wants to
10588
** use the N-th constraint.
10589
**
10590
** <li><p> The last call to sqlite3_vtab_in(P,N,F) for which F was
10591
** non-negative had F>=1.
10592
** </ol>)^
10593
**
10594
** ^If either or both of the conditions above are false, then SQLite uses
10595
** the traditional one-at-a-time processing strategy for the IN constraint.
10596
** ^If both conditions are true, then the argvIndex-th parameter to the
10597
** xFilter method will be an [sqlite3_value] that appears to be NULL,
10598
** but which can be passed to [sqlite3_vtab_in_first()] and
10599
** [sqlite3_vtab_in_next()] to find all values on the right-hand side
10600
** of the IN constraint.
10601
*/
10602
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_vtab_in(sqlite3_index_info*, int iCons, int bHandle);
10603
10604
/*
10605
** CAPI3REF: Find all elements on the right-hand side of an IN constraint.
10606
**
10607
** These interfaces are only useful from within the
10608
** [xFilter|xFilter() method] of a [virtual table] implementation.
10609
** The result of invoking these interfaces from any other context
10610
** is undefined and probably harmful.
10611
**
10612
** The X parameter in a call to sqlite3_vtab_in_first(X,P) or
10613
** sqlite3_vtab_in_next(X,P) should be one of the parameters to the
10614
** xFilter method which invokes these routines, and specifically
10615
** a parameter that was previously selected for all-at-once IN constraint
10616
** processing using the [sqlite3_vtab_in()] interface in the
10617
** [xBestIndex|xBestIndex method].  ^(If the X parameter is not
10618
** an xFilter argument that was selected for all-at-once IN constraint
10619
** processing, then these routines return [SQLITE_ERROR].)^
10620
**
10621
** ^(Use these routines to access all values on the right-hand side
10622
** of the IN constraint using code like the following:
10623
**
10624
** <blockquote><pre>
10625
** &nbsp;  for(rc=sqlite3_vtab_in_first(pList, &pVal);
10626
** &nbsp;      rc==SQLITE_OK && pVal;
10627
** &nbsp;      rc=sqlite3_vtab_in_next(pList, &pVal)
10628
** &nbsp;  ){
10629
** &nbsp;    // do something with pVal
10630
** &nbsp;  }
10631
** &nbsp;  if( rc!=SQLITE_DONE ){
10632
** &nbsp;    // an error has occurred
10633
** &nbsp;  }
10634
** </pre></blockquote>)^
10635
**
10636
** ^On success, the sqlite3_vtab_in_first(X,P) and sqlite3_vtab_in_next(X,P)
10637
** routines return SQLITE_OK and set *P to point to the first or next value
10638
** on the RHS of the IN constraint.  ^If there are no more values on the
10639
** right hand side of the IN constraint, then *P is set to NULL and these
10640
** routines return [SQLITE_DONE].  ^The return value might be
10641
** some other value, such as SQLITE_NOMEM, in the event of a malfunction.
10642
**
10643
** The *ppOut values returned by these routines are only valid until the
10644
** next call to either of these routines or until the end of the xFilter
10645
** method from which these routines were called.  If the virtual table
10646
** implementation needs to retain the *ppOut values for longer, it must make
10647
** copies.  The *ppOut values are [protected sqlite3_value|protected].
10648
*/
10649
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_vtab_in_first(sqlite3_value *pVal, sqlite3_value **ppOut);
10650
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_vtab_in_next(sqlite3_value *pVal, sqlite3_value **ppOut);
10651
10652
/*
10653
** CAPI3REF: Constraint values in xBestIndex()
10654
** METHOD: sqlite3_index_info
10655
**
10656
** This API may only be used from within the [xBestIndex|xBestIndex method]
10657
** of a [virtual table] implementation. The result of calling this interface
10658
** from outside of an xBestIndex method are undefined and probably harmful.
10659
**
10660
** ^When the sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value(P,J,V) interface is invoked from within
10661
** the [xBestIndex] method of a [virtual table] implementation, with P being
10662
** a copy of the [sqlite3_index_info] object pointer passed into xBestIndex and
10663
** J being a 0-based index into P->aConstraint[], then this routine
10664
** attempts to set *V to the value of the right-hand operand of
10665
** that constraint if the right-hand operand is known.  ^If the
10666
** right-hand operand is not known, then *V is set to a NULL pointer.
10667
** ^The sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value(P,J,V) interface returns SQLITE_OK if
10668
** and only if *V is set to a value.  ^The sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value(P,J,V)
10669
** inteface returns SQLITE_NOTFOUND if the right-hand side of the J-th
10670
** constraint is not available.  ^The sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value() interface
10671
** can return a result code other than SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_NOTFOUND if
10672
** something goes wrong.
10673
**
10674
** The sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value() interface is usually only successful if
10675
** the right-hand operand of a constraint is a literal value in the original
10676
** SQL statement.  If the right-hand operand is an expression or a reference
10677
** to some other column or a [host parameter], then sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value()
10678
** will probably return [SQLITE_NOTFOUND].
10679
**
10680
** ^(Some constraints, such as [SQLITE_INDEX_CONSTRAINT_ISNULL] and
10681
** [SQLITE_INDEX_CONSTRAINT_ISNOTNULL], have no right-hand operand.  For such
10682
** constraints, sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value() always returns SQLITE_NOTFOUND.)^
10683
**
10684
** ^The [sqlite3_value] object returned in *V is a protected sqlite3_value
10685
** and remains valid for the duration of the xBestIndex method call.
10686
** ^When xBestIndex returns, the sqlite3_value object returned by
10687
** sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value() is automatically deallocated.
10688
**
10689
** The "_rhs_" in the name of this routine is an abbreviation for
10690
** "Right-Hand Side".
10691
*/
10692
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_vtab_rhs_value(sqlite3_index_info*, int, sqlite3_value **ppVal);
10693
10694
/*
10695
** CAPI3REF: Conflict resolution modes
10696
** KEYWORDS: {conflict resolution mode}
10697
**
10698
** These constants are returned by [sqlite3_vtab_on_conflict()] to
10699
** inform a [virtual table] implementation of the [ON CONFLICT] mode
10700
** for the SQL statement being evaluated.
10701
**
10702
** Note that the [SQLITE_IGNORE] constant is also used as a potential
10703
** return value from the [sqlite3_set_authorizer()] callback and that
10704
** [SQLITE_ABORT] is also a [result code].
10705
*/
10706
#define SQLITE_ROLLBACK 1
10707
/* #define SQLITE_IGNORE 2 // Also used by sqlite3_authorizer() callback */
10708
#define SQLITE_FAIL     3
10709
/* #define SQLITE_ABORT 4  // Also an error code */
10710
#define SQLITE_REPLACE  5
10711
10712
/*
10713
** CAPI3REF: Prepared Statement Scan Status Opcodes
10714
** KEYWORDS: {scanstatus options}
10715
**
10716
** The following constants can be used for the T parameter to the
10717
** [sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus(S,X,T,V)] interface.  Each constant designates a
10718
** different metric for sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus() to return.
10719
**
10720
** When the value returned to V is a string, space to hold that string is
10721
** managed by the prepared statement S and will be automatically freed when
10722
** S is finalized.
10723
**
10724
** Not all values are available for all query elements. When a value is
10725
** not available, the output variable is set to -1 if the value is numeric,
10726
** or to NULL if it is a string (SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NAME).
10727
**
10728
** <dl>
10729
** [[SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NLOOP]] <dt>SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NLOOP</dt>
10730
** <dd>^The [sqlite3_int64] variable pointed to by the V parameter will be
10731
** set to the total number of times that the X-th loop has run.</dd>
10732
**
10733
** [[SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NVISIT]] <dt>SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NVISIT</dt>
10734
** <dd>^The [sqlite3_int64] variable pointed to by the V parameter will be set
10735
** to the total number of rows examined by all iterations of the X-th loop.</dd>
10736
**
10737
** [[SQLITE_SCANSTAT_EST]] <dt>SQLITE_SCANSTAT_EST</dt>
10738
** <dd>^The "double" variable pointed to by the V parameter will be set to the
10739
** query planner's estimate for the average number of rows output from each
10740
** iteration of the X-th loop.  If the query planner's estimate was accurate,
10741
** then this value will approximate the quotient NVISIT/NLOOP and the
10742
** product of this value for all prior loops with the same SELECTID will
10743
** be the NLOOP value for the current loop.</dd>
10744
**
10745
** [[SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NAME]] <dt>SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NAME</dt>
10746
** <dd>^The "const char *" variable pointed to by the V parameter will be set
10747
** to a zero-terminated UTF-8 string containing the name of the index or table
10748
** used for the X-th loop.</dd>
10749
**
10750
** [[SQLITE_SCANSTAT_EXPLAIN]] <dt>SQLITE_SCANSTAT_EXPLAIN</dt>
10751
** <dd>^The "const char *" variable pointed to by the V parameter will be set
10752
** to a zero-terminated UTF-8 string containing the [EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN]
10753
** description for the X-th loop.</dd>
10754
**
10755
** [[SQLITE_SCANSTAT_SELECTID]] <dt>SQLITE_SCANSTAT_SELECTID</dt>
10756
** <dd>^The "int" variable pointed to by the V parameter will be set to the
10757
** id for the X-th query plan element. The id value is unique within the
10758
** statement. The select-id is the same value as is output in the first
10759
** column of an [EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN] query.</dd>
10760
**
10761
** [[SQLITE_SCANSTAT_PARENTID]] <dt>SQLITE_SCANSTAT_PARENTID</dt>
10762
** <dd>The "int" variable pointed to by the V parameter will be set to the
10763
** id of the parent of the current query element, if applicable, or
10764
** to zero if the query element has no parent. This is the same value as
10765
** returned in the second column of an [EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN] query.</dd>
10766
**
10767
** [[SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NCYCLE]] <dt>SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NCYCLE</dt>
10768
** <dd>The sqlite3_int64 output value is set to the number of cycles,
10769
** according to the processor time-stamp counter, that elapsed while the
10770
** query element was being processed. This value is not available for
10771
** all query elements - if it is unavailable the output variable is
10772
** set to -1.</dd>
10773
** </dl>
10774
*/
10775
#define SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NLOOP    0
10776
#define SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NVISIT   1
10777
#define SQLITE_SCANSTAT_EST      2
10778
#define SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NAME     3
10779
#define SQLITE_SCANSTAT_EXPLAIN  4
10780
#define SQLITE_SCANSTAT_SELECTID 5
10781
#define SQLITE_SCANSTAT_PARENTID 6
10782
#define SQLITE_SCANSTAT_NCYCLE   7

/*
10785
** CAPI3REF: Prepared Statement Scan Status
10786
** METHOD: sqlite3_stmt
10787
**
10788
** These interfaces return information about the predicted and measured
10789
** performance for pStmt.  Advanced applications can use this
10790
** interface to compare the predicted and the measured performance and
10791
** issue warnings and/or rerun [ANALYZE] if discrepancies are found.
10792
**
10793
** Since this interface is expected to be rarely used, it is only
10794
** available if SQLite is compiled using the [SQLITE_ENABLE_STMT_SCANSTATUS]
10795
** compile-time option.
10796
**
10797
** The "iScanStatusOp" parameter determines which status information to return.
10798
** The "iScanStatusOp" must be one of the [scanstatus options] or the behavior
10799
** of this interface is undefined. ^The requested measurement is written into
10800
** a variable pointed to by the "pOut" parameter.
10801
**
10802
** The "flags" parameter must be passed a mask of flags. At present only
10803
** one flag is defined - [SQLITE_SCANSTAT_COMPLEX]. If SQLITE_SCANSTAT_COMPLEX
10804
** is specified, then status information is available for all elements
10805
** of a query plan that are reported by "[EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN]" output. If
10806
** SQLITE_SCANSTAT_COMPLEX is not specified, then only query plan elements
10807
** that correspond to query loops (the "SCAN..." and "SEARCH..." elements of
10808
** the EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output) are available. Invoking API
10809
** sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus() is equivalent to calling
10810
** sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus_v2() with a zeroed flags parameter.
10811
**
10812
** Parameter "idx" identifies the specific query element to retrieve statistics
10813
** for. Query elements are numbered starting from zero. A value of -1 may
10814
** retrieve statistics for the entire query. ^If idx is out of range
10815
** - less than -1 or greater than or equal to the total number of query
10816
** elements used to implement the statement - a non-zero value is returned and
10817
** the variable that pOut points to is unchanged.
10818
**
10819
** See also: [sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus_reset()] and the
10820
** [nexec and ncycle] columns of the [bytecode virtual table].
10821
*/
10822
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus(
10823
  sqlite3_stmt *pStmt,      /* Prepared statement for which info desired */
10824
  int idx,                  /* Index of loop to report on */
10825
  int iScanStatusOp,        /* Information desired.  SQLITE_SCANSTAT_* */
10826
  void *pOut                /* Result written here */
10827
);
10828
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus_v2(
10829
  sqlite3_stmt *pStmt,      /* Prepared statement for which info desired */
10830
  int idx,                  /* Index of loop to report on */
10831
  int iScanStatusOp,        /* Information desired.  SQLITE_SCANSTAT_* */
10832
  int flags,                /* Mask of flags defined below */
10833
  void *pOut                /* Result written here */
10834
);
10835
10836

10837

10838
** KEYWORDS: {scan status flags}
10839

10840

10843

/*
10854
** CAPI3REF: Flush caches to disk mid-transaction
10855
** METHOD: sqlite3
10856
**
10857
** ^If a write-transaction is open on [database connection] D when the
10858
** [sqlite3_db_cacheflush(D)] interface is invoked, any dirty
10859
** pages in the pager-cache that are not currently in use are written out
10860
** to disk. A dirty page may be in use if a database cursor created by an
10861
** active SQL statement is reading from it, or if it is page 1 of a database
10862
** file (page 1 is always "in use").  ^The [sqlite3_db_cacheflush(D)]
10863
** interface flushes caches for all schemas - "main", "temp", and
10864
** any [attached] databases.
10865
**
10866
** ^If this function needs to obtain extra database locks before dirty pages
10867
** can be flushed to disk, it does so. ^If those locks cannot be obtained
10868
** immediately and there is a busy-handler callback configured, it is invoked
10869
** in the usual manner. ^If the required lock still cannot be obtained, then
10870
** the database is skipped and an attempt made to flush any dirty pages
10871
** belonging to the next (if any) database. ^If any databases are skipped
10872
** because locks cannot be obtained, but no other error occurs, this
10873
** function returns SQLITE_BUSY.
10874
**
10875
** ^If any other error occurs while flushing dirty pages to disk (for
10876
** example an IO error or out-of-memory condition), then processing is
10877
** abandoned and an SQLite [error code] is returned to the caller immediately.
10878
**
10879
** ^Otherwise, if no error occurs, [sqlite3_db_cacheflush()] returns SQLITE_OK.
10880
**
10881
** ^This function does not set the database handle error code or message
10882
** returned by the [sqlite3_errcode()] and [sqlite3_errmsg()] functions.
10883
*/
10884
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_db_cacheflush(sqlite3*);
10885
10886
/*
10887
** CAPI3REF: The pre-update hook.
10888
** METHOD: sqlite3
10889
**
10890
** ^These interfaces are only available if SQLite is compiled using the
10891
** [SQLITE_ENABLE_PREUPDATE_HOOK] compile-time option.
10892
**
10893
** ^The [sqlite3_preupdate_hook()] interface registers a callback function
10894
** that is invoked prior to each [INSERT], [UPDATE], and [DELETE] operation
10895
** on a database table.
10896
** ^At most one preupdate hook may be registered at a time on a single
10897
** [database connection]; each call to [sqlite3_preupdate_hook()] overrides
10898
** the previous setting.
10899
** ^The preupdate hook is disabled by invoking [sqlite3_preupdate_hook()]
10900
** with a NULL pointer as the second parameter.
10901
** ^The third parameter to [sqlite3_preupdate_hook()] is passed through as
10902
** the first parameter to callbacks.
10903
**
10904
** ^The preupdate hook only fires for changes to real database tables; the
10905
** preupdate hook is not invoked for changes to [virtual tables] or to
10906
** system tables like sqlite_sequence or sqlite_stat1.
10907
**
10908
** ^The second parameter to the preupdate callback is a pointer to
10909
** the [database connection] that registered the preupdate hook.
10910
** ^The third parameter to the preupdate callback is one of the constants
10911
** [SQLITE_INSERT], [SQLITE_DELETE], or [SQLITE_UPDATE] to identify the
10912
** kind of update operation that is about to occur.
10913
** ^(The fourth parameter to the preupdate callback is the name of the
10914
** database within the database connection that is being modified.  This
10915
** will be "main" for the main database or "temp" for TEMP tables or
10916
** the name given after the AS keyword in the [ATTACH] statement for attached
10917
** databases.)^
10918
** ^The fifth parameter to the preupdate callback is the name of the
10919
** table that is being modified.
10920
**
10921
** For an UPDATE or DELETE operation on a [rowid table], the sixth
10922
** parameter passed to the preupdate callback is the initial [rowid] of the
10923
** row being modified or deleted. For an INSERT operation on a rowid table,
10924
** or any operation on a WITHOUT ROWID table, the value of the sixth
10925
** parameter is undefined. For an INSERT or UPDATE on a rowid table the
10926
** seventh parameter is the final rowid value of the row being inserted
10927
** or updated. The value of the seventh parameter passed to the callback
10928
** function is not defined for operations on WITHOUT ROWID tables, or for
10929
** DELETE operations on rowid tables.
10930
**
10931
** ^The sqlite3_preupdate_hook(D,C,P) function returns the P argument from
10932
** the previous call on the same [database connection] D, or NULL for
10933
** the first call on D.
10934
**
10935
** The [sqlite3_preupdate_old()], [sqlite3_preupdate_new()],
10936
** [sqlite3_preupdate_count()], and [sqlite3_preupdate_depth()] interfaces
10937
** provide additional information about a preupdate event. These routines
10938
** may only be called from within a preupdate callback.  Invoking any of
10939
** these routines from outside of a preupdate callback or with a
10940
** [database connection] pointer that is different from the one supplied
10941
** to the preupdate callback results in undefined and probably undesirable
10942
** behavior.
10943
**
10944
** ^The [sqlite3_preupdate_count(D)] interface returns the number of columns
10945
** in the row that is being inserted, updated, or deleted.
10946
**
10947
** ^The [sqlite3_preupdate_old(D,N,P)] interface writes into P a pointer to
10948
** a [protected sqlite3_value] that contains the value of the Nth column of
10949
** the table row before it is updated.  The N parameter must be between 0
10950
** and one less than the number of columns or the behavior will be
10951
** undefined. This must only be used within SQLITE_UPDATE and SQLITE_DELETE
10952
** preupdate callbacks; if it is used by an SQLITE_INSERT callback then the
10953
** behavior is undefined.  The [sqlite3_value] that P points to
10954
** will be destroyed when the preupdate callback returns.
10955
**
10956
** ^The [sqlite3_preupdate_new(D,N,P)] interface writes into P a pointer to
10957
** a [protected sqlite3_value] that contains the value of the Nth column of
10958
** the table row after it is updated.  The N parameter must be between 0
10959
** and one less than the number of columns or the behavior will be
10960
** undefined. This must only be used within SQLITE_INSERT and SQLITE_UPDATE
10961
** preupdate callbacks; if it is used by an SQLITE_DELETE callback then the
10962
** behavior is undefined.  The [sqlite3_value] that P points to
10963
** will be destroyed when the preupdate callback returns.
10964
**
10965
** ^The [sqlite3_preupdate_depth(D)] interface returns 0 if the preupdate
10966
** callback was invoked as a result of a direct insert, update, or delete
10967
** operation; or 1 for inserts, updates, or deletes invoked by top-level
10968
** triggers; or 2 for changes resulting from triggers called by top-level
10969
** triggers; and so forth.
10970
**
10971
** When the [sqlite3_blob_write()] API is used to update a blob column,
10972
** the pre-update hook is invoked with SQLITE_DELETE, because
10973
** the new values are not yet available. In this case, when a
10974
** callback made with op==SQLITE_DELETE is actually a write using the
10975
** sqlite3_blob_write() API, the [sqlite3_preupdate_blobwrite()] returns
10976
** the index of the column being written. In other cases, where the
10977
** pre-update hook is being invoked for some other reason, including a
10978
** regular DELETE, sqlite3_preupdate_blobwrite() returns -1.
10979
**
10980
** See also:  [sqlite3_update_hook()]
10981
*/
10982
#if defined(SQLITE_ENABLE_PREUPDATE_HOOK)
10983
SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_preupdate_hook(
10984
  sqlite3 *db,
10985
  void(*xPreUpdate)(
10986
    void *pCtx,                   /* Copy of third arg to preupdate_hook() */
10987
    sqlite3 *db,                  /* Database handle */
10988
    int op,                       /* SQLITE_UPDATE, DELETE or INSERT */
10989
    char const *zDb,              /* Database name */
10990
    char const *zName,            /* Table name */
10991
    sqlite3_int64 iKey1,          /* Rowid of row about to be deleted/updated */
10992
    sqlite3_int64 iKey2           /* New rowid value (for a rowid UPDATE) */
10993
  ),
10994
  void*
10995
);
10996
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_preupdate_old(sqlite3 *, int, sqlite3_value **);
10997
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_preupdate_count(sqlite3 *);
10998
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_preupdate_depth(sqlite3 *);
10999
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_preupdate_new(sqlite3 *, int, sqlite3_value **);
11000
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_preupdate_blobwrite(sqlite3 *);
11001
#endif

** called to get back the underlying "errno" that caused the problem, such

*/
11014

/*
11017
** CAPI3REF: Database Snapshot
11018
** KEYWORDS: {snapshot} {sqlite3_snapshot}
11019
**
11020
** An instance of the snapshot object records the state of a [WAL mode]
11021
** database for some specific point in history.
11022
**
11023
** In [WAL mode], multiple [database connections] that are open on the
11024
** same database file can each be reading a different historical version
11025
** of the database file.  When a [database connection] begins a read
11026
** transaction, that connection sees an unchanging copy of the database
11027
** as it existed for the point in time when the transaction first started.
11028
** Subsequent changes to the database from other connections are not seen
11029
** by the reader until a new read transaction is started.
11030
**
11031
** The sqlite3_snapshot object records state information about an historical
11032
** version of the database file so that it is possible to later open a new read
11033
** transaction that sees that historical version of the database rather than
11034
** the most recent version.
11035
*/
11036
typedef struct sqlite3_snapshot {
11037
  unsigned char hidden[48];
11038
} sqlite3_snapshot;
11039
11040
/*
11041
** CAPI3REF: Record A Database Snapshot
11042
** CONSTRUCTOR: sqlite3_snapshot
11043
**
11044
** ^The [sqlite3_snapshot_get(D,S,P)] interface attempts to make a
11045
** new [sqlite3_snapshot] object that records the current state of
11046
** schema S in database connection D.  ^On success, the
11047
** [sqlite3_snapshot_get(D,S,P)] interface writes a pointer to the newly
11048
** created [sqlite3_snapshot] object into *P and returns SQLITE_OK.
11049
** If there is not already a read-transaction open on schema S when
11050
** this function is called, one is opened automatically.
11051
**
11052
** If a read-transaction is opened by this function, then it is guaranteed
11053
** that the returned snapshot object may not be invalidated by a database
11054
** writer or checkpointer until after the read-transaction is closed. This
11055
** is not guaranteed if a read-transaction is already open when this
11056
** function is called. In that case, any subsequent write or checkpoint
11057
** operation on the database may invalidate the returned snapshot handle,
11058
** even while the read-transaction remains open.
11059
**
11060
** The following must be true for this function to succeed. If any of
11061
** the following statements are false when sqlite3_snapshot_get() is
11062
** called, SQLITE_ERROR is returned. The final value of *P is undefined
11063
** in this case.
11064
**
11065
** <ul>
11066
**   <li> The database handle must not be in [autocommit mode].
11067
**
11068
**   <li> Schema S of [database connection] D must be a [WAL mode] database.
11069
**
11070
**   <li> There must not be a write transaction open on schema S of database
11071
**        connection D.
11072
**
11073
**   <li> One or more transactions must have been written to the current wal
11074
**        file since it was created on disk (by any connection). This means
11075
**        that a snapshot cannot be taken on a wal mode database with no wal
11076
**        file immediately after it is first opened. At least one transaction
11077
**        must be written to it first.
11078
** </ul>
11079
**
11080
** This function may also return SQLITE_NOMEM.  If it is called with the
11081
** database handle in autocommit mode but fails for some other reason,
11082
** whether or not a read transaction is opened on schema S is undefined.
11083
**
11084
** The [sqlite3_snapshot] object returned from a successful call to
11085
** [sqlite3_snapshot_get()] must be freed using [sqlite3_snapshot_free()]
11086
** to avoid a memory leak.
11087
**
11088
** The [sqlite3_snapshot_get()] interface is only available when the
11089
** [SQLITE_ENABLE_SNAPSHOT] compile-time option is used.
11090
*/
11091
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_snapshot_get(
11092
  sqlite3 *db,
11093
  const char *zSchema,
11094
  sqlite3_snapshot **ppSnapshot
11095
);
11096
11097
/*
11098
** CAPI3REF: Start a read transaction on an historical snapshot
11099
** METHOD: sqlite3_snapshot
11100
**
11101
** ^The [sqlite3_snapshot_open(D,S,P)] interface either starts a new read
11102
** transaction or upgrades an existing one for schema S of
11103
** [database connection] D such that the read transaction refers to
11104
** historical [snapshot] P, rather than the most recent change to the
11105
** database. ^The [sqlite3_snapshot_open()] interface returns SQLITE_OK
11106
** on success or an appropriate [error code] if it fails.
11107
**
11108
** ^In order to succeed, the database connection must not be in
11109
** [autocommit mode] when [sqlite3_snapshot_open(D,S,P)] is called. If there
11110
** is already a read transaction open on schema S, then the database handle
11111
** must have no active statements (SELECT statements that have been passed
11112
** to sqlite3_step() but not sqlite3_reset() or sqlite3_finalize()).
11113
** SQLITE_ERROR is returned if either of these conditions is violated, or
11114
** if schema S does not exist, or if the snapshot object is invalid.
11115
**
11116
** ^A call to sqlite3_snapshot_open() will fail to open if the specified
11117
** snapshot has been overwritten by a [checkpoint]. In this case
11118
** SQLITE_ERROR_SNAPSHOT is returned.
11119
**
11120
** If there is already a read transaction open when this function is
11121
** invoked, then the same read transaction remains open (on the same
11122
** database snapshot) if SQLITE_ERROR, SQLITE_BUSY or SQLITE_ERROR_SNAPSHOT
11123
** is returned. If another error code - for example SQLITE_PROTOCOL or an
11124
** SQLITE_IOERR error code - is returned, then the final state of the
11125
** read transaction is undefined. If SQLITE_OK is returned, then the
11126
** read transaction is now open on database snapshot P.
11127
**
11128
** ^(A call to [sqlite3_snapshot_open(D,S,P)] will fail if the
11129
** database connection D does not know that the database file for
11130
** schema S is in [WAL mode].  A database connection might not know
11131
** that the database file is in [WAL mode] if there has been no prior
11132
** I/O on that database connection, or if the database entered [WAL mode]
11133
** after the most recent I/O on the database connection.)^
11134
** (Hint: Run "[PRAGMA application_id]" against a newly opened
11135
** database connection in order to make it ready to use snapshots.)
11136
**
11137
** The [sqlite3_snapshot_open()] interface is only available when the
11138
** [SQLITE_ENABLE_SNAPSHOT] compile-time option is used.
11139
*/
11140
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_snapshot_open(
11141
  sqlite3 *db,
11142
  const char *zSchema,
11143
  sqlite3_snapshot *pSnapshot
11144
);
11145
11146
/*
11147
** CAPI3REF: Destroy a snapshot
11148
** DESTRUCTOR: sqlite3_snapshot
11149
**
11150
** ^The [sqlite3_snapshot_free(P)] interface destroys [sqlite3_snapshot] P.
11151
** The application must eventually free every [sqlite3_snapshot] object
11152
** using this routine to avoid a memory leak.
11153
**
11154
** The [sqlite3_snapshot_free()] interface is only available when the
11155
** [SQLITE_ENABLE_SNAPSHOT] compile-time option is used.
11156
*/
11157
SQLITE_API void sqlite3_snapshot_free(sqlite3_snapshot*);
11158
11159
/*
11160
** CAPI3REF: Compare the ages of two snapshot handles.
11161
** METHOD: sqlite3_snapshot
11162
**
11163
** The sqlite3_snapshot_cmp(P1, P2) interface is used to compare the ages
11164
** of two valid snapshot handles.
11165
**
11166
** If the two snapshot handles are not associated with the same database
11167
** file, the result of the comparison is undefined.
11168
**
11169
** Additionally, the result of the comparison is only valid if both of the
11170
** snapshot handles were obtained by calling sqlite3_snapshot_get() since the
11171
** last time the wal file was deleted. The wal file is deleted when the
11172
** database is changed back to rollback mode or when the number of database
11173
** clients drops to zero. If either snapshot handle was obtained before the
11174
** wal file was last deleted, the value returned by this function
11175
** is undefined.
11176
**
11177
** Otherwise, this API returns a negative value if P1 refers to an older
11178
** snapshot than P2, zero if the two handles refer to the same database
11179
** snapshot, and a positive value if P1 is a newer snapshot than P2.
11180
**
11181
** This interface is only available if SQLite is compiled with the
11182
** [SQLITE_ENABLE_SNAPSHOT] option.
11183
*/
11184
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_snapshot_cmp(
11185
  sqlite3_snapshot *p1,
11186
  sqlite3_snapshot *p2
11187
);
11188
11189
/*
11190
** CAPI3REF: Recover snapshots from a wal file
11191
** METHOD: sqlite3_snapshot
11192
**
11193
** If a [WAL file] remains on disk after all database connections close
11194
** (either through the use of the [SQLITE_FCNTL_PERSIST_WAL] [file control]
11195
** or because the last process to have the database opened exited without
11196
** calling [sqlite3_close()]) and a new connection is subsequently opened
11197
** on that database and [WAL file], the [sqlite3_snapshot_open()] interface
11198
** will only be able to open the last transaction added to the WAL file
11199
** even though the WAL file contains other valid transactions.
11200
**
11201
** This function attempts to scan the WAL file associated with database zDb
11202
** of database handle db and make all valid snapshots available to
11203
** sqlite3_snapshot_open(). It is an error if there is already a read
11204
** transaction open on the database, or if the database is not a WAL mode
11205
** database.
11206
**
11207
** SQLITE_OK is returned if successful, or an SQLite error code otherwise.
11208
**
11209
** This interface is only available if SQLite is compiled with the
11210
** [SQLITE_ENABLE_SNAPSHOT] option.
11211
*/
11212
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_snapshot_recover(sqlite3 *db, const char *zDb);
11213
11214
/*
11215
** CAPI3REF: Serialize a database
11216
**
11217
** The sqlite3_serialize(D,S,P,F) interface returns a pointer to
11218
** memory that is a serialization of the S database on
11219
** [database connection] D.  If S is a NULL pointer, the main database is used.
11220
** If P is not a NULL pointer, then the size of the database in bytes
11221
** is written into *P.
11222
**
11223
** For an ordinary on-disk database file, the serialization is just a
11224
** copy of the disk file.  For an in-memory database or a "TEMP" database,
11225
** the serialization is the same sequence of bytes which would be written
11226
** to disk if that database were backed up to disk.
11227
**
11228
** The usual case is that sqlite3_serialize() copies the serialization of
11229
** the database into memory obtained from [sqlite3_malloc64()] and returns
11230
** a pointer to that memory.  The caller is responsible for freeing the
11231
** returned value to avoid a memory leak.  However, if the F argument
11232
** contains the SQLITE_SERIALIZE_NOCOPY bit, then no memory allocations
11233
** are made, and the sqlite3_serialize() function will return a pointer
11234
** to the contiguous memory representation of the database that SQLite
11235
** is currently using for that database, or NULL if no such contiguous
11236
** memory representation of the database exists.  A contiguous memory
11237
** representation of the database will usually only exist if there has
11238
** been a prior call to [sqlite3_deserialize(D,S,...)] with the same
11239
** values of D and S.
11240
** The size of the database is written into *P even if the
11241
** SQLITE_SERIALIZE_NOCOPY bit is set but no contiguous copy
11242
** of the database exists.
11243
**
11244
** After the call, if the SQLITE_SERIALIZE_NOCOPY bit had been set,
11245
** the returned buffer content will remain accessible and unchanged
11246
** until either the next write operation on the connection or when
11247
** the connection is closed, and applications must not modify the
11248
** buffer. If the bit had been clear, the returned buffer will not
11249
** be accessed by SQLite after the call.
11250
**
11251
** A call to sqlite3_serialize(D,S,P,F) might return NULL even if the
11252
** SQLITE_SERIALIZE_NOCOPY bit is omitted from argument F if a memory
11253
** allocation error occurs.
11254
**
11255
** This interface is omitted if SQLite is compiled with the
11256
** [SQLITE_OMIT_DESERIALIZE] option.
11257
*/
11258
SQLITE_API unsigned char *sqlite3_serialize(
11259
  sqlite3 *db,           /* The database connection */
11260
  const char *zSchema,   /* Which DB to serialize. ex: "main", "temp", ... */
11261
  sqlite3_int64 *piSize, /* Write size of the DB here, if not NULL */
11262
  unsigned int mFlags    /* Zero or more SQLITE_SERIALIZE_* flags */
11263
);
11264
11265
/*
11266
** CAPI3REF: Flags for sqlite3_serialize
11267
**
11268
** Zero or more of the following constants can be OR-ed together for
11269
** the F argument to [sqlite3_serialize(D,S,P,F)].
11270
**
11271
** SQLITE_SERIALIZE_NOCOPY means that [sqlite3_serialize()] will return
11272
** a pointer to contiguous in-memory database that it is currently using,
11273
** without making a copy of the database.  If SQLite is not currently using
11274
** a contiguous in-memory database, then this option causes
11275
** [sqlite3_serialize()] to return a NULL pointer.  SQLite will only be
11276
** using a contiguous in-memory database if it has been initialized by a
11277
** prior call to [sqlite3_deserialize()].
11278
*/
11279
#define SQLITE_SERIALIZE_NOCOPY 0x001   /* Do no memory allocations */
11280
11281
/*
11282
** CAPI3REF: Deserialize a database
11283
**
11284
** The sqlite3_deserialize(D,S,P,N,M,F) interface causes the
11285
** [database connection] D to disconnect from database S and then
11286
** reopen S as an in-memory database based on the serialization
11287
** contained in P.  If S is a NULL pointer, the main database is
11288
** used. The serialized database P is N bytes in size.  M is the size
11289
** of the buffer P, which might be larger than N.  If M is larger than
11290
** N, and the SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_READONLY bit is not set in F, then
11291
** SQLite is permitted to add content to the in-memory database, in
11292
** page-sized chunks, as long as the total size does not exceed M bytes.
11293
**
11294
** The parameter M must be greater than or equal to N.  Ideally, M
11295
** should have a value which is N+(512&times;K)+20 where K determines how
11296
** must extra space is available to hold new content as the database
11297
** grows.  K can be 0 if the database is read-only.
11298
**
11299
** If the database content in P is malformed in a malicious way then
11300
** it is possible that SQLite might try to read a few more than N bytes
11301
** from P.  If the veracity of the database content P is uncertain,
11302
** then applications are advised to allocate about 20 extra bytes on
11303
** the end of the P buffer to avoid a memory error.
11304
**
11305
** If the SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_FREEONCLOSE bit is set in F, then SQLite will
11306
** invoke sqlite3_free() on the serialization buffer when the database
11307
** connection closes.  If the SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_RESIZEABLE bit is set, then
11308
** SQLite will try to increase the buffer size using sqlite3_realloc64()
11309
** if writes on the database cause it to grow larger than M bytes.
11310
**
11311
** Applications must not modify the buffer P or invalidate it before
11312
** the database connection D is closed.
11313
**
11314
** The sqlite3_deserialize() interface will fail with SQLITE_BUSY if the
11315
** database is currently in a read transaction or is involved in a backup
11316
** operation.
11317
**
11318
** It is not possible to deserialize into the TEMP database.  If the
11319
** S argument to sqlite3_deserialize(D,S,P,N,M,F) is "temp" then the
11320
** function returns SQLITE_ERROR.
11321
**
11322
** The deserialized database should not be in [WAL mode].  If the database
11323
** is in WAL mode, then any attempt to use the database file will result
11324
** in an [SQLITE_CANTOPEN] error.  The application can set the
11325
** [file format version numbers] (bytes 18 and 19) of the input database P
11326
** to 0x01 prior to invoking sqlite3_deserialize(D,S,P,N,M,F) to force the
11327
** database file into rollback mode and work around this limitation.
11328
**
11329
** If sqlite3_deserialize(D,S,P,N,M,F) fails for any reason and if the
11330
** SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_FREEONCLOSE bit is set in argument F, then
11331
** [sqlite3_free()] is invoked on argument P prior to returning.
11332
**
11333
** This interface is omitted if SQLite is compiled with the
11334
** [SQLITE_OMIT_DESERIALIZE] option.
11335
*/
11336
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_deserialize(
11337
  sqlite3 *db,            /* The database connection */
11338
  const char *zSchema,    /* Which DB to reopen with the deserialization */
11339
  unsigned char *pData,   /* The serialized database content */
11340
  sqlite3_int64 szDb,     /* Number of bytes in the deserialization */
11341
  sqlite3_int64 szBuf,    /* Total size of buffer pData[] */
11342
  unsigned mFlags         /* Zero or more SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_* flags */
11343
);
11344
11345
/*
11346
** CAPI3REF: Flags for sqlite3_deserialize()
11347
**
11348
** The following are allowed values for the 6th argument (the F argument) to
11349
** the [sqlite3_deserialize(D,S,P,N,M,F)] interface.
11350
**
11351
** The SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_FREEONCLOSE means that the database serialization
11352
** in the P argument is held in memory obtained from [sqlite3_malloc64()]
11353
** and that SQLite should take ownership of this memory and automatically
11354
** free it when it has finished using it.  Without this flag, the caller
11355
** is responsible for freeing any dynamically allocated memory.
11356
**
11357
** The SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_RESIZEABLE flag means that SQLite is allowed to
11358
** grow the size of the database using calls to [sqlite3_realloc64()].  This
11359
** flag should only be used if SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_FREEONCLOSE is also used.
11360
** Without this flag, the deserialized database cannot increase in size beyond
11361
** the number of bytes specified by the M parameter.
11362
**
11363
** The SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_READONLY flag means that the deserialized database
11364
** should be treated as read-only.
11365
*/
11366
#define SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_FREEONCLOSE 1 /* Call sqlite3_free() on close */
11367
#define SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_RESIZEABLE  2 /* Resize using sqlite3_realloc64() */
11368
#define SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_READONLY    4 /* Database is read-only */
11369
11370
/*
11371
** CAPI3REF: Bind array values to the CARRAY table-valued function
11372
**
11373
** The sqlite3_carray_bind_v2(S,I,P,N,F,X,D) interface binds an array value to
11374
** parameter that is the first argument of the [carray() table-valued function].
11375
** The S parameter is a pointer to the [prepared statement] that uses the
11376
** carray() functions.  I is the parameter index to be bound.  I must be the
11377
** index of the parameter that is the first argument to the carray()
11378
** table-valued function. P is a pointer to the array to be bound, and N
11379
** is the number of elements in the array.  The F argument is one of
11380
** constants [SQLITE_CARRAY_INT32], [SQLITE_CARRAY_INT64],
11381
** [SQLITE_CARRAY_DOUBLE], [SQLITE_CARRAY_TEXT],
11382
** or [SQLITE_CARRAY_BLOB] to indicate the datatype of the array P.
11383
**
11384
** If the X argument is not a NULL pointer or one of the special
11385
** values [SQLITE_STATIC] or [SQLITE_TRANSIENT], then SQLite will invoke
11386
** the function X with argument D when it is finished using the data in P.
11387
** The call to X(D) is a destructor for the array P. The destructor X(D)
11388
** is invoked even if the call to sqlite3_carray_bind_v2() fails. If the X
11389
** parameter is the special-case value [SQLITE_STATIC], then SQLite assumes
11390
** that the data static and the destructor is never invoked.  If the X
11391
** parameter is the special-case value [SQLITE_TRANSIENT], then
11392
** sqlite3_carray_bind_v2() makes its own private copy of the data prior
11393
** to returning and never invokes the destructor X.
11394
**
11395
** The sqlite3_carray_bind() function works the same as sqlite3_carray_bind_v2()
11396
** with a D parameter set to P.  In other words,
11397
** sqlite3_carray_bind(S,I,P,N,F,X) is same as
11398
** sqlite3_carray_bind_v2(S,I,P,N,F,X,P).
11399
*/
11400
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_carray_bind_v2(
11401
  sqlite3_stmt *pStmt,        /* Statement to be bound */
11402
  int i,                      /* Parameter index */
11403
  void *aData,                /* Pointer to array data */
11404
  int nData,                  /* Number of data elements */
11405
  int mFlags,                 /* CARRAY flags */
11406
  void (*xDel)(void*),        /* Destructor for aData */
11407
  void *pDel                  /* Optional argument to xDel() */
11408
);
11409
SQLITE_API int sqlite3_carray_bind(
11410
  sqlite3_stmt *pStmt,        /* Statement to be bound */
11411
  int i,                      /* Parameter index */
11412
  void *aData,                /* Pointer to array data */
11413
  int nData,                  /* Number of data elements */
11414
  int mFlags,                 /* CARRAY flags */
11415
  void (*xDel)(void*)         /* Destructor for aData */
11416
);
11417
11418

#define SQLITE_CARRAY_INT64     1    /* Data is 64-bit signed integers */

11430

11438
#define CARRAY_TEXT      3    /* Data is char* */
11439
#define CARRAY_BLOB      4    /* Data is struct iovec */

11640

11641

11642
** to the database when the session object is created.
