11715
** Enable or disable the recording of changes by a session object. When
11716
** enabled, a session object records changes made to the database. When
11717
** disabled - it does not. A newly created session object is enabled.
11718
** Refer to the documentation for [sqlite3session_changeset()] for further
11719
** details regarding how enabling and disabling a session object affects
11720
** the eventual changesets.
11721
**
11722
** Passing zero to this function disables the session. Passing a value
11723
** greater than zero enables it. Passing a value less than zero is a
11724
** no-op, and may be used to query the current state of the session.
11725
**
11726
** The return value indicates the final state of the session object: 0 if
11727
** the session is disabled, or 1 if it is enabled.
11728
*/
11729
SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_enable(sqlite3_session *pSession, int bEnable);
11730
11731
/*
11732
** CAPI3REF: Set Or Clear the Indirect Change Flag
11733
** METHOD: sqlite3_session
11734
**
11735
** Each change recorded by a session object is marked as either direct or
11736
** indirect. A change is marked as indirect if either:
11737
**
11738
** <ul>
11739
**   <li> The session object "indirect" flag is set when the change is
11740
**        made, or
11741
**   <li> The change is made by an SQL trigger or foreign key action
11742
**        instead of directly as a result of a users SQL statement.
11743
** </ul>
11744
**
11745
** If a single row is affected by more than one operation within a session,
11746
** then the change is considered indirect if all operations meet the criteria
11747
** for an indirect change above, or direct otherwise.
11748
**
11749
** This function is used to set, clear or query the session object indirect
11750
** flag.  If the second argument passed to this function is zero, then the
11751
** indirect flag is cleared. If it is greater than zero, the indirect flag
11752
** is set. Passing a value less than zero does not modify the current value
11753
** of the indirect flag, and may be used to query the current state of the
11754
** indirect flag for the specified session object.
11755
**
11756
** The return value indicates the final state of the indirect flag: 0 if
11757
** it is clear, or 1 if it is set.
11758
*/
11759
SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_indirect(sqlite3_session *pSession, int bIndirect);
11760
11761
/*
11762
** CAPI3REF: Attach A Table To A Session Object
11763
** METHOD: sqlite3_session
11764
**
11765
** If argument zTab is not NULL, then it is the name of a table to attach
11766
** to the session object passed as the first argument. All subsequent changes
11767
** made to the table while the session object is enabled will be recorded. See
11768
** documentation for [sqlite3session_changeset()] for further details.
11769
**
11770
** Or, if argument zTab is NULL, then changes are recorded for all tables
11771
** in the database. If additional tables are added to the database (by
11772
** executing "CREATE TABLE" statements) after this call is made, changes for
11773
** the new tables are also recorded.
11774
**
11775
** Changes can only be recorded for tables that have a PRIMARY KEY explicitly
11776
** defined as part of their CREATE TABLE statement. It does not matter if the
11777
** PRIMARY KEY is an "INTEGER PRIMARY KEY" (rowid alias) or not. The PRIMARY
11778
** KEY may consist of a single column, or may be a composite key.
11779
**
11780
** It is not an error if the named table does not exist in the database. Nor
11781
** is it an error if the named table does not have a PRIMARY KEY. However,
11782
** no changes will be recorded in either of these scenarios.
11783
**
11784
** Changes are not recorded for individual rows that have NULL values stored
11785
** in one or more of their PRIMARY KEY columns.
11786
**
11787
** SQLITE_OK is returned if the call completes without error. Or, if an error
11788
** occurs, an SQLite error code (e.g. SQLITE_NOMEM) is returned.
11789
**
11790
** <h3>Special sqlite_stat1 Handling</h3>
11791
**
11792
** As of SQLite version 3.22.0, the "sqlite_stat1" table is an exception to
11793
** some of the rules above. In SQLite, the schema of sqlite_stat1 is:
11794
**  <pre>
11795
**  &nbsp;     CREATE TABLE sqlite_stat1(tbl,idx,stat)
11796
**  </pre>
11797
**
11798
** Even though sqlite_stat1 does not have a PRIMARY KEY, changes are
11799
** recorded for it as if the PRIMARY KEY is (tbl,idx). Additionally, changes
11800
** are recorded for rows for which (idx IS NULL) is true. However, for such
11801
** rows a zero-length blob (SQL value X'') is stored in the changeset or
11802
** patchset instead of a NULL value. This allows such changesets to be
11803
** manipulated by legacy implementations of sqlite3changeset_invert(),
11804
** concat() and similar.
11805
**
11806
** The sqlite3changeset_apply() function automatically converts the
11807
** zero-length blob back to a NULL value when updating the sqlite_stat1
11808
** table. However, if the application calls sqlite3changeset_new(),
11809
** sqlite3changeset_old() or sqlite3changeset_conflict on a changeset
11810
** iterator directly (including on a changeset iterator passed to a
11811
** conflict-handler callback) then the X'' value is returned. The application
11812
** must translate X'' to NULL itself if required.
11813
**
11814
** Legacy (older than 3.22.0) versions of the sessions module cannot capture
11815
** changes made to the sqlite_stat1 table. Legacy versions of the
11816
** sqlite3changeset_apply() function silently ignore any modifications to the
11817
** sqlite_stat1 table that are part of a changeset or patchset.
11818
*/
11819
SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_attach(
11820
  sqlite3_session *pSession,      /* Session object */
11821
  const char *zTab                /* Table name */
11822
);
11823
11824
/*
11825
** CAPI3REF: Set a table filter on a Session Object.
11826
** METHOD: sqlite3_session
11827
**
11828
** The second argument (xFilter) is the "filter callback". For changes to rows
11829
** in tables that are not attached to the Session object, the filter is called
11830
** to determine whether changes to the table's rows should be tracked or not.
11831
** If xFilter returns 0, changes are not tracked. Note that once a table is
11832
** attached, xFilter will not be called again.
11833
*/
11834
SQLITE_API void sqlite3session_table_filter(
11835
  sqlite3_session *pSession,      /* Session object */
11836
  int(*xFilter)(
11837
    void *pCtx,                   /* Copy of third arg to _filter_table() */
11838
    const char *zTab              /* Table name */
11839
  ),
11840
  void *pCtx                      /* First argument passed to xFilter */
11841
);
11842
11843
/*
11844
** CAPI3REF: Generate A Changeset From A Session Object
11845
** METHOD: sqlite3_session
11846
**
11847
** Obtain a changeset containing changes to the tables attached to the
11848
** session object passed as the first argument. If successful,
11849
** set *ppChangeset to point to a buffer containing the changeset
11850
** and *pnChangeset to the size of the changeset in bytes before returning
11851
** SQLITE_OK. If an error occurs, set both *ppChangeset and *pnChangeset to
11852
** zero and return an SQLite error code.
11853
**
11854
** A changeset consists of zero or more INSERT, UPDATE and/or DELETE changes,
11855
** each representing a change to a single row of an attached table. An INSERT
11856
** change contains the values of each field of a new database row. A DELETE
11857
** contains the original values of each field of a deleted database row. An
11858
** UPDATE change contains the original values of each field of an updated
11859
** database row along with the updated values for each updated non-primary-key
11860
** column. It is not possible for an UPDATE change to represent a change that
11861
** modifies the values of primary key columns. If such a change is made, it
11862
** is represented in a changeset as a DELETE followed by an INSERT.
11863
**
11864
** Changes are not recorded for rows that have NULL values stored in one or
11865
** more of their PRIMARY KEY columns. If such a row is inserted or deleted,
11866
** no corresponding change is present in the changesets returned by this
11867
** function. If an existing row with one or more NULL values stored in
11868
** PRIMARY KEY columns is updated so that all PRIMARY KEY columns are non-NULL,
11869
** only an INSERT is appears in the changeset. Similarly, if an existing row
11870
** with non-NULL PRIMARY KEY values is updated so that one or more of its
11871
** PRIMARY KEY columns are set to NULL, the resulting changeset contains a
11872
** DELETE change only.
11873
**
11874
** The contents of a changeset may be traversed using an iterator created
11875
** using the [sqlite3changeset_start()] API. A changeset may be applied to
11876
** a database with a compatible schema using the [sqlite3changeset_apply()]
11877
** API.
11878
**
11879
** Within a changeset generated by this function, all changes related to a
11880
** single table are grouped together. In other words, when iterating through
11881
** a changeset or when applying a changeset to a database, all changes related
11882
** to a single table are processed before moving on to the next table. Tables
11883
** are sorted in the same order in which they were attached (or auto-attached)
11884
** to the sqlite3_session object. The order in which the changes related to
11885
** a single table are stored is undefined.
11886
**
11887
** Following a successful call to this function, it is the responsibility of
11888
** the caller to eventually free the buffer that *ppChangeset points to using
11889
** [sqlite3_free()].
11890
**
11891
** <h3>Changeset Generation</h3>
11892
**
11893
** Once a table has been attached to a session object, the session object
11894
** records the primary key values of all new rows inserted into the table.
11895
** It also records the original primary key and other column values of any
11896
** deleted or updated rows. For each unique primary key value, data is only
11897
** recorded once - the first time a row with said primary key is inserted,
11898
** updated or deleted in the lifetime of the session.
11899
**
11900
** There is one exception to the previous paragraph: when a row is inserted,
11901
** updated or deleted, if one or more of its primary key columns contain a
11902
** NULL value, no record of the change is made.
11903
**
11904
** The session object therefore accumulates two types of records - those
11905
** that consist of primary key values only (created when the user inserts
11906
** a new record) and those that consist of the primary key values and the
11907
** original values of other table columns (created when the users deletes
11908
** or updates a record).
11909
**
11910
** When this function is called, the requested changeset is created using
11911
** both the accumulated records and the current contents of the database
11912
** file. Specifically:
11913
**
11914
** <ul>
11915
**   <li> For each record generated by an insert, the database is queried
11916
**        for a row with a matching primary key. If one is found, an INSERT
11917
**        change is added to the changeset. If no such row is found, no change
11918
**        is added to the changeset.
11919
**
11920
**   <li> For each record generated by an update or delete, the database is
11921
**        queried for a row with a matching primary key. If such a row is
11922
**        found and one or more of the non-primary key fields have been
11923
**        modified from their original values, an UPDATE change is added to
11924
**        the changeset. Or, if no such row is found in the table, a DELETE
11925
**        change is added to the changeset. If there is a row with a matching
11926
**        primary key in the database, but all fields contain their original
11927
**        values, no change is added to the changeset.
11928
** </ul>
11929
**
11930
** This means, amongst other things, that if a row is inserted and then later
11931
** deleted while a session object is active, neither the insert nor the delete
11932
** will be present in the changeset. Or if a row is deleted and then later a
11933
** row with the same primary key values inserted while a session object is
11934
** active, the resulting changeset will contain an UPDATE change instead of
11935
** a DELETE and an INSERT.
11936
**
11937
** When a session object is disabled (see the [sqlite3session_enable()] API),
11938
** it does not accumulate records when rows are inserted, updated or deleted.
11939
** This may appear to have some counter-intuitive effects if a single row
11940
** is written to more than once during a session. For example, if a row
11941
** is inserted while a session object is enabled, then later deleted while
11942
** the same session object is disabled, no INSERT record will appear in the
11943
** changeset, even though the delete took place while the session was disabled.
11944
** Or, if one field of a row is updated while a session is enabled, and
11945
** then another field of the same row is updated while the session is disabled,
11946
** the resulting changeset will contain an UPDATE change that updates both
11947
** fields.
11948
*/
11949
SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_changeset(
11950
  sqlite3_session *pSession,      /* Session object */
11951
  int *pnChangeset,               /* OUT: Size of buffer at *ppChangeset */
11952
  void **ppChangeset              /* OUT: Buffer containing changeset */
11953
);
11954
11955
/*
11956
** CAPI3REF: Return An Upper-limit For The Size Of The Changeset
11957
** METHOD: sqlite3_session
11958
**
11959
** By default, this function always returns 0. For it to return
11960
** a useful result, the sqlite3_session object must have been configured
11961
** to enable this API using sqlite3session_object_config() with the
11962
** SQLITE_SESSION_OBJCONFIG_SIZE verb.
11963
**
11964
** When enabled, this function returns an upper limit, in bytes, for the size
11965
** of the changeset that might be produced if sqlite3session_changeset() were
11966
** called. The final changeset size might be equal to or smaller than the
11967
** size in bytes returned by this function.
11968
*/
11969
SQLITE_API sqlite3_int64 sqlite3session_changeset_size(sqlite3_session *pSession);
11970
11971
/*
11972
** CAPI3REF: Load The Difference Between Tables Into A Session
11973
** METHOD: sqlite3_session
11974
**
11975
** If it is not already attached to the session object passed as the first
11976
** argument, this function attaches table zTbl in the same manner as the
11977
** [sqlite3session_attach()] function. If zTbl does not exist, or if it
11978
** does not have a primary key, this function is a no-op (but does not return
11979
** an error).
11980
**
11981
** Argument zFromDb must be the name of a database ("main", "temp" etc.)
11982
** attached to the same database handle as the session object that contains
11983
** a table compatible with the table attached to the session by this function.
11984
** A table is considered compatible if it:
11985
**
11986
** <ul>
11987
**   <li> Has the same name,
11988
**   <li> Has the same set of columns declared in the same order, and
11989
**   <li> Has the same PRIMARY KEY definition.
11990
** </ul>
11991
**
11992
** If the tables are not compatible, SQLITE_SCHEMA is returned. If the tables
11993
** are compatible but do not have any PRIMARY KEY columns, it is not an error
11994
** but no changes are added to the session object. As with other session
11995
** APIs, tables without PRIMARY KEYs are simply ignored.
11996
**
11997
** This function adds a set of changes to the session object that could be
11998
** used to update the table in database zFrom (call this the "from-table")
11999
** so that its content is the same as the table attached to the session
12000
** object (call this the "to-table"). Specifically:
12001
**
12002
** <ul>
12003
**   <li> For each row (primary key) that exists in the to-table but not in
12004
**     the from-table, an INSERT record is added to the session object.
12005
**
12006
**   <li> For each row (primary key) that exists in the to-table but not in
12007
**     the from-table, a DELETE record is added to the session object.
12008
**
12009
**   <li> For each row (primary key) that exists in both tables, but features
12010
**     different non-PK values in each, an UPDATE record is added to the
12011
**     session.
12012
** </ul>
12013
**
12014
** To clarify, if this function is called and then a changeset constructed
12015
** using [sqlite3session_changeset()], then after applying that changeset to
12016
** database zFrom the contents of the two compatible tables would be
12017
** identical.
12018
**
12019
** Unless the call to this function is a no-op as described above, it is an
12020
** error if database zFrom does not exist or does not contain the required
12021
** compatible table.
12022
**
12023
** If the operation is successful, SQLITE_OK is returned. Otherwise, an SQLite
12024
** error code. In this case, if argument pzErrMsg is not NULL, *pzErrMsg
12025
** may be set to point to a buffer containing an English language error
12026
** message. It is the responsibility of the caller to free this buffer using
12027
** sqlite3_free().
12028
*/
12029
SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_diff(
12030
  sqlite3_session *pSession,
12031
  const char *zFromDb,
12032
  const char *zTbl,
12033
  char **pzErrMsg
12034
);
12035
12036
12037
/*
12038
** CAPI3REF: Generate A Patchset From A Session Object
12039
** METHOD: sqlite3_session
12040
**
12041
** The differences between a patchset and a changeset are that:
12042
**
12043
** <ul>
12044
**   <li> DELETE records consist of the primary key fields only. The
12045
**        original values of other fields are omitted.
12046
**   <li> The original values of any modified fields are omitted from
12047
**        UPDATE records.
12048
** </ul>
12049
**
12050
** A patchset blob may be used with up to date versions of all
12051
** sqlite3changeset_xxx API functions except for sqlite3changeset_invert(),
12052
** which returns SQLITE_CORRUPT if it is passed a patchset. Similarly,
12053
** attempting to use a patchset blob with old versions of the
12054
** sqlite3changeset_xxx APIs also provokes an SQLITE_CORRUPT error.
12055
**
12056
** Because the non-primary key "old.*" fields are omitted, no
12057
** SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA conflicts can be detected or reported if a patchset
12058
** is passed to the sqlite3changeset_apply() API. Other conflict types work
12059
** in the same way as for changesets.
12060
**
12061
** Changes within a patchset are ordered in the same way as for changesets
12062
** generated by the sqlite3session_changeset() function (i.e. all changes for
12063
** a single table are grouped together, tables appear in the order in which
12064
** they were attached to the session object).
12065
*/
12066
SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_patchset(
12067
  sqlite3_session *pSession,      /* Session object */
12068
  int *pnPatchset,                /* OUT: Size of buffer at *ppPatchset */
12069
  void **ppPatchset               /* OUT: Buffer containing patchset */
12070
);
12071
12072
/*
12073
** CAPI3REF: Test if a changeset has recorded any changes.
12074
**
12075
** Return non-zero if no changes to attached tables have been recorded by
12076
** the session object passed as the first argument. Otherwise, if one or
12077
** more changes have been recorded, return zero.
12078
**
12079
** Even if this function returns zero, it is possible that calling
12080
** [sqlite3session_changeset()] on the session handle may still return a
12081
** changeset that contains no changes. This can happen when a row in
12082
** an attached table is modified and then later on the original values
12083
** are restored. However, if this function returns non-zero, then it is
12084
** guaranteed that a call to sqlite3session_changeset() will return a
12085
** changeset containing zero changes.
12086
*/
12087
SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_isempty(sqlite3_session *pSession);

12089
/*
12090
** CAPI3REF: Query for the amount of heap memory used by a session object.
12091
**
12092
** This API returns the total amount of heap memory in bytes currently
12093
** used by the session object passed as the only argument.
12094
*/
12095
SQLITE_API sqlite3_int64 sqlite3session_memory_used(sqlite3_session *pSession);
12096
12097
/*
12098
** CAPI3REF: Create An Iterator To Traverse A Changeset
12099
** CONSTRUCTOR: sqlite3_changeset_iter
12100
**
12101
** Create an iterator used to iterate through the contents of a changeset.
12102
** If successful, *pp is set to point to the iterator handle and SQLITE_OK
12103
** is returned. Otherwise, if an error occurs, *pp is set to zero and an
12104
** SQLite error code is returned.
12105
**
12106
** The following functions can be used to advance and query a changeset
12107
** iterator created by this function:
12108
**
12109
** <ul>
12110
**   <li> [sqlite3changeset_next()]
12111
**   <li> [sqlite3changeset_op()]
12112
**   <li> [sqlite3changeset_new()]
12113
**   <li> [sqlite3changeset_old()]
12114
** </ul>
12115
**
12116
** It is the responsibility of the caller to eventually destroy the iterator
12117
** by passing it to [sqlite3changeset_finalize()]. The buffer containing the
12118
** changeset (pChangeset) must remain valid until after the iterator is
12119
** destroyed.
12120
**
12121
** Assuming the changeset blob was created by one of the
12122
** [sqlite3session_changeset()], [sqlite3changeset_concat()] or
12123
** [sqlite3changeset_invert()] functions, all changes within the changeset
12124
** that apply to a single table are grouped together. This means that when
12125
** an application iterates through a changeset using an iterator created by
12126
** this function, all changes that relate to a single table are visited
12127
** consecutively. There is no chance that the iterator will visit a change
12128
** the applies to table X, then one for table Y, and then later on visit
12129
** another change for table X.
12130
**
12131
** The behavior of sqlite3changeset_start_v2() and its streaming equivalent
12132
** may be modified by passing a combination of
12133
** [SQLITE_CHANGESETSTART_INVERT | supported flags] as the 4th parameter.
12134
**
12135
** Note that the sqlite3changeset_start_v2() API is still <b>experimental</b>
12136
** and therefore subject to change.
12137
*/
12138
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_start(
12139
  sqlite3_changeset_iter **pp,    /* OUT: New changeset iterator handle */
12140
  int nChangeset,                 /* Size of changeset blob in bytes */
12141
  void *pChangeset                /* Pointer to blob containing changeset */
12142
);
12143
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_start_v2(
12144
  sqlite3_changeset_iter **pp,    /* OUT: New changeset iterator handle */
12145
  int nChangeset,                 /* Size of changeset blob in bytes */
12146
  void *pChangeset,               /* Pointer to blob containing changeset */
12147
  int flags                       /* SESSION_CHANGESETSTART_* flags */
12148
);
12149
12150
/*
12151
** CAPI3REF: Flags for sqlite3changeset_start_v2
12152
**
12153
** The following flags may passed via the 4th parameter to
12154
** [sqlite3changeset_start_v2] and [sqlite3changeset_start_v2_strm]:
12155
**
12156
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESETSTART_INVERT <dd>
12157
**   Invert the changeset while iterating through it. This is equivalent to
12158
**   inverting a changeset using sqlite3changeset_invert() before applying it.
12159
**   It is an error to specify this flag with a patchset.
12160
*/
12161
#define SQLITE_CHANGESETSTART_INVERT        0x0002
12162
12163
12164
/*
12165
** CAPI3REF: Advance A Changeset Iterator
12166
** METHOD: sqlite3_changeset_iter
12167
**
12168
** This function may only be used with iterators created by the function
12169
** [sqlite3changeset_start()]. If it is called on an iterator passed to
12170
** a conflict-handler callback by [sqlite3changeset_apply()], SQLITE_MISUSE
12171
** is returned and the call has no effect.
12172
**
12173
** Immediately after an iterator is created by sqlite3changeset_start(), it
12174
** does not point to any change in the changeset. Assuming the changeset
12175
** is not empty, the first call to this function advances the iterator to
12176
** point to the first change in the changeset. Each subsequent call advances
12177
** the iterator to point to the next change in the changeset (if any). If
12178
** no error occurs and the iterator points to a valid change after a call
12179
** to sqlite3changeset_next() has advanced it, SQLITE_ROW is returned.
12180
** Otherwise, if all changes in the changeset have already been visited,
12181
** SQLITE_DONE is returned.
12182
**
12183
** If an error occurs, an SQLite error code is returned. Possible error
12184
** codes include SQLITE_CORRUPT (if the changeset buffer is corrupt) or
12185
** SQLITE_NOMEM.
12186
*/
12187
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_next(sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter);
12188
12189
/*
12190
** CAPI3REF: Obtain The Current Operation From A Changeset Iterator
12191
** METHOD: sqlite3_changeset_iter
12192
**
12193
** The pIter argument passed to this function may either be an iterator
12194
** passed to a conflict-handler by [sqlite3changeset_apply()], or an iterator
12195
** created by [sqlite3changeset_start()]. In the latter case, the most recent
12196
** call to [sqlite3changeset_next()] must have returned [SQLITE_ROW]. If this
12197
** is not the case, this function returns [SQLITE_MISUSE].
12198
**
12199
** Arguments pOp, pnCol and pzTab may not be NULL. Upon return, three
12200
** outputs are set through these pointers:
12201
**
12202
** *pOp is set to one of [SQLITE_INSERT], [SQLITE_DELETE] or [SQLITE_UPDATE],
12203
** depending on the type of change that the iterator currently points to;
12204
**
12205
** *pnCol is set to the number of columns in the table affected by the change; and
12206
**
12207
** *pzTab is set to point to a nul-terminated utf-8 encoded string containing
12208
** the name of the table affected by the current change. The buffer remains
12209
** valid until either sqlite3changeset_next() is called on the iterator
12210
** or until the conflict-handler function returns.
12211
**
12212
** If pbIndirect is not NULL, then *pbIndirect is set to true (1) if the change
12213
** is an indirect change, or false (0) otherwise. See the documentation for
12214
** [sqlite3session_indirect()] for a description of direct and indirect
12215
** changes.
12216
**
12217
** If no error occurs, SQLITE_OK is returned. If an error does occur, an
12218
** SQLite error code is returned. The values of the output variables may not
12219
** be trusted in this case.
12220
*/
12221
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_op(
12222
  sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter,  /* Iterator object */
12223
  const char **pzTab,             /* OUT: Pointer to table name */
12224
  int *pnCol,                     /* OUT: Number of columns in table */
12225
  int *pOp,                       /* OUT: SQLITE_INSERT, DELETE or UPDATE */
12226
  int *pbIndirect                 /* OUT: True for an 'indirect' change */
12227
);
12228
12229
/*
12230
** CAPI3REF: Obtain The Primary Key Definition Of A Table
12231
** METHOD: sqlite3_changeset_iter
12232
**
12233
** For each modified table, a changeset includes the following:
12234
**
12235
** <ul>
12236
**   <li> The number of columns in the table, and
12237
**   <li> Which of those columns make up the tables PRIMARY KEY.
12238
** </ul>
12239
**
12240
** This function is used to find which columns comprise the PRIMARY KEY of
12241
** the table modified by the change that iterator pIter currently points to.
12242
** If successful, *pabPK is set to point to an array of nCol entries, where
12243
** nCol is the number of columns in the table. Elements of *pabPK are set to
12244
** 0x01 if the corresponding column is part of the tables primary key, or
12245
** 0x00 if it is not.
12246
**
12247
** If argument pnCol is not NULL, then *pnCol is set to the number of columns
12248
** in the table.
12249
**
12250
** If this function is called when the iterator does not point to a valid
12251
** entry, SQLITE_MISUSE is returned and the output variables zeroed. Otherwise,
12252
** SQLITE_OK is returned and the output variables populated as described
12253
** above.
12254
*/
12255
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_pk(
12256
  sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter,  /* Iterator object */
12257
  unsigned char **pabPK,          /* OUT: Array of boolean - true for PK cols */
12258
  int *pnCol                      /* OUT: Number of entries in output array */
12259
);

/*
12262
** CAPI3REF: Obtain old.* Values From A Changeset Iterator
12263
** METHOD: sqlite3_changeset_iter
12264
**
12265
** The pIter argument passed to this function may either be an iterator
12266
** passed to a conflict-handler by [sqlite3changeset_apply()], or an iterator
12267
** created by [sqlite3changeset_start()]. In the latter case, the most recent
12268
** call to [sqlite3changeset_next()] must have returned SQLITE_ROW.
12269
** Furthermore, it may only be called if the type of change that the iterator
12270
** currently points to is either [SQLITE_DELETE] or [SQLITE_UPDATE]. Otherwise,
12271
** this function returns [SQLITE_MISUSE] and sets *ppValue to NULL.
12272
**
12273
** Argument iVal must be greater than or equal to 0, and less than the number
12274
** of columns in the table affected by the current change. Otherwise,
12275
** [SQLITE_RANGE] is returned and *ppValue is set to NULL.
12276
**
12277
** If successful, this function sets *ppValue to point to a protected
12278
** sqlite3_value object containing the iVal'th value from the vector of
12279
** original row values stored as part of the UPDATE or DELETE change and
12280
** returns SQLITE_OK. The name of the function comes from the fact that this
12281
** is similar to the "old.*" columns available to update or delete triggers.
12282
**
12283
** If some other error occurs (e.g. an OOM condition), an SQLite error code
12284
** is returned and *ppValue is set to NULL.
12285
*/
12286
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_old(
12287
  sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter,  /* Changeset iterator */
12288
  int iVal,                       /* Column number */
12289
  sqlite3_value **ppValue         /* OUT: Old value (or NULL pointer) */
12290
);

/*
12293
** CAPI3REF: Obtain new.* Values From A Changeset Iterator
12294
** METHOD: sqlite3_changeset_iter
12295
**
12296
** The pIter argument passed to this function may either be an iterator
12297
** passed to a conflict-handler by [sqlite3changeset_apply()], or an iterator
12298
** created by [sqlite3changeset_start()]. In the latter case, the most recent
12299
** call to [sqlite3changeset_next()] must have returned SQLITE_ROW.
12300
** Furthermore, it may only be called if the type of change that the iterator
12301
** currently points to is either [SQLITE_UPDATE] or [SQLITE_INSERT]. Otherwise,
12302
** this function returns [SQLITE_MISUSE] and sets *ppValue to NULL.
12303
**
12304
** Argument iVal must be greater than or equal to 0, and less than the number
12305
** of columns in the table affected by the current change. Otherwise,
12306
** [SQLITE_RANGE] is returned and *ppValue is set to NULL.
12307
**
12308
** If successful, this function sets *ppValue to point to a protected
12309
** sqlite3_value object containing the iVal'th value from the vector of
12310
** new row values stored as part of the UPDATE or INSERT change and
12311
** returns SQLITE_OK. If the change is an UPDATE and does not include
12312
** a new value for the requested column, *ppValue is set to NULL and
12313
** SQLITE_OK returned. The name of the function comes from the fact that
12314
** this is similar to the "new.*" columns available to update or delete
12315
** triggers.
12316
**
12317
** If some other error occurs (e.g. an OOM condition), an SQLite error code
12318
** is returned and *ppValue is set to NULL.
12319
*/
12320
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_new(
12321
  sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter,  /* Changeset iterator */
12322
  int iVal,                       /* Column number */
12323
  sqlite3_value **ppValue         /* OUT: New value (or NULL pointer) */
12324
);

**
12330
** This function should only be used with iterator objects passed to a
12331
** conflict-handler callback by [sqlite3changeset_apply()] with either
12332
** [SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA] or [SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONFLICT]. If this function
12333
** is called on any other iterator, [SQLITE_MISUSE] is returned and *ppValue
12334
** is set to NULL.
12335
**
12336
** Argument iVal must be greater than or equal to 0, and less than the number
12337
** of columns in the table affected by the current change. Otherwise,
12338
** [SQLITE_RANGE] is returned and *ppValue is set to NULL.
12339
**
12340
** If successful, this function sets *ppValue to point to a protected
12341
** sqlite3_value object containing the iVal'th value from the
12342
** "conflicting row" associated with the current conflict-handler callback
12343
** and returns SQLITE_OK.
12344
**
12345
** If some other error occurs (e.g. an OOM condition), an SQLite error code
12346
** is returned and *ppValue is set to NULL.
12347
*/

SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_conflict(
12349
  sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter,  /* Changeset iterator */

12352

/*

** CAPI3REF: Determine The Number Of Foreign Key Constraint Violations
12356
** METHOD: sqlite3_changeset_iter
12357
**
12358
** This function may only be called with an iterator passed to an
12359
** SQLITE_CHANGESET_FOREIGN_KEY conflict handler callback. In this case
12360
** it sets the output variable to the total number of known foreign key
12361
** violations in the destination database and returns SQLITE_OK.
12362
**
12363
** In all other cases this function returns SQLITE_MISUSE.
12364
*/
12365
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_fk_conflicts(

  sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter,  /* Changeset iterator */

/*
12372
** CAPI3REF: Finalize A Changeset Iterator
12373
** METHOD: sqlite3_changeset_iter
12374
**
12375
** This function is used to finalize an iterator allocated with
12376
** [sqlite3changeset_start()].
12377
**
12378
** This function should only be called on iterators created using the
12379
** [sqlite3changeset_start()] function. If an application calls this
12380
** function with an iterator passed to a conflict-handler by
12381
** [sqlite3changeset_apply()], [SQLITE_MISUSE] is immediately returned and the
12382
** call has no effect.
12383
**
12384
** If an error was encountered within a call to an sqlite3changeset_xxx()
12385
** function (for example an [SQLITE_CORRUPT] in [sqlite3changeset_next()] or an
12386
** [SQLITE_NOMEM] in [sqlite3changeset_new()]) then an error code corresponding
12387
** to that error is returned by this function. Otherwise, SQLITE_OK is
12388
** returned. This is to allow the following pattern (pseudo-code):
12389
**
12390
** <pre>
12391
**   sqlite3changeset_start();
12392
**   while( SQLITE_ROW==sqlite3changeset_next() ){
12393
**     // Do something with change.
12394
**   }
12395
**   rc = sqlite3changeset_finalize();
12396
**   if( rc!=SQLITE_OK ){
12397
**     // An error has occurred
12398
**   }
12399
** </pre>
12400
*/
12401
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_finalize(sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter);

/*
12404
** CAPI3REF: Invert A Changeset
12405
**
12406
** This function is used to "invert" a changeset object. Applying an inverted
12407
** changeset to a database reverses the effects of applying the uninverted
12408
** changeset. Specifically:
12409
**
12410
** <ul>
12411
**   <li> Each DELETE change is changed to an INSERT, and
12412
**   <li> Each INSERT change is changed to a DELETE, and
12413
**   <li> For each UPDATE change, the old.* and new.* values are exchanged.
12414
** </ul>
12415
**
12416
** This function does not change the order in which changes appear within
12417
** the changeset. It merely reverses the sense of each individual change.
12418
**
12419
** If successful, a pointer to a buffer containing the inverted changeset
12420
** is stored in *ppOut, the size of the same buffer is stored in *pnOut, and
12421
** SQLITE_OK is returned. If an error occurs, both *pnOut and *ppOut are
12422
** zeroed and an SQLite error code returned.
12423
**
12424
** It is the responsibility of the caller to eventually call sqlite3_free()
12425
** on the *ppOut pointer to free the buffer allocation following a successful
12426
** call to this function.
12427
**
12428
** WARNING/TODO: This function currently assumes that the input is a valid
12429
** changeset. If it is not, the results are undefined.
12430
*/
12431
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_invert(
12432
  int nIn, const void *pIn,       /* Input changeset */
12433
  int *pnOut, void **ppOut        /* OUT: Inverse of input */
12434
);
12435
12436
/*
12437
** CAPI3REF: Concatenate Two Changeset Objects
12438
**
12439
** This function is used to concatenate two changesets, A and B, into a
12440
** single changeset. The result is a changeset equivalent to applying
12441
** changeset A followed by changeset B.
12442
**
12443
** This function combines the two input changesets using an
12444
** sqlite3_changegroup object. Calling it produces similar results as the
12445
** following code fragment:
12446
**
12447
** <pre>
12448
**   sqlite3_changegroup *pGrp;
12449
**   rc = sqlite3_changegroup_new(&pGrp);
12450
**   if( rc==SQLITE_OK ) rc = sqlite3changegroup_add(pGrp, nA, pA);
12451
**   if( rc==SQLITE_OK ) rc = sqlite3changegroup_add(pGrp, nB, pB);
12452
**   if( rc==SQLITE_OK ){
12453
**     rc = sqlite3changegroup_output(pGrp, pnOut, ppOut);
12454
**   }else{
12455
**     *ppOut = 0;
12456
**     *pnOut = 0;
12457
**   }
12458
** </pre>
12459
**
12460
** Refer to the sqlite3_changegroup documentation below for details.
12461
*/
12462
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_concat(
12463
  int nA,                         /* Number of bytes in buffer pA */
12464
  void *pA,                       /* Pointer to buffer containing changeset A */
12465
  int nB,                         /* Number of bytes in buffer pB */
12466
  void *pB,                       /* Pointer to buffer containing changeset B */
12467
  int *pnOut,                     /* OUT: Number of bytes in output changeset */
12468
  void **ppOut                    /* OUT: Buffer containing output changeset */
12469
);
12470
12471
/*
12472
** CAPI3REF: Changegroup Handle
12473
**
12474
** A changegroup is an object used to combine two or more
12475
** [changesets] or [patchsets]
12476
*/
12477
typedef struct sqlite3_changegroup sqlite3_changegroup;
12478
12479
/*
12480
** CAPI3REF: Create A New Changegroup Object
12481
** CONSTRUCTOR: sqlite3_changegroup
12482
**
12483
** An sqlite3_changegroup object is used to combine two or more changesets
12484
** (or patchsets) into a single changeset (or patchset). A single changegroup
12485
** object may combine changesets or patchsets, but not both. The output is
12486
** always in the same format as the input.
12487
**
12488
** If successful, this function returns SQLITE_OK and populates (*pp) with
12489
** a pointer to a new sqlite3_changegroup object before returning. The caller
12490
** should eventually free the returned object using a call to
12491
** sqlite3changegroup_delete(). If an error occurs, an SQLite error code
12492
** (i.e. SQLITE_NOMEM) is returned and *pp is set to NULL.
12493
**
12494
** The usual usage pattern for an sqlite3_changegroup object is as follows:
12495
**
12496
** <ul>
12497
**   <li> It is created using a call to sqlite3changegroup_new().
12498
**
12499
**   <li> Zero or more changesets (or patchsets) are added to the object
12500
**        by calling sqlite3changegroup_add().
12501
**
12502
**   <li> The result of combining all input changesets together is obtained
12503
**        by the application via a call to sqlite3changegroup_output().
12504
**
12505
**   <li> The object is deleted using a call to sqlite3changegroup_delete().
12506
** </ul>
12507
**
12508
** Any number of calls to add() and output() may be made between the calls to
12509
** new() and delete(), and in any order.
12510
**
12511
** As well as the regular sqlite3changegroup_add() and
12512
** sqlite3changegroup_output() functions, also available are the streaming
12513
** versions sqlite3changegroup_add_strm() and sqlite3changegroup_output_strm().
12514
*/
12515
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changegroup_new(sqlite3_changegroup **pp);
12516
12517
/*
12518
** CAPI3REF: Add a Schema to a Changegroup
12519
** METHOD: sqlite3_changegroup_schema
12520
**
12521
** This method may be used to optionally enforce the rule that the changesets
12522
** added to the changegroup handle must match the schema of database zDb
12523
** ("main", "temp", or the name of an attached database). If
12524
** sqlite3changegroup_add() is called to add a changeset that is not compatible
12525
** with the configured schema, SQLITE_SCHEMA is returned and the changegroup
12526
** object is left in an undefined state.
12527
**
12528
** A changeset schema is considered compatible with the database schema in
12529
** the same way as for sqlite3changeset_apply(). Specifically, for each
12530
** table in the changeset, there exists a database table with:
12531
**
12532
** <ul>
12533
**   <li> The name identified by the changeset, and
12534
**   <li> at least as many columns as recorded in the changeset, and
12535
**   <li> the primary key columns in the same position as recorded in
12536
**        the changeset.
12537
** </ul>
12538
**
12539
** The output of the changegroup object always has the same schema as the
12540
** database nominated using this function. In cases where changesets passed
12541
** to sqlite3changegroup_add() have fewer columns than the corresponding table
12542
** in the database schema, these are filled in using the default column
12543
** values from the database schema. This makes it possible to combined
12544
** changesets that have different numbers of columns for a single table
12545
** within a changegroup, provided that they are otherwise compatible.
12546
*/
12547
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changegroup_schema(sqlite3_changegroup*, sqlite3*, const char *zDb);
12548
12549
/*
12550
** CAPI3REF: Add A Changeset To A Changegroup
12551
** METHOD: sqlite3_changegroup
12552
**
12553
** Add all changes within the changeset (or patchset) in buffer pData (size
12554
** nData bytes) to the changegroup.
12555
**
12556
** If the buffer contains a patchset, then all prior calls to this function
12557
** on the same changegroup object must also have specified patchsets. Or, if
12558
** the buffer contains a changeset, so must have the earlier calls to this
12559
** function. Otherwise, SQLITE_ERROR is returned and no changes are added
12560
** to the changegroup.
12561
**
12562
** Rows within the changeset and changegroup are identified by the values in
12563
** their PRIMARY KEY columns. A change in the changeset is considered to
12564
** apply to the same row as a change already present in the changegroup if
12565
** the two rows have the same primary key.
12566
**
12567
** Changes to rows that do not already appear in the changegroup are
12568
** simply copied into it. Or, if both the new changeset and the changegroup
12569
** contain changes that apply to a single row, the final contents of the
12570
** changegroup depends on the type of each change, as follows:
12571
**
12572
** <table border=1 style="margin-left:8ex;margin-right:8ex">
12573
**   <tr><th style="white-space:pre">Existing Change  </th>
12574
**       <th style="white-space:pre">New Change       </th>
12575
**       <th>Output Change
12576
**   <tr><td>INSERT <td>INSERT <td>
12577
**       The new change is ignored. This case does not occur if the new
12578
**       changeset was recorded immediately after the changesets already
12579
**       added to the changegroup.
12580
**   <tr><td>INSERT <td>UPDATE <td>
12581
**       The INSERT change remains in the changegroup. The values in the
12582
**       INSERT change are modified as if the row was inserted by the
12583
**       existing change and then updated according to the new change.
12584
**   <tr><td>INSERT <td>DELETE <td>
12585
**       The existing INSERT is removed from the changegroup. The DELETE is
12586
**       not added.
12587
**   <tr><td>UPDATE <td>INSERT <td>
12588
**       The new change is ignored. This case does not occur if the new
12589
**       changeset was recorded immediately after the changesets already
12590
**       added to the changegroup.
12591
**   <tr><td>UPDATE <td>UPDATE <td>
12592
**       The existing UPDATE remains within the changegroup. It is amended
12593
**       so that the accompanying values are as if the row was updated once
12594
**       by the existing change and then again by the new change.
12595
**   <tr><td>UPDATE <td>DELETE <td>
12596
**       The existing UPDATE is replaced by the new DELETE within the
12597
**       changegroup.
12598
**   <tr><td>DELETE <td>INSERT <td>
12599
**       If one or more of the column values in the row inserted by the
12600
**       new change differ from those in the row deleted by the existing
12601
**       change, the existing DELETE is replaced by an UPDATE within the
12602
**       changegroup. Otherwise, if the inserted row is exactly the same
12603
**       as the deleted row, the existing DELETE is simply discarded.
12604
**   <tr><td>DELETE <td>UPDATE <td>
12605
**       The new change is ignored. This case does not occur if the new
12606
**       changeset was recorded immediately after the changesets already
12607
**       added to the changegroup.
12608
**   <tr><td>DELETE <td>DELETE <td>
12609
**       The new change is ignored. This case does not occur if the new
12610
**       changeset was recorded immediately after the changesets already
12611
**       added to the changegroup.
12612
** </table>
12613
**
12614
** If the new changeset contains changes to a table that is already present
12615
** in the changegroup, then the number of columns and the position of the
12616
** primary key columns for the table must be consistent. If this is not the
12617
** case, this function fails with SQLITE_SCHEMA. Except, if the changegroup
12618
** object has been configured with a database schema using the
12619
** sqlite3changegroup_schema() API, then it is possible to combine changesets
12620
** with different numbers of columns for a single table, provided that
12621
** they are otherwise compatible.
12622
**
12623
** If the input changeset appears to be corrupt and the corruption is
12624
** detected, SQLITE_CORRUPT is returned. Or, if an out-of-memory condition
12625
** occurs during processing, this function returns SQLITE_NOMEM.
12626
**
12627
** In all cases, if an error occurs the state of the final contents of the
12628
** changegroup is undefined. If no error occurs, SQLITE_OK is returned.
12629
*/
12630
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changegroup_add(sqlite3_changegroup*, int nData, void *pData);
12631
12632
/*
12633
** CAPI3REF: Add A Single Change To A Changegroup
12634
** METHOD: sqlite3_changegroup
12635
**
12636
** This function adds the single change currently indicated by the iterator
12637
** passed as the second argument to the changegroup object. The rules for
12638
** adding the change are just as described for [sqlite3changegroup_add()].
12639
**
12640
** If the change is successfully added to the changegroup, SQLITE_OK is
12641
** returned. Otherwise, an SQLite error code is returned.
12642
**
12643
** The iterator must point to a valid entry when this function is called.
12644
** If it does not, SQLITE_ERROR is returned and no change is added to the
12645
** changegroup. Additionally, the iterator must not have been opened with
12646
** the SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_INVERT flag. In this case SQLITE_ERROR is also
12647
** returned.
12648
*/
12649
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changegroup_add_change(
12650
  sqlite3_changegroup*,
12651
  sqlite3_changeset_iter*
12652
);
12653
12654
12655
12656
/*
12657
** CAPI3REF: Obtain A Composite Changeset From A Changegroup
12658
** METHOD: sqlite3_changegroup
12659
**
12660
** Obtain a buffer containing a changeset (or patchset) representing the
12661
** current contents of the changegroup. If the inputs to the changegroup
12662
** were themselves changesets, the output is a changeset. Or, if the
12663
** inputs were patchsets, the output is also a patchset.
12664
**
12665
** As with the output of the sqlite3session_changeset() and
12666
** sqlite3session_patchset() functions, all changes related to a single
12667
** table are grouped together in the output of this function. Tables appear
12668
** in the same order as for the very first changeset added to the changegroup.
12669
** If the second or subsequent changesets added to the changegroup contain
12670
** changes for tables that do not appear in the first changeset, they are
12671
** appended onto the end of the output changeset, again in the order in
12672
** which they are first encountered.
12673
**
12674
** If an error occurs, an SQLite error code is returned and the output
12675
** variables (*pnData) and (*ppData) are set to 0. Otherwise, SQLITE_OK
12676
** is returned and the output variables are set to the size of and a
12677
** pointer to the output buffer, respectively. In this case it is the
12678
** responsibility of the caller to eventually free the buffer using a
12679
** call to sqlite3_free().
12680
*/
12681
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changegroup_output(
12682
  sqlite3_changegroup*,
12683
  int *pnData,                    /* OUT: Size of output buffer in bytes */
12684
  void **ppData                   /* OUT: Pointer to output buffer */
12685
);
12686
12687
/*
12688
** CAPI3REF: Delete A Changegroup Object
12689
** DESTRUCTOR: sqlite3_changegroup
12690
*/
12691
SQLITE_API void sqlite3changegroup_delete(sqlite3_changegroup*);
12692
12693
/*
12694
** CAPI3REF: Apply A Changeset To A Database
12695
**
12696
** Apply a changeset or patchset to a database. These functions attempt to
12697
** update the "main" database attached to handle db with the changes found in
12698
** the changeset passed via the second and third arguments.
12699
**
12700
** All changes made by these functions are enclosed in a savepoint transaction.
12701
** If any other error (aside from a constraint failure when attempting to
12702
** write to the target database) occurs, then the savepoint transaction is
12703
** rolled back, restoring the target database to its original state, and an
12704
** SQLite error code returned. Additionally, starting with version 3.51.0,
12705
** an error code and error message that may be accessed using the
12706
** [sqlite3_errcode()] and [sqlite3_errmsg()] APIs are left in the database
12707
** handle.
12708
**
12709
** The fourth argument (xFilter) passed to these functions is the "filter
12710
** callback". This may be passed NULL, in which case all changes in the
12711
** changeset are applied to the database. For sqlite3changeset_apply() and
12712
** sqlite3_changeset_apply_v2(), if it is not NULL, then it is invoked once
12713
** for each table affected by at least one change in the changeset. In this
12714
** case the table name is passed as the second argument, and a copy of
12715
** the context pointer passed as the sixth argument to apply() or apply_v2()
12716
** as the first. If the "filter callback" returns zero, then no attempt is
12717
** made to apply any changes to the table. Otherwise, if the return value is
12718
** non-zero, all changes related to the table are attempted.
12719
**
12720
** For sqlite3_changeset_apply_v3(), the xFilter callback is invoked once
12721
** per change. The second argument in this case is an sqlite3_changeset_iter
12722
** that may be queried using the usual APIs for the details of the current
12723
** change. If the "filter callback" returns zero in this case, then no attempt
12724
** is made to apply the current change. If it returns non-zero, the change
12725
** is applied.
12726
**
12727
** For each table that is not excluded by the filter callback, this function
12728
** tests that the target database contains a compatible table. A table is
12729
** considered compatible if all of the following are true:
12730
**
12731
** <ul>
12732
**   <li> The table has the same name as the name recorded in the
12733
**        changeset, and
12734
**   <li> The table has at least as many columns as recorded in the
12735
**        changeset, and
12736
**   <li> The table has primary key columns in the same position as
12737
**        recorded in the changeset.
12738
** </ul>
12739
**
12740
** If there is no compatible table, it is not an error, but none of the
12741
** changes associated with the table are applied. A warning message is issued
12742
** via the sqlite3_log() mechanism with the error code SQLITE_SCHEMA. At most
12743
** one such warning is issued for each table in the changeset.
12744
**
12745
** For each change for which there is a compatible table, an attempt is made
12746
** to modify the table contents according to each UPDATE, INSERT or DELETE
12747
** change that is not excluded by a filter callback. If a change cannot be
12748
** applied cleanly, the conflict handler function passed as the fifth argument
12749
** to sqlite3changeset_apply() may be invoked. A description of exactly when
12750
** the conflict handler is invoked for each type of change is below.
12751
**
12752
** Unlike the xFilter argument, xConflict may not be passed NULL. The results
12753
** of passing anything other than a valid function pointer as the xConflict
12754
** argument are undefined.
12755
**
12756
** Each time the conflict handler function is invoked, it must return one
12757
** of [SQLITE_CHANGESET_OMIT], [SQLITE_CHANGESET_ABORT] or
12758
** [SQLITE_CHANGESET_REPLACE]. SQLITE_CHANGESET_REPLACE may only be returned
12759
** if the second argument passed to the conflict handler is either
12760
** SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA or SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONFLICT. If the conflict-handler
12761
** returns an illegal value, any changes already made are rolled back and
12762
** the call to sqlite3changeset_apply() returns SQLITE_MISUSE. Different
12763
** actions are taken by sqlite3changeset_apply() depending on the value
12764
** returned by each invocation of the conflict-handler function. Refer to
12765
** the documentation for the three
12766
** [SQLITE_CHANGESET_OMIT|available return values] for details.
12767
**
12768
** <dl>
12769
** <dt>DELETE Changes<dd>
12770
**   For each DELETE change, the function checks if the target database
12771
**   contains a row with the same primary key value (or values) as the
12772
**   original row values stored in the changeset. If it does, and the values
12773
**   stored in all non-primary key columns also match the values stored in
12774
**   the changeset the row is deleted from the target database.
12775
**
12776
**   If a row with matching primary key values is found, but one or more of
12777
**   the non-primary key fields contains a value different from the original
12778
**   row value stored in the changeset, the conflict-handler function is
12779
**   invoked with [SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA] as the second argument. If the
12780
**   database table has more columns than are recorded in the changeset,
12781
**   only the values of those non-primary key fields are compared against
12782
**   the current database contents - any trailing database table columns
12783
**   are ignored.
12784
**
12785
**   If no row with matching primary key values is found in the database,
12786
**   the conflict-handler function is invoked with [SQLITE_CHANGESET_NOTFOUND]
12787
**   passed as the second argument.
12788
**
12789
**   If the DELETE operation is attempted, but SQLite returns SQLITE_CONSTRAINT
12790
**   (which can only happen if a foreign key constraint is violated), the
12791
**   conflict-handler function is invoked with [SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONSTRAINT]
12792
**   passed as the second argument. This includes the case where the DELETE
12793
**   operation is attempted because an earlier call to the conflict handler
12794
**   function returned [SQLITE_CHANGESET_REPLACE].
12795
**
12796
** <dt>INSERT Changes<dd>
12797
**   For each INSERT change, an attempt is made to insert the new row into
12798
**   the database. If the changeset row contains fewer fields than the
12799
**   database table, the trailing fields are populated with their default
12800
**   values.
12801
**
12802
**   If the attempt to insert the row fails because the database already
12803
**   contains a row with the same primary key values, the conflict handler
12804
**   function is invoked with the second argument set to
12805
**   [SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONFLICT].
12806
**
12807
**   If the attempt to insert the row fails because of some other constraint
12808
**   violation (e.g. NOT NULL or UNIQUE), the conflict handler function is
12809
**   invoked with the second argument set to [SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONSTRAINT].
12810
**   This includes the case where the INSERT operation is re-attempted because
12811
**   an earlier call to the conflict handler function returned
12812
**   [SQLITE_CHANGESET_REPLACE].
12813
**
12814
** <dt>UPDATE Changes<dd>
12815
**   For each UPDATE change, the function checks if the target database
12816
**   contains a row with the same primary key value (or values) as the
12817
**   original row values stored in the changeset. If it does, and the values
12818
**   stored in all modified non-primary key columns also match the values
12819
**   stored in the changeset the row is updated within the target database.
12820
**
12821
**   If a row with matching primary key values is found, but one or more of
12822
**   the modified non-primary key fields contains a value different from an
12823
**   original row value stored in the changeset, the conflict-handler function
12824
**   is invoked with [SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA] as the second argument. Since
12825
**   UPDATE changes only contain values for non-primary key fields that are
12826
**   to be modified, only those fields need to match the original values to
12827
**   avoid the SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA conflict-handler callback.
12828
**
12829
**   If no row with matching primary key values is found in the database,
12830
**   the conflict-handler function is invoked with [SQLITE_CHANGESET_NOTFOUND]
12831
**   passed as the second argument.
12832
**
12833
**   If the UPDATE operation is attempted, but SQLite returns
12834
**   SQLITE_CONSTRAINT, the conflict-handler function is invoked with
12835
**   [SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONSTRAINT] passed as the second argument.
12836
**   This includes the case where the UPDATE operation is attempted after
12837
**   an earlier call to the conflict handler function returned
12838
**   [SQLITE_CHANGESET_REPLACE].
12839
** </dl>
12840
**
12841
** It is safe to execute SQL statements, including those that write to the
12842
** table that the callback related to, from within the xConflict callback.
12843
** This can be used to further customize the application's conflict
12844
** resolution strategy.
12845
**
12846
** If the output parameters (ppRebase) and (pnRebase) are non-NULL and
12847
** the input is a changeset (not a patchset), then sqlite3changeset_apply_v2()
12848
** may set (*ppRebase) to point to a "rebase" that may be used with the
12849
** sqlite3_rebaser APIs buffer before returning. In this case (*pnRebase)
12850
** is set to the size of the buffer in bytes. It is the responsibility of the
12851
** caller to eventually free any such buffer using sqlite3_free(). The buffer
12852
** is only allocated and populated if one or more conflicts were encountered
12853
** while applying the patchset. See comments surrounding the sqlite3_rebaser
12854
** APIs for further details.
12855
**
12856
** The behavior of sqlite3changeset_apply_v2() and its streaming equivalent
12857
** may be modified by passing a combination of
12858
** [SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_NOSAVEPOINT | supported flags] as the 9th parameter.
12859
**
12860
** Note that the sqlite3changeset_apply_v2() API is still <b>experimental</b>
12861
** and therefore subject to change.
12862
*/
12863
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_apply(
12864
  sqlite3 *db,                    /* Apply change to "main" db of this handle */
12865
  int nChangeset,                 /* Size of changeset in bytes */
12866
  void *pChangeset,               /* Changeset blob */
12867
  int(*xFilter)(
12868
    void *pCtx,                   /* Copy of sixth arg to _apply() */
12869
    const char *zTab              /* Table name */
12870
  ),
12871
  int(*xConflict)(
12872
    void *pCtx,                   /* Copy of sixth arg to _apply() */
12873
    int eConflict,                /* DATA, MISSING, CONFLICT, CONSTRAINT */
12874
    sqlite3_changeset_iter *p     /* Handle describing change and conflict */
12875
  ),
12876
  void *pCtx                      /* First argument passed to xConflict */
12877
);
12878
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_apply_v2(
12879
  sqlite3 *db,                    /* Apply change to "main" db of this handle */
12880
  int nChangeset,                 /* Size of changeset in bytes */
12881
  void *pChangeset,               /* Changeset blob */
12882
  int(*xFilter)(
12883
    void *pCtx,                   /* Copy of sixth arg to _apply() */
12884
    const char *zTab              /* Table name */
12885
  ),
12886
  int(*xConflict)(
12887
    void *pCtx,                   /* Copy of sixth arg to _apply() */
12888
    int eConflict,                /* DATA, MISSING, CONFLICT, CONSTRAINT */
12889
    sqlite3_changeset_iter *p     /* Handle describing change and conflict */
12890
  ),
12891
  void *pCtx,                     /* First argument passed to xConflict */
12892
  void **ppRebase, int *pnRebase, /* OUT: Rebase data */
12893
  int flags                       /* SESSION_CHANGESETAPPLY_* flags */
12894
);
12895
SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_apply_v3(
12896
  sqlite3 *db,                    /* Apply change to "main" db of this handle */
12897
  int nChangeset,                 /* Size of changeset in bytes */
12898
  void *pChangeset,               /* Changeset blob */
12899
  int(*xFilter)(
12900
    void *pCtx,                   /* Copy of sixth arg to _apply() */
12901
    sqlite3_changeset_iter *p     /* Handle describing change */
12902
  ),
12903
  int(*xConflict)(
12904
    void *pCtx,                   /* Copy of sixth arg to _apply() */
12905
    int eConflict,                /* DATA, MISSING, CONFLICT, CONSTRAINT */
12906
    sqlite3_changeset_iter *p     /* Handle describing change and conflict */
12907
  ),
12908
  void *pCtx,                     /* First argument passed to xConflict */
12909
  void **ppRebase, int *pnRebase, /* OUT: Rebase data */
12910
  int flags                       /* SESSION_CHANGESETAPPLY_* flags */
12911

12913
/*
12914
** CAPI3REF: Flags for sqlite3changeset_apply_v2
12915
**
12916
** The following flags may passed via the 9th parameter to
12917
** [sqlite3changeset_apply_v2] and [sqlite3changeset_apply_v2_strm]:
12918
**
12919
** <dl>
12920
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_NOSAVEPOINT <dd>
12921
**   Usually, the sessions module encloses all operations performed by
12922
**   a single call to apply_v2() or apply_v2_strm() in a [SAVEPOINT]. The
12923
**   SAVEPOINT is committed if the changeset or patchset is successfully
12924
**   applied, or rolled back if an error occurs. Specifying this flag
12925
**   causes the sessions module to omit this savepoint. In this case, if the
12926
**   caller has an open transaction or savepoint when apply_v2() is called,
12927
**   it may revert the partially applied changeset by rolling it back.
12928
**
12929
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_INVERT <dd>
12930
**   Invert the changeset before applying it. This is equivalent to inverting
12931
**   a changeset using sqlite3changeset_invert() before applying it. It is
12932
**   an error to specify this flag with a patchset.
12933
**
12934
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_IGNORENOOP <dd>
12935
**   Do not invoke the conflict handler callback for any changes that
12936
**   would not actually modify the database even if they were applied.
12937
**   Specifically, this means that the conflict handler is not invoked
12938
**   for:
12939
**    <ul>
12940
**    <li>a delete change if the row being deleted cannot be found,
12941
**    <li>an update change if the modified fields are already set to
12942
**        their new values in the conflicting row, or
12943
**    <li>an insert change if all fields of the conflicting row match
12944
**        the row being inserted.
12945
**    </ul>
12946
**
12947
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_FKNOACTION <dd>
12948
**   If this flag it set, then all foreign key constraints in the target
12949
**   database behave as if they were declared with "ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON
12950
**   DELETE NO ACTION", even if they are actually CASCADE, RESTRICT, SET NULL
12951
**   or SET DEFAULT.
12952
**
12953
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_NOUPDATELOOP <dd>
12954
**   Sometimes, a changeset contains two or more update statements such that
12955
**   although after applying all updates the database will contain no
12956
**   constraint violations, no single update can be applied before the others.
12957
**   The simplest example of this is a pair of UPDATEs that have "swapped"
12958
**   two column values with a UNIQUE constraint.
12959
**   <p>
12960
**   Usually, sqlite3changeset_apply() and similar functions work hard to try
12961
**   to find a way to apply such a changeset. However, if this flag is set,
12962
**   then all such updates are considered CONSTRAINT conflicts.
12963
*/
12964
#define SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_NOSAVEPOINT   0x0001
12965
#define SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_INVERT        0x0002
12966
#define SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_IGNORENOOP    0x0004
12967
#define SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_FKNOACTION    0x0008
12968
#define SQLITE_CHANGESETAPPLY_NOUPDATELOOP  0x0010
12969
12970
/*
12971
** CAPI3REF: Constants Passed To The Conflict Handler
12972
**
12973
** Values that may be passed as the second argument to a conflict-handler.
12974
**
12975
** <dl>
12976
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA<dd>
12977
**   The conflict handler is invoked with CHANGESET_DATA as the second argument
12978
**   when processing a DELETE or UPDATE change if a row with the required
12979
**   PRIMARY KEY fields is present in the database, but one or more other
12980
**   (non primary-key) fields modified by the update do not contain the
12981
**   expected "before" values.
12982
**
12983
**   The conflicting row, in this case, is the database row with the matching
12984
**   primary key.
12985
**
12986
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESET_NOTFOUND<dd>
12987
**   The conflict handler is invoked with CHANGESET_NOTFOUND as the second
12988
**   argument when processing a DELETE or UPDATE change if a row with the
12989
**   required PRIMARY KEY fields is not present in the database.
12990
**
12991
**   There is no conflicting row in this case. The results of invoking the
12992
**   sqlite3changeset_conflict() API are undefined.
12993
**
12994
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONFLICT<dd>
12995
**   CHANGESET_CONFLICT is passed as the second argument to the conflict
12996
**   handler while processing an INSERT change if the operation would result
12997
**   in duplicate primary key values.
12998
**
12999
**   The conflicting row in this case is the database row with the matching
13000
**   primary key.
13001
**
13002
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESET_FOREIGN_KEY<dd>
13003
**   If foreign key handling is enabled, and applying a changeset leaves the
13004
**   database in a state containing foreign key violations, the conflict
13005
**   handler is invoked with CHANGESET_FOREIGN_KEY as the second argument
13006
**   exactly once before the changeset is committed. If the conflict handler
13007
**   returns CHANGESET_OMIT, the changes, including those that caused the
13008
**   foreign key constraint violation, are committed. Or, if it returns
13009
**   CHANGESET_ABORT, the changeset is rolled back.
13010
**
13011
**   No current or conflicting row information is provided. The only function
13012
**   it is possible to call on the supplied sqlite3_changeset_iter handle
13013
**   is sqlite3changeset_fk_conflicts().
13014
**
13015
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONSTRAINT<dd>
13016
**   If any other constraint violation occurs while applying a change (i.e.
13017
**   a UNIQUE, CHECK or NOT NULL constraint), the conflict handler is
13018
**   invoked with CHANGESET_CONSTRAINT as the second argument.
13019
**
13020
**   There is no conflicting row in this case. The results of invoking the
13021
**   sqlite3changeset_conflict() API are undefined.
13022
**
13023
** </dl>
13024
*/
13025
#define SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA        1
13026
#define SQLITE_CHANGESET_NOTFOUND    2
13027
#define SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONFLICT    3
13028
#define SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONSTRAINT  4
13029
#define SQLITE_CHANGESET_FOREIGN_KEY 5
13030
13031
/*
13032
** CAPI3REF: Constants Returned By The Conflict Handler
13033
**
13034
** A conflict handler callback must return one of the following three values.
13035
**
13036
** <dl>
13037
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESET_OMIT<dd>
13038
**   If a conflict handler returns this value no special action is taken. The
13039
**   change that caused the conflict is not applied. The session module
13040
**   continues to the next change in the changeset.
13041
**
13042
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESET_REPLACE<dd>
13043
**   This value may only be returned if the second argument to the conflict
13044
**   handler was SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA or SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONFLICT. If this
13045
**   is not the case, any changes applied so far are rolled back and the
13046
**   call to sqlite3changeset_apply() returns SQLITE_MISUSE.
13047
**
13048
**   If CHANGESET_REPLACE is returned by an SQLITE_CHANGESET_DATA conflict
13049
**   handler, then the conflicting row is either updated or deleted, depending
13050
**   on the type of change.
13051
**
13052
**   If CHANGESET_REPLACE is returned by an SQLITE_CHANGESET_CONFLICT conflict
13053
**   handler, then the conflicting row is removed from the database and a
13054
**   second attempt to apply the change is made. If this second attempt fails,
13055
**   the original row is restored to the database before continuing.
13056
**
13057
** <dt>SQLITE_CHANGESET_ABORT<dd>
13058
**   If this value is returned, any changes applied so far are rolled back
13059
**   and the call to sqlite3changeset_apply() returns SQLITE_ABORT.
13060
** </dl>
13061
*/
13062
#define SQLITE_CHANGESET_OMIT       0
13063
#define SQLITE_CHANGESET_REPLACE    1
13064
#define SQLITE_CHANGESET_ABORT      2
13065
13066
/*
13067
** CAPI3REF: Rebasing changesets
13068
** EXPERIMENTAL
13069
**
13070
** Suppose there is a site hosting a database in state S0. And that
13071
** modifications are made that move that database to state S1 and a
13072
** changeset recorded (the "local" changeset). Then, a changeset based
13073
** on S0 is received from another site (the "remote" changeset) and
13074
** applied to the database. The database is then in state
13075
** (S1+"remote"), where the exact state depends on any conflict
13076
** resolution decisions (OMIT or REPLACE) made while applying "remote".
13077
** Rebasing a changeset is to update it to take those conflict
13078
** resolution decisions into account, so that the same conflicts
13079
** do not have to be resolved elsewhere in the network.
13080
**
13081
** For example, if both the local and remote changesets contain an
13082
** INSERT of the same key on "CREATE TABLE t1(a PRIMARY KEY, b)":
13083
**
13084
**   local:  INSERT INTO t1 VALUES(1, 'v1');
13085
**   remote: INSERT INTO t1 VALUES(1, 'v2');
13086
**
13087
** and the conflict resolution is REPLACE, then the INSERT change is
13088
** removed from the local changeset (it was overridden). Or, if the
13089
** conflict resolution was "OMIT", then the local changeset is modified
13090
** to instead contain:
13091
**
13092
**           UPDATE t1 SET b = 'v2' WHERE a=1;
13093
**
13094
** Changes within the local changeset are rebased as follows:
13095
**
13096
** <dl>
13097
** <dt>Local INSERT<dd>
13098
**   This may only conflict with a remote INSERT. If the conflict
13099
**   resolution was OMIT, then add an UPDATE change to the rebased
13100
**   changeset. Or, if the conflict resolution was REPLACE, add
13101
**   nothing to the rebased changeset.
13102
**
13103
** <dt>Local DELETE<dd>
13104
**   This may conflict with a remote UPDATE or DELETE. In both cases the
13105
**   only possible resolution is OMIT. If the remote operation was a
13106
**   DELETE, then add no change to the rebased changeset. If the remote
13107
**   operation was an UPDATE, then the old.* fields of change are updated
13108
**   to reflect the new.* values in the UPDATE.
13109
**
13110
** <dt>Local UPDATE<dd>
13111
**   This may conflict with a remote UPDATE or DELETE. If it conflicts
13112
**   with a DELETE, and the conflict resolution was OMIT, then the update
13113
**   is changed into an INSERT. Any undefined values in the new.* record
13114
**   from the update change are filled in using the old.* values from
13115
**   the conflicting DELETE. Or, if the conflict resolution was REPLACE,
13116
**   the UPDATE change is simply omitted from the rebased changeset.
13117
**
13118
**   If conflict is with a remote UPDATE and the resolution is OMIT, then
13119
**   the old.* values are rebased using the new.* values in the remote
13120
**   change. Or, if the resolution is REPLACE, then the change is copied
13121
**   into the rebased changeset with updates to columns also updated by
13122
**   the conflicting remote UPDATE removed. If this means no columns would
13123
**   be updated, the change is omitted.
13124
** </dl>
13125
**
13126
** A local change may be rebased against multiple remote changes
13127
** simultaneously. If a single key is modified by multiple remote
13128
** changesets, they are combined as follows before the local changeset
13129
** is rebased:
13130
**
13131
** <ul>
13132
**    <li> If there has been one or more REPLACE resolutions on a
13133
**         key, it is rebased according to a REPLACE.
13134
**
13135
**    <li> If there have been no REPLACE resolutions on a key, then
13136
**         the local changeset is rebased according to the most recent
13137
**         of the OMIT resolutions.
13138
** </ul>
13139
**
13140
** Note that conflict resolutions from multiple remote changesets are
13141
** combined on a per-field basis, not per-row. This means that in the
13142
** case of multiple remote UPDATE operations, some fields of a single
13143
** local change may be rebased for REPLACE while others are rebased for
13144
** OMIT.
13145
**
13146
** In order to rebase a local changeset, the remote changeset must first
13147
** be applied to the local database using sqlite3changeset_apply_v2() and
13148
** the buffer of rebase information captured. Then:
13149
**
13150
** <ol>
13151
**   <li> An sqlite3_rebaser object is created by calling
13152
**        sqlite3rebaser_create().
13153
**   <li> The new object is configured with the rebase buffer obtained from
13154
**        sqlite3changeset_apply_v2() by calling sqlite3rebaser_configure().
13155
**        If the local changeset is to be rebased against multiple remote
13156
**        changesets, then sqlite3rebaser_configure() should be called
13157
**        multiple times, in the same order that the multiple
13158
**        sqlite3changeset_apply_v2() calls were made.
13159
**   <li> Each local changeset is rebased by calling sqlite3rebaser_rebase().
13160
**   <li> The sqlite3_rebaser object is deleted by calling
13161
**        sqlite3rebaser_delete().
13162
** </ol>
13163
*/
13164
typedef struct sqlite3_rebaser sqlite3_rebaser;
13165
13166
/*
13167
** CAPI3REF: Create a changeset rebaser object.
13168
** EXPERIMENTAL
13169
**
13170
** Allocate a new changeset rebaser object. If successful, set (*ppNew) to
13171
** point to the new object and return SQLITE_OK. Otherwise, if an error
13172
** occurs, return an SQLite error code (e.g. SQLITE_NOMEM) and set (*ppNew)
13173
** to NULL.
13174
*/

SQLITE_API int sqlite3rebaser_create(sqlite3_rebaser **ppNew);

13184

SQLITE_API int sqlite3rebaser_configure(

13198
